summary: Exodus II is Sandia's netCDF-based FE mesh and results container, maintained in SEACAS. exodusII.h on master gives EX_API_VERS 9.06f (release 2025-08-25) and NEMESIS_FILE_VERSION 2.6. It is the de facto interchange format for Cubit, MOOSE/libMesh, Sierra, STK and ParaView. Polygons and polyhedra arrived in v4.93 as NSIDED/NFACED blocks that reference separate face blocks. The model is block-centric: flat per-block arrays, no stored adjacency, no geometry association. It is mature and ubiquitous, but the only spec is the C header plus Doxygen pages, and polyhedra are an add-on to a format built around single-topology blocks. Verified against cloned SEACAS and libMesh source; unverified items are marked.
data_model: Entities: nodes, edges, faces, elements; edge and face blocks exist but most files use only nodes and elements. A block holds entities of ONE topology string (HEX8, TET10, NSIDED, NFACED...), created by ex_put_block(exoid, blk_type, blk_id, topology, num_entries, num_nodes_per_entry, num_edges_per_entry, num_faces_per_entry, num_attr_per_entry). Ids are int64 (ex_entity_id). Entity enums: EX_ELEM_BLOCK=1, EX_EDGE_BLOCK=6, EX_FACE_BLOCK=8, EX_ASSEMBLY=16, EX_BLOB=17. Element ids are implicit and global (1..N in block order); optional maps (ex_put_map, ex_put_map_param) carry user numbering. Connectivity is one dense array per block (nodes_per_entry x num_entries). Node-to-element, element-to-element and face-to-element relations are NOT stored. Coordinates are split into coordx/coordy/coordz datasets; nodal variables are one dataset per variable (time, nodes). Sets (node, edge, face, side, elem) are lists; sidesets are (element id, local side number) pairs, so they depend on per-topology local face numbering. Newer API has ex_field (types incl. EX_BASIS, nesting) for field metadata; its semantics beyond the struct in exodusII.h are unverified.
polyhedra: From seacas/packages/seacas/libraries/exodus/include/polyhedra.md (v4.93 and later). A 3D polyhedron element block has type "NFACED". Its faces are defined in one or more face blocks; arbitrary polygon faces use type "NSIDED". Layout: (1) ex_put_init_ext with num_face and num_face_blk set. (2) Face block: ex_put_block(EX_FACE_BLOCK, id, "nsided", nfaces, total_nodes_in_block, 0,0,0); ex_put_conn(EX_FACE_BLOCK, id, node_conn,NULL,NULL) writes the concatenated node lists; ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra(EX_FACE_BLOCK, id, counts) writes nodes-per-face. (3) NFACED block: ex_put_block(EX_ELEM_BLOCK, id, "nfaced", nelem, 0 nodes, 0 edges, total_faces, 0); ex_put_conn(EX_ELEM_BLOCK, id, NULL, NULL, face_conn) writes concatenated face ids (global implicit face ids, shared faces appear in two elements, as in the doc's example where face 4 is shared); ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra(EX_ELEM_BLOCK, id, counts) writes faces-per-element. So it is CSR-like: a flat list plus a counts array rather than offsets. ex_get_block returns TOTAL node/face counts for these blocks, not per-entity. Note: the doc shows no face orientation or sign, so outward normals / winding relative to each cell is not stored (unverified beyond the doc). libMesh: exodusII_io_helper.C maps NSIDED to C0POLYGON and NFACED to C0POLYHEDRON (lines ~463-467, 588-589) and has both reader and writer (ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra at ~3712-3745). The reader errors unless the NFACED block's faces come from NSIDED face blocks without edge connectivity or face-in-face connectivity; NFACED blocks with edge connectivity are rejected. The writer splits a subdomain with mixed types (e.g. HEX8 plus C0POLYHEDRON) into several blocks because Exodus requires one type per block. A 2016 ParaView thread (public.kitware.com/pipermail/paraview/2016-April/036632.html, search snippet only, page returned 403) reports the reader wrongly assumed one face block per element block, and that face ids are file-implicit; treat as unverified detail.
nonconformal: Exodus has no native non-conformal concept. Non-conformal interfaces are expressed only as two sidesets (one per side) on the mismatched surfaces, with the pairing left to the application (contact/mortar/mesh-tying code detects and projects). Hanging nodes are not represented. Nothing in the spec marks two faces as imprinted or paired. I found no mechanism in the headers; not exhaustively searched for contact-pair conventions in Sierra (unverified).
sets_and_partitions: Blocks give the primary partition (one block per material/topology, typically one per CAD volume/material). Node sets, side sets, element sets, edge and face sets are lists of ids with optional distribution factors. Assemblies (EX_ASSEMBLY, ex_put_assembly with struct {id, name, type, entity_count, entity_list}; type is EX_ELEM_BLOCK or EX_ASSEMBLY) are named, hierarchical groupings of blocks or other assemblies, a lightweight material/region layer. Blobs (ex_blob {id, name, num_entry}) hold arbitrary non-mesh arrays. Entities carry names (ex_put_name), integer properties and attributes (ex_put_attr_param). Nemesis (file version 2.6) adds parallel info: per-processor internal/border/external nodes and elements, plus communication maps; the SEACAS doc nemesis-to-exodus-api-mapping.md shows it being folded into the Exodus API. Each rank writes its own file (name.N.rank); nem_slice and nem_spread decompose/distribute. Ghost/halo handling is limited to these maps (details unverified).
strengths: Ubiquitous: readable by ParaView, Cubit, MOOSE, Sierra, Trilinos/STK and most neutronics preprocessors, so exporting to it gives instant reach.
Explicit separation of topology (blocks) from grouping (sets, assemblies); assemblies give a hierarchical partition layer.
Block-per-topology gives dense, contiguous arrays and fast bulk I/O via netCDF-4/HDF5; works with MPI-IO style parallel.
Extensible metadata: names, attributes, properties, blobs, field descriptors.
64-bit integer mode removes the 2^31 limit (netCDF-4 non-classic, models of billions of entities reported in Exodus-Formats.md).
weaknesses: No stored adjacency; every consumer rebuilds node-to-element, face-to-element and neighbour graphs.
Implicit global ids (position in block order) make editing, merging and partition-local ids fragile.
Polyhedra are bolted on: face blocks must be NSIDED, element-face lists lack orientation, tool support is partial (libMesh rejects several variants).
One topology per block forces mixed-element subdomains to be split into many blocks.
No high-order geometry description beyond node-count-keyed element names (e.g. HEX27, TET10, tet up to 40 nodes in exodus-element-types.md); no node ordering spec beyond the table and docs.
No geometry (B-rep) association, no non-conformal/imprint semantics, no formal versioned schema beyond the header.

Classic and 64-bit-offset netCDF variants cap dataset size (about 2^29 nodes per coordinate component, 4 GiB per dataset; Exodus-Formats.md); classic netCDF-4 caps at 2^31 entities; 32-char default names (MAX_NAME_LENGTH 32) with longer allowed via netCDF.
lessons_for_us: Adopt its separation of topology blocks from grouping layers; model assemblies as a first-class hierarchical partition layer (our layer 2) rather than overloading blocks.

Deliberately differ: store adjacency explicitly (CSR of face-to-cell with left/right sides and orientation sign) so polyhedra and non-conformal logic do not depend on per-topology local-face numbering as Exodus sidesets do.
Make polyhedra the general case (faces with node CSR, cells with oriented face CSR) and treat HEX/TET as typed fast-path views, the opposite of Exodus where NFACED is an exception.
Use stable explicit ids with a separate position index, not implicit order, to survive repartitioning and edits.
Allow mixed topologies in one region via a per-cell type array, with 'blocks' as derived views.
Add an explicit non-conformal interface entity (paired face sets plus tolerance and mapping metadata), since Exodus leaves this to applications.

Carry geometry association (B-rep entity id plus dimension on every mesh entity) and a formal versioned schema; keep Exodus as an export target (blocks from regions, sidesets from boundary sets, assemblies from the partition tree) and expect to lose adjacency and orientation on export.
Keep counts-array/CSR layout for variable-size entities, but prefer offsets over counts for O(1) random access; use HDF5 chunked, 64-bit ids from day one.
database_like_aspects: Weak. It is a self-describing netCDF container with named dimensions/variables, which gives schema-like introspection, but no queries, no indexes and no stored relations. Entity-set lists act like tagged selections, and assemblies/blobs add some structure. Adjacency is not stored and must be computed on demand by clients.
high_order: Handled by element topology names keyed on node count (e.g. HEX8/20/27, TET4/10/11/14/15/16/40, QUAD up to 16 nodes, TRI up to 13; exodus-element-types.md). Nodes are the only high-order carriers; there is no separate geometry-order vs solution-order concept. Node ordering follows tables in the documentation. No arbitrary-order or per-cell polynomial-degree description; polyhedra with curved faces are not covered (unverified). The newer ex_field/EX_BASIS field type hints at basis metadata but I did not verify its semantics.
parallel: Nemesis extension (NEMESIS_FILE_VERSION 2.6) holds per-processor files with internal/border/external node and element lists and communication maps; nem_slice/nem_spread/epu split and join. Exodus has since absorbed this in the main API (nemesis-to-exodus-api-mapping.md). Ghost layers are implicit via the external/border entities. Parallel I/O via netCDF-4/HDF5 is possible. Details of ghost-layer depth are unverified.
geometry_association: None in the format. Block ids, names and properties are used by convention to carry CAD volume/surface ids (Cubit puts them in block/sideset ids), but there is no entity-to-B-rep link, no parametric coordinates and no geometry storage.
spec_quality: Informal. The 'spec' is the C API header (exodusII.h, version 9.06) plus Doxygen pages and example tests (testwt-nfaced.c). The file format (netCDF dimension/variable names) is documented only indirectly. No formally versioned schema or conformance suite found; version bumps tracked in header macros.
storage: netCDF container. Formats: classic (read only; about 2 GiB model limit), 64-bit offset (default; 4 GiB per dataset), netCDF-4 classic (HDF5, 32-bit ints), netCDF-4 non-classic (HDF5, 64-bit ints, effectively unlimited), and CDF5 (PnetCDF, evaluated). Per-component coordinate datasets avoid single huge arrays. One file per rank in parallel runs. Performance is good for bulk reads, with no random-access index structures.
ecosystem: Writers/readers: Cubit, Sierra, MOOSE/libMesh (ExodusII_IO, C0Polygon/C0Polyhedron support verified in source, with the restrictions above), Trilinos/STK/IOSS, ParaView/VTK (reader had polyhedra bugs per the 2016 thread), MFEM (exodus writer), GiD, many neutronics tools. Bindings: C, Fortran, Python (exodus3.py, in SEACAS). IOSS provides a unified C++ abstraction over Exodus, CGNS and others.

corrections.claim: EX_API_VERS 9.06f (release 2025-08-25)
corrections.correction: exodusII.h on master (clone tip 2026-10-22) has EXODUS_VERSION "9.06", EX_API_VERS 9.06f, EXODUS_RELEASE_DATE "August 25, 2025", NEMESIS_FILE_VERSION 2.6 — all confirmed. But 2025-08-25 is the Exodus library's internal date macro, not a SEACAS release: GitHub tags are v2025-08-19 and v2025-08-28 (latest v2026-08-11; header still 9.06).

corrections.claim: Assemblies: type is EX_ELEM_BLOCK or EX_ASSEMBLY
corrections.correction: That is only a comment in the ex_assembly struct. ex_put_assemblies.c writes assemblies[i].type as an int attribute with no validation of allowed values; IOSS Assembly::add() accepts any GroupingEntity and enforces only homogeneity (first member fixes m_type; mixed types raise 'member entities must be homogeneous'). So an assembly may hold any one entity kind (blocks, sets, assemblies), but not a mix.

corrections.claim: ex_field/EX_BASIS semantics unverified; no separate geometry-order vs solution-order concept
corrections.correction: ex_basis is self-describing in exodusII.h: per-DoF subc_dim (0 node/1 edge/2 face/3 volume), subc_ordinal, subc_dof_ordinal, subc_num_dof and parametric xi/eta/zeta; ex_quadrature stores points+weights; ex_field nests up to 2 types (EX_MAX_FIELD_NESTING 2) with EX_SCALAR/VECTOR/TENSOR/QUATERNION kinds. So Exodus does now carry a DoF-on-subcell basis descriptor for fields (solution order), separate from node-count-keyed element geometry. Consumer support is unknown.

corrections.claim: Each rank writes its own file (name.N.rank); nem_slice and nem_spread decompose/distribute
corrections.correction: File-per-rank is one mode. The header also has PARALLEL_AWARE_EXODUS with ex_create_par/ex_open_par (netCDF-4 parallel HDF5 or PnetCDF single-file I/O). IOSS reads a single undecomposed file in parallel with on-the-fly decomposition (DECOMPOSITION_METHOD: default LINEAR; EXTERNAL/MAP/VARIABLE; RCB/RIB/HSFC/BLOCK/CYCLIC/RANDOM need Zoltan; KWAY/GEOM_KWAY/METIS_SFC need ParMETIS) and can auto-join output. Per-rank naming is basename.NPROC.RANK with rank zero-padded to the width of NPROC (e.g. basename.64.03).

corrections.claim: 2016 ParaView thread (search snippet only, unverified) reports the reader wrongly assumed one face block per element block
corrections.correction: Now verified (via search summaries; kitware pages return 403): Ethan Coon (LANL) reported it; Greg Sjaardema confirmed NFACED face ids are file-scope implicit ids spanning all face blocks in file order; fixed as ParaView issue 16062 / VTK MR 2187 (target 5.1). Polyhedra handling regressed later: issue 18360 (clip crash on NFACED), 19915 (sideset rendering on polyhedral meshes fails, v5.8), 21318 (5.10 reader rejects nsided face block). Treat ParaView polyhedra support as fragile.

corrections.claim: Non-conformal: not exhaustively searched for contact-pair conventions in Sierra (unverified)
corrections.correction: Confirmed: Sierra codes pair the two sidesets in the solver input deck, not in the Exodus file. Fuego: 'begin nonconformal boundary condition on surface surface_4 / opposing sides = surface_5 / end' (DG contact condition, applied on both sides). Aria/Adagio contact: 'Contact Surface ... Contains' plus search tolerance in the deck. Exodus itself stores only the two sidesets.

corrections.claim: Cubit puts [CAD volume/surface ids] in block/sideset ids
corrections.correction: Cubit block/sideset/nodeset ids are user-specified integers ('Access to an Element Block is accomplished through a user-specified integer Block ID'); sidesets are built by assigning surfaces/curves to a chosen sideset id. No option to export CAD entity ids into Exodus was found; only names are written. Geometry association lives in Cubit's .cub, not the Exodus file.

corrections.claim: The file format (netCDF dimension/variable names) is documented only indirectly
corrections.correction: There is no standalone schema document, but the on-disk names are enumerated as ~290 DIM_*/VAR_* macros in the internal header exodusII_int.h (e.g. coordx, connect<n>, fbconn<n>, ebepecnt<n>, fbepecnt<n>). NetCDF-Mapping.md only counts dims/vars per entity for NC_MAX limits but does state the data-model invariants: a mesh-entity is in exactly one block, zero or more sets, and there is a single implicit node block.

corrections.claim: Node-to-element, element-to-element and face-to-element relations are NOT stored
corrections.correction: True for upward adjacency, but downward adjacency can be stored for any block: ex_put_block takes num_edges_per_entry/num_faces_per_entry and ex_put_conn(node_conn, elem_edge_conn, elem_face_conn) writes element->edge and element->face connectivity for standard (HEX/TET) blocks too, not just NFACED. Almost no writers use it. Also NFACED blocks may optionally carry node connectivity ('can be defined, but it isn't required').

corrections.claim: CDF5 (PnetCDF, evaluated)
corrections.correction: Exodus-Formats.md still says 'being evaluated', but the create flag EX_64BIT_DATA (0x400000, 'CDF-5 format: classic model but 64 bit dimensions and sizes') exists in the API alongside EX_NETCDF4, EX_NOCLASSIC, EX_ALL_INT64_DB/API, so it is a usable mode.

corrections.claim: tet up to 40 nodes in exodus-element-types.md
corrections.correction: Table also lists hex up to 64 nodes and wedge up to 52 (Exodus+IOSS only; nem_slice/nem_spread cap at hex27/wedge21), pyramid to 19, tri to 13, quad to 16. Only the base topology name is required; node count may be appended. Unknown element types can be stored losslessly but the library then cannot return side-set node lists or convert nodes<->sides.

missing_important: Side sets on polyhedral blocks are unsupported by the Exodus library itself: 'nfaced'/'nsided' appear only in the 4 polyhedra-specific source files; ex_int_get_block_param.c maps them to EX_EL_UNK, so ex_get_side_set_node_list / ex_cvt_nodes_to_sides hit the 'unsupported element type' error branch. (elem, local side) pairs can still be written, but no node resolution or side numbering is defined for NFACED — a first-order gap for a polyhedra-first boundary-set design.

libMesh C0Polyhedron/NFACED Exodus I/O is very new (header copyright 2025; PRs #4451-#4539 through Sep 2026 still touching cell_c0polyhedron.h), and only writes/reads a restricted subset; MFEM's ExodusII writer (v4.8+) writes Exodus API/DB version 4.72 and one block per attribute with a single element type — polyhedra ecosystem support is immature across the board, not just ParaView.
Assemblies and blobs can carry per-timestep 'reduction variables' (ex_put_reduction_vars), i.e. scalar results per grouping entity — a partition-layer result channel absent from the report.

Exodus has 'coordinate frames' (ex_put_coordinate_frames) and per-entity 'properties' (ex_put_prop) as the only metadata hooks beyond names/attributes — relevant if geometry association is to be smuggled in by convention.
Names: MAX_NAME_LENGTH default 32 but ex_set_max_name_length allows up to NC_MAX_NAME (256); EX_INQ_DB_MAX_ALLOWED/USED_NAME_LENGTH inquiry exists.

Data-model invariants stated in NetCDF-Mapping.md: every mesh-entity belongs to exactly one block and zero or more sets; there is a single implicit node block; each entity has an optional name and a required non-negative id — this is the closest thing to a formal schema statement.

Exodus is also a results container (time steps, nodal/element/set/global variables, truth tables), which is why most consumers (ParaView, Sierra) treat it as the canonical interchange; an IR that only exports mesh will still need a results-export story.

topic: CGNS (SIDS + HDF5): NGON_n/NFACE_n polyhedra, zones, ZoneBC, families, GridConnectivity (abutting non-1to1), high-order, CPEX, 4.x changes
summary: CGNS (CFD General Notation System) is a long-lived, standards-body-governed (CGNS Steering Committee) data model, the SIDS (Standard Interface Data Structures), stored as a tree of typed nodes. The tree is serialized in ADF (legacy) or HDF5 (default), accessed through the Mid-Level Library (cgnslib, C/Fortran, parallel via cgp_*). It is a hierarchical, self-describing node tree (name, label ending in _t, data type, dims, data), not a relational store. Unstructured meshes live in Zone_t -> Elements_t sections (one per ElementType, global 1-based ElementRange), with NGON_n/NFACE_n for arbitrary polyhedra, and ZoneBC_t / ZoneGridConnectivity_t / Family_t for boundaries, interfaces and sets. Maturity is high: releases run through 4.5.2 (4.5.x added the CPEX0046 particle extension and poly-element APIs; 4.4.0 added HDF5 multi-dataset parallel IO). CPEX0041 reworked NGON/NFACE storage (SIDS V3.4; reverted in the 3.4.2 library, reintroduced in 4.0.0). It is the nearest existing baseline for a versatile exchangeable mesh IR, but its non-conformal support is thin and its polyhedra remain a face-list encoding. Docs were read from cgns.org/cgns-archives (cgns.github.io URLs 301-redirect to cgns.org; some non-archive paths returned 404).
data_model: Tree: CGNSBase_t (CellDimension, PhysicalDimension) -> Zone_t (Structured/Unstructured/UserDefined; VertexSize, CellSize, VertexSizeBoundary) -> GridCoordinates_t (one DataArray per coordinate), Elements_t sections, FlowSolution_t, ZoneBC_t, ZoneGridConnectivity_t, Family links. Elements_t fields (verified, SIDS gridflow page): ElementRange (IndexRange_t, global 1-based; ElementSize = end-start+1), ElementType (enum), ElementConnectivity (DataArray int [ElementDataSize]), ElementStartOffset (int [ElementSize+1]; required only for MIXED, NGON_n, NFACE_n), ParentElements (int [ElementSize,2], optional, second parent 0 on boundary), ParentElementsPosition (int [ElementSize,2], optional, canonical face position in each parent), ElementSizeBoundary (optional; 0 = unsorted, else boundary elements first), Rind. Standard types: connectivity = nodes per element concatenated, ElementDataSize = ElementSize*NPE[type]. MIXED: per element the type code then its nodes; offsets advance by NPE+1. NGON_n: ElementConnectivity lists the nodes of each face; face i occupies [Offset[i], Offset[i+1]). NFACE_n: lists face element numbers (from the NGON_n section) per polyhedron; sign = orientation (positive = face normal outward, negative = inward). Pre-CPEX0041 layout interleaved counts (Nnodes1,Node11,...; Nfaces1,Face11,...); CPEX0041 moves counts into ElementStartOffset (CSR-style, e.g. [0,4,7,11,...] instead of [4,3,4,...], last value = total connectivity length) so parallel readers can slice offset ranges independently. Identity is positional integer index; the SIDS core has no global ids. Boundary facets are ordinary face elements in their own sections, referenced from ZoneBC PointList (GridLocation FaceCenter) by element number. HDF5 mapping: each node holds one array; types MT, I4, R4, R8, C1, LK (link); CGNSLibraryVersion_t sits under the file root; 64-bit cgsize_t is the default build since 4.2.0.
polyhedra: First-class but encoded as a two-level face-based structure: one NGON_n section holds all faces (node lists), one NFACE_n section holds cells as signed lists of face numbers. Per SIDS: except for boundary faces, each face of a polyhedral element must be shared by another polyhedral element (closed, face-sharing). ParentElements/ParentElementsPosition give optional materialized face-to-cell adjacency. Guidance seen in search results (secondary, unverified): a zone should not mix NGON/NFACE with simple MIXED elements, so such meshes are split into separate zones. CPEX0041 fixed NGON; its authors state MIXED and NFACE have the same interleaved-count parallel-IO problem and should be fixed in a later CPEX (the current SIDS page does require ElementStartOffset for all three). 4.3.0 added basic duplicate-face-index detection in NFACE; 4.5.0 added poly-element read/write APIs (cg_poly_elements_read is used by PETSc; exact signatures unverified). No edge entities for 3D polyhedra, no planarity/convexity guarantees, no curved or high-order polygon faces.
nonconformal: Represented not in mesh topology but in ZoneGridConnectivity_t as relations between zones. GridConnectivity1to1_t is structured-only (PointRange, PointRangeDonor, Transform). General GridConnectivity_t has GridConnectivityType = Overset (default) | Abutting | Abutting1to1; GridLocation Vertex or FaceCenter for abutting (CellCenter for overset); receiver PointRange or PointList (unstructured: node ids or face element numbers); ZoneDonorName; optional CellListDonor (donor cell/element containing each receiver point); optional InterpolantsDonor (real [CellDimension, PointListSize] parametric coordinates; unstructured limited to BAR_2, TRI_3, QUAD_4, TETRA_4, PYRA_5, PENTA_6, HEXA_8). PointListDonor is allowed only for Abutting1to1. Three donor-detail levels: full (zone+cell+interpolants), partial (zone+cell), minimal (zone name only), so for mismatched abutting the standard allows storing only the pairing and leaving geometric projection/intersection to the solver. Each interface is stored twice, once per zone. GridConnectivityProperty_t holds Periodic_t (RotationCenter, RotationAngle, Translation) and AverageInterface_t (AverageAll/Circumferential/Radial/I/J/K, for mixing planes). Detection is declarative: the writer must tag the patch as Abutting; there is no rule to infer non-conformity from geometry, no imprint/overlap-area data, and no conservative face-to-face weights (only point-in-cell interpolants). Hanging nodes inside one zone: nothing found in the pages read (unverified). Which solvers consume Abutting non-1to1 interfaces: not verified in this pass.
sets_and_partitions: Boundaries: ZoneBC_t holds BC_t patches; each BC_t has BCType (required enum, e.g. BCWall, BCSymmetryPlane, BCFarfield, FamilySpecified), GridLocation (default Vertex), exactly one of PointRange or PointList (unstructured: node ids or element numbers per GridLocation; FaceCenter in 3D), optional BCDataSet_t (Dirichlet/Neumann), FamilyName, AdditionalFamilyName, BCProperty. BCType vocabulary is CFD (no vacuum/reflective/albedo for neutron transport except BCGeneral/UserDefined). Regions and materials: Family_t at CGNSBase_t level is an intermediate object between mesh regions and CAD geometry; BC_t or Zone_t reference it by FamilyName, so BC/properties can change without touching mesh or geometry. Family_t children: FamilyBC_t (BCType, FamilyBCDataSet_t), GeometryReference_t, RotatingCoordinates_t, nested Family_t (hierarchy; CPEX43 in 4.1.0 makes it an explicit tree). A family may extend to a volume of cells for zone properties. Cell-level subsets within a zone via ZoneSubRegion_t and separate Elements sections (details unverified). Partitions: multi-zone is the primary partition mechanism, each zone self-contained with interface lists. Mapping to the user's three layers: geometry = GeometryReference_t pointing at external CAD files, partition/material = Family_t, mesh = Zone/Elements; the layers are linked by name strings, not typed references.
high_order: Verified ElementType_t list: BAR_2/3/4, TRI_3/6/9/10, QUAD_4/8/9/12/16, TETRA_4/10/16/20, PYRA_5/13/14/21/29/30, PENTA_6/15/18/24/38/40, HEXA_8/20/27/32/56/64, plus NODE, MIXED, NGON_n, NFACE_n. This covers up to cubic and quartic types (quartic added via CPEX0038, SIDS 2014). Each type is a fixed enum with NPE[type] nodes; node ordering is defined on a separate 'Unstructured Grid Element Numbering Conventions' page that was not read (ordering unverified). Consequences: no degree parameter, orders beyond the table are inexpressible, no basis flag (Lagrange assumed), no high-order polyhedra/polygons (NGON_n faces are plain node lists). InterpolantsDonor works only for linear types.
parallel: Parallel CGNS (cgp_* API over parallel HDF5/MPI, added around 2013; CGNS_CONFIG_HDF5_MPI_COMM option). One global file with global 1-based element/vertex numbering; ranks read contiguous slices (slice ElementStartOffset, then the matching connectivity range; the explicit design goal of CPEX0041). 4.4.0 added cgp_*_multi_* APIs using HDF5 1.14 multi-dataset I/O; 4.5.0 added PointSet parallel read/write; 4.5.2 fixed multi-dataset bugs. The SIDS has no ghost/halo or owner-rank concept: partitioning is either by zones or application-defined slicing of global arrays with the application building halos. Interface pairs are stored twice for consistency.
geometry_association: Weak, indirect, name-based. Family_t + GeometryReference_t (GeometryFormat enum: NASA-IGES, SDRC, Unigraphics, ProEngineer, ICEM-CFD; GeometryFile; optional GeometryEntity_t list, default one entity named after the family). CAD entities stay in the external file and are not redefined in CGNS; mesh surfaces reference the family via FamilyName on BC_t or Zone_t. No per-facet or per-node classification (dimension + CAD entity id), no parametric coordinates on boundary nodes, and no STEP/B-rep format in the enum.
spec_quality: Strong and versioned. The SIDS is a formal text spec with typed node definitions (required/optional/default flags), a separate HDF5 mapping spec, and Mid-Level Library docs. Changes go through numbered CPEX proposals voted by the Steering Committee (0038 quartic, 0041 NGON, 0042 bounding box, 0043 family tree, 0046 particles). Weak spots: some semantics left informal (memory order of ParentElements, donor-detail levels), the CPEX0041 layout change broke compatibility (3.4.1 change reverted in 3.4.2, reintroduced in 4.0.0, with compatibility fixes through 4.1.2), and the docs site has moved between hosts/paths. Latest release seen: 4.5.2 (30 Apr; year not shown on the release page); 4.4.0 was June 2023 per the news page.
storage: Backends: ADF (legacy) and HDF5 (default). HDF5 mapping: each CGNS node maps to an HDF5 node, children unordered and identified by name/label/id; one array of a single type per node; LK links can reference nodes in the same or other files (shared grids without copying); CGNSLibraryVersion_t under root; names printable ASCII, no '/' or leading '.'. 4.1.0 introduced HDF5 compact storage for datasets under 64 KiB; 4.2.0 made 64-bit the default build, added in-memory (diskless) files and *_general element/parent-data APIs; 4.4.0 parallel multi-dataset I/O; 4.5.1 HDF5 2.0 compatibility. Performance: bulk arrays are plain HDF5 datasets so large I/O is efficient; pain points are many small nodes (hence compact storage) and the old interleaved NGON array that required scanning for random access. Exact HDF5 attribute/group layout not confirmed (the general mapping page did not specify it).
database_like_aspects: Moderately database-like but not queryable. A typed, schema-governed hierarchical store: entity sets are Elements_t sections sharing one global numbering space across dimensions; relations are stored arrays (NGON face-nodes, NFACE cell-faces, optional ParentElements as materialized face-to-cell adjacency); tags/sets are BC PointLists plus Family names; cross-references are by name string or integer index (no foreign keys). It has a schema with required/optional/default flags, but no indexes, no query language, no on-demand derived adjacency (only precomputed ParentElements), and per-entity data only via fields at a GridLocation (FlowSolution_t, ZoneSubRegion_t).
ecosystem: Broad CFD ecosystem. Verified by search results: VTK/ParaView vtkCGNSReader (polyhedra support via merge requests), PETSc DMPlex (plexcgns2.c using cg_poly_elements_read). Commonly cited but not individually verified here: Fluent, STAR-CCM+, CFX, Pointwise, ICEM, Gmsh, SU2, Code_Saturne, NASA FUN3D/OVERFLOW, ONERA elsA/Cassiopee. Bindings: C and Fortran mid-level library; Python wrappers (pyCGNS, h5py-style reading) unverified. No evidence found of a nuclear/neutron-transport user base; the BC vocabulary is CFD-centric. Exporting to CGNS gives ParaView/PETSc compatibility cheaply.
strengths: Formal, versioned, committee-governed spec with an extension process (CPEX) and HDF5 as default container: the most direct existing baseline for an exchangeable mesh IR.
Polyhedra are first-class via NGON_n + NFACE_n with signed face references and CSR-style ElementStartOffset (CPEX0041), parallel-read friendly.
Family_t separates mesh regions from BC/material properties and from CAD references, mirroring the geometry / partition / mesh layering.
Multi-zone model with ZoneGridConnectivity_t covers 1to1, abutting, overset, periodic and mixing-plane in one framework.
Wide tool support (ParaView/VTK, PETSc, commercial CFD) so a CGNS export buys interoperability.
Parallel HDF5 I/O built in (cgp_*), including multi-dataset I/O since 4.4.0.
weaknesses: Positional integer identity only; no stable global ids, no ghost/owner model in the SIDS.

Non-conformal interfaces are declarative only (Abutting tag, donor cell, point interpolants); no face-overlap/imprint data, no conservative face-to-face weights; interpolants only for linear element types.
NGON/NFACE require closed face-sharing polyhedra and mixing with standard elements in a zone is discouraged; polyhedra are a face-list encoding with no edges.
High-order is a closed enumeration of Lagrange types (max quartic-ish tabulated), no degree parameter, no high-order polyhedra, no curved-geometry metadata.
Geometry association is only a file name plus entity name; no entity-level classification of mesh facets to B-rep faces/edges/vertices, no parametric coordinates.
BC vocabulary is CFD-specific (no vacuum/reflective/albedo); tree storage is awkward to query; no on-demand derived adjacency.
Compatibility has been brittle: the CPEX0041 layout change forced the 3.4.1 revert and several 4.x fixes.
lessons_for_us: Adopt: offsets + flat index (CSR) for all variable-arity relations (cell->faces, face->nodes) with N+1 offsets, uniformly for polygons, polyhedra and mixed cells from day one; never interleave counts with data.

Adopt: signed face references (or separate orientation bits) for cell->face, plus an optional materialized face->(left,right) adjacency like ParentElements, but with the local face position and array memory order explicitly defined.

Adopt the Family indirection: mesh entity -> family/label -> (material/BC properties, CAD reference). Differ by making these typed ids with referential integrity rather than name strings, and allow sets at any dimension (cells, faces, edges, nodes), not only BC PointLists.

Differ: model the three layers (geometry B-rep, partition/material, mesh) as separate tables with typed foreign keys: mesh entity -> classification (B-rep dim + id) and cell -> region -> material. CGNS offers only a filename + entity name string.

Differ: represent non-conformal interfaces as first-class interface entities owning paired face sets plus a derived overlap table (face_a, face_b, overlap area/fraction, optional projection transform), detected by tolerance-based coincidence of faces on the same B-rep interface (information-level imprinting). CGNS stores only the Abutting tag and point-in-cell donors.

Adopt: a single container (HDF5, or Zarr/Arrow-like columnar) with typed arrays, explicit schema version, and a proposal process; treat CGNS as an export/import target, not the native IR, which gives ParaView/PETSc access for free.
Differ: stable global ids and owner-rank/ghost metadata in the schema so partitioning is part of the IR.

Differ: describe high-order by (cell shape, polynomial degree, basis/node set) instead of a closed enum of node counts, and allow curved faces on polyhedra; export to CGNS Lagrange enums when the degree fits.
Lesson from 4.x: layout changes break files. Version every array layout and ship converters at the same time.
Add neutron-transport boundary types (vacuum, reflective, albedo, white) as first-class; CGNS BCType is CFD-only.

missing_important: Pending accepted CPEXs (all 'accepted; awaiting implementation', none in any release): CPEX0045 high-order/curved elements (target 5.0); CPEX0047 Quadrature Rules and Data Storage (2021); CPEX0049 Compatibility Version Control for Interoperability (2026-08-04) which targets exactly the file-compat brittleness the report flags; CPEX0050 DOF Storage Layout and Interface Continuity (2026-08-04, GitHub CGNS/CGNS#974, target 5.0 with 0045): DofStorage_t {SharedDofs, IndependentDofs} and InterfaceContinuity_t {ContinuousInterface, DiscontinuousInterface} on FlowSolution_t/DiscreteData_t/ZoneSubRegion_t, directly relevant to a DG neutron-transport consumer. CPEX0044 Encoding Functions still under review. Source: https://cgns.org/current/CPEX.html, CPEX PDFs.

Rejected CPEXs define what CGNS chose not to be and are the clearest baseline for 'we differ in X': 0008 Hierarchical Elements (hanging nodes / refinement trees, requested since the 2000 NUMECA proposal, never accepted), 0028 Face-Based Storage, 0016 Element Regions, 0037 Improvements for Multiblock Unstructured. CGNS has no hanging-node or constraint representation; a hanging-node mesh is expressible only as general polyhedra (a coarse cell adjacent to refined neighbours becomes a polyhedron with extra faces, satisfying the 'each face shared by another polyhedral element' rule) at the cost of losing hierarchy information (inference from the SIDS rule).

NGON_n is defined as 'all the faces in the grid' (interior and boundary in one section); on polyhedral meshes BC PointLists reference face ids inside the NGON_n section. ParentElements alone lets readers reconstruct NFACE_n (VTK MR 9342, merged 2022-07-06), so cell->face storage is effectively optional downstream.

Unstructured conformal 1-to-1 interfaces must be written as GridConnectivity_t with GridConnectivityType=Abutting1to1 plus PointListDonor, because GridConnectivity1to1_t is structured-only (confirmed; Pointwise README calls this 'legal but confusing').

Production non-conformal practice: Cassiopee/elsA write near-match interfaces as GridConnectivity_t Abutting with PointListDonor and an NMRatio node (outside the SIDS rule that PointListDonor is Abutting1to1-only) and then move the details into solver-specific '.Solver#Property' nodes (elsAProfile.adaptNearMatch); Flow360 reads ZoneGridConnectivity (Abutting1to1/Abutting/Overset, since release 23.3.2.0) and auto-detects interfaces if absent. Non-conformal semantics live in vendor UserDefinedData, not in the standard.

CPEX0045 scope note: ElementInterpolation_t is keyed by ElementType_t and 'the standard will only allow element types defined up to now', so even the accepted high-order extension does not give curved or high-order polygons/polyhedra; the report's 'differ: curved faces on polyhedra' is a genuine gap in both current and planned CGNS.
pyCGNS (MAP/PAT/VAL/NAV; v6.3.0 on PyPI, LGPL) reads/writes CGNS/HDF5 trees as Python lists via CHLone without the MLL, useful for prototyping an exporter and for validating trees (VAL).

HDF5 tuning: the CGNS/HDF5 mapping page states the MLL forces all HDF5 property lists to defaults (no chunking/compression exposed), partially stale since 4.1.0 compact storage; the 2022 news promised 4.3.0 'with HDF5 compression' but the 4.3.0 release notes list none. Treat compression through the MLL as unavailable unless verified.

Family hierarchy history: CPEX0033 (v3.2, 2013) enabled hierarchy via FamilyName_t 'FamilyParent' references; CPEX0043 (v4.1, 2020) added nested Family_t children; both mechanisms coexist in the current SIDS.

summary: MOAB (Mesh-Oriented datABase, Argonne; v5.6.0 per CMakeLists, repo HEAD checked 2026-10) is a C++ in-memory mesh database whose core idea is: a mesh is a flat set of typed entities (vertex, edge, tri, quad, polygon, tet, pyramid, prism, knife, hex, polyhedron, entity-set) identified by one integer handle, plus two generic grouping/annotation mechanisms: entity sets (with parent/child links) and tags (named typed key-value data on entities or sets). Everything semantic (materials, boundary conditions, geometry association, parallel partition, global IDs) is layered on top as TAG CONVENTIONS rather than as schema. It is the closest existing precedent for the 'mesh as database' framing. ITAPS (iMesh/iGeom/iRel/iMeshP) was the DOE SciDAC attempt to standardize that data model as language-neutral C interfaces; MOAB's own 5.6.0 release notes (PR #681) and README now declare ITAPS/iMesh deprecated in favor of native MOAB/iMOAB. DAGMC (Univ. Wisconsin/Svalinn; v3.2.4 in CMakeLists) stores a CAD B-rep topology as faceted triangles inside a MOAB .h5m file using exactly these sets/tags/parent-child conventions, and is integrated into OpenMC, MCNP5/6, Geant4, FLUKA, Tripoli4, Shift. MOAB is mature and widely used (E3SM, DAGMC, SIGMA) but has no formal versioned data-model spec: the contract is header comments, MBTagConventions.hpp and doc pages.
data_model: Handles (src/Internals.hpp): EntityHandle is an integer whose top MB_TYPE_WIDTH=4 bits hold the EntityType and the remaining bits (MB_ID_WIDTH = 8*sizeof(EntityHandle)-4) hold a 1-based ID (MB_START_ID=1). So the type is derivable from the handle with a shift, no lookup. EntityType enum (MBEntityType.h) includes MBVERTEX, MBEDGE, MBTRI, MBQUAD, MBPOLYGON, MBTET, MBPYRAMID, MBPRISM, MBKNIFE, MBHEX, MBPOLYHEDRON, MBENTITYSET (verified from the lines I read; MBVERTEX line not shown in my grep but the h5m doc lists the same topologies). Storage: SequenceManager holds per-type TypeSequenceManager of EntitySequence objects, each backed by SequenceData with startHandle..endHandle and 'arraySet' arrays (connectivity, coordinates, dense tag arrays per sequence). Handles are therefore allocated in contiguous runs so a Range (compressed list of [first,last] handle pairs) represents 'all hexes in a block' in O(1). Elements store connectivity down to vertices only (element -> vertex handles); polyhedra store face handles (faces are real entities of type MBPOLYGON/MBTRI/MBQUAD). Higher-dimension to lower-dimension adjacencies beyond that, and 'up' adjacencies (vertex->elements, face->cells), are created on demand and cached by AEntityFactory as std::vector<EntityHandle> adjacency lists (add_adjacency/remove_adjacency, 'create_if_missing' semantics) - i.e. adjacency is derived data, not stored in the file. Entity sets (MeshSet.hpp, MeshSetSequence): sets are entities (type MBENTITYSET), may contain entities AND other sets, and carry parent and child set lists. Option flags (Types.hpp): MESHSET_TRACK_OWNER=0x1 (entities keep back-pointers to sets), MESHSET_SET=0x2 (unique), MESHSET_ORDERED=0x4. Tags (Types.hpp): MB_TAG_BIT/SPARSE/DENSE/MESH/BYTES/VARLEN; DataType MB_TYPE_OPAQUE/INTEGER/DOUBLE/BIT/HANDLE. Sparse tags are an (unordered_)map<EntityHandle,void*> (SparseTag.hpp); dense tags are arrays per SequenceData (DenseTag.hpp); VarLen variants exist; MB_TYPE_HANDLE lets a tag point to other entities/sets, which is how relations are made first-class. h5m file (src/io/mhdf, names-and-paths.h, doc/details/c_h5mformat.h): HDF5 root group '/tstt' with sub-groups 'nodes' (dataset 'coordinates'), 'elements' (one subgroup per type+node-count, dataset 'connectivity'; polys add 'poly_indices'), 'sets' (datasets 'list','contents','children','parents'), 'tags' (per-tag subgroups with 'id_list' and 'values' for sparse; dense tags stored under nodes/elements groups), 'history', and enum 'elemtypes'. One global ID space across vertices, elements and sets (IDs positive, unique over all types; start_id/max_id attributes). Set table 'list' is n x 4: end index into contents, end index into children, end index into parents, and flags; flag mhdf_SET_RANGE_BIT=0x8 means contents are stored as (start,count) ranges instead of a flat list. Element type = topology + node count, so HEX8 vs HEX27 are separate groups.
polyhedra: First-class: MBPOLYGON and MBPOLYHEDRON are native EntityTypes (also PolyElementSeq.cpp). In h5m, a poly group stores two lists: concatenated connectivity and a per-poly 'last index' array (CSR-style offsets), per mhdf_createPolyConnectivity doc; polygons list node IDs, polyhedra list FACE IDs (faces are real entities, either MBPOLYGON or fixed 2D elements). So the cell->face->vertex hierarchy is explicit only for polyhedra; ordinary elements skip the face level. Face orientation within a polyhedron is not described in the doc text I read (unverified how outward-orientation is conveyed). Mixed element types coexist naturally because the handle encodes type.
high_order: Element type in h5m is topology plus node count (e.g. HEX20/HEX27, TET10), so mid-edge/face/body nodes are extra connectivity entries ordered per CN (canonical numbering) tables; HigherOrderFactory.cpp converts linear to quadratic and back, and a 'HAS_MID_NODES' tag convention marks which sub-entities carry mid nodes (MBTagConventions.hpp). It is Lagrange-node-based only: no notion of polynomial basis, geometry order versus solution order, or curved-geometry mapping stored with the mesh (unverified beyond the code inspected). Tools such as honodes.cpp exist.
nonconformal: MOAB has no native non-conformal-interface concept. Conformity is simply whatever shared vertices/faces exist: a non-conformal interface is just two surfaces whose faces do not share vertices, and nothing in the model records that they are meant to be coupled. tools/merge.cpp (mesh merge of coincident vertices) and Skinner.cpp (extract boundary skin) are utilities for making conformal / finding boundaries. For solution transfer between non-matching meshes MOAB provides mbcoupler, intersection meshes (mbIntxCheck, mbtempest.cpp / TempestRemap integration, E3SM-oriented) which compute overlap meshes and remap weights offline. DAGMC likewise relies on a watertight faceted surface model (make_watertight tool; OpenMC docs say DAGMC models must be clean/watertight, with overlap support a future goal) - so imprint/merge is done upstream in Cubit before export, and the h5m only records the already-merged topology via shared surface sets with GEOM_SENSE_2 pointing to the two adjacent volumes. This is the 'imprint and merge at the information level' idea: a surface set is shared by two volumes via the sense tag rather than duplicated.
sets_and_partitions: Entity sets + tags are the single mechanism for every grouping. Conventions (doc/details/b_iometadata.h and MBTagConventions.hpp): GEOM_DIMENSION (int, default -1) tags a set as geometric vertex/curve/surface/volume (0-3) and the set holds the mesh owned by that model entity (not mesh of bounding entities); parent/child links encode B-rep topology (volume parent -> surface -> curve -> vertex), order not significant so face loops cannot be reliably reconstructed; GLOBAL_ID (int, default 0) is the CAD id; CATEGORY (char[32]) and NAME (char[32]) give generic labels; GROUP-category sets hold geometric-entity sets plus mesh entities; GEOM_SENSE_2 is a sparse tag of 2 EntityHandles on a surface: first = volume for which the surface is forward-sensed (normal points out), second = reverse; edges use variable-length GEOM_SENSE_N_ENTS / GEOM_SENSE_N_SENSES (sense 0 forward, 1 reverse, -1 unknown). MOAB explicitly states it does NOT represent the geometric model's shape, only topology and ids; shape stays in CGM/another kernel. Mesh-side semantics: MATERIAL_SET (int) sets = Exodus/Cubit element blocks (typically containing the volume sets, retrieved recursively), DIRICHLET_SET (usually vertices), NEUMANN_SET (faces; reverse-sense faces go into a sub-set tagged NEUSET_SENSE=-1). Parallel: PARALLEL_PARTITION sets, plus per-entity tags __PARALLEL_STATUS (bit flags NOT_OWNED 0x1, SHARED 0x2, MULTISHARED 0x4, INTERFACE 0x8, GHOST 0x10), __PARALLEL_SHARED_PROC(S), shared handles. DAGMC conventions (DAGMC/doc, DagMC.cpp, dagmcmetadata.cpp): volumes are EMPTY sets (parents of their surface sets); surface sets contain triangles and vertices; curves contain edges; group sets (CATEGORY 'Group', NAME strings) carry metadata as strings like 'mat:fuel', 'rho:10.5', 'importance:...', 'boundary:Reflecting', and a 'mat:graveyard' group marks the bounding void; an implicit complement volume is synthesized at load from surfaces with only one sense defined; an OBB tree (tag 'OBB_TREE') is built per surface and merged per volume for ray tracing. OpenMC (src/dagmc.cpp) maps 'mat:' to cell material, 'void/vacuum/graveyard' to void, and 'boundary:' values (vacuum, reflective) to surface BCs; periodic unsupported in DAGMC.
strengths: Single, tiny conceptual core (typed entities + sets + tags) that has absorbed very different needs: FE meshes, CAD topology (DAGMC), climate grids (E3SM), parallel partitions, with no schema change
Handle with embedded type and contiguous sequences gives O(1) type queries and compact Range representation; dense tags as per-sequence arrays give SoA performance
Tag-with-handle-type makes arbitrary relations (sense, owner, periodic partner) first-class and persisted
Sets that contain sets plus parent/child links give exactly the layered geometry / material-partition / mesh structure the user describes; same file holds all three layers
Polygon/polyhedron first-class, mixed elements natural, HDF5/MPI-IO parallel read with ghosting and shared-entity tags
Proven in production Monte Carlo transport (DAGMC with OpenMC, MCNP, Geant4, FLUKA) and ships Python bindings (pymoab), iMOAB, C and Fortran interfaces
Adjacency is derived and cached on demand, not stored, keeping files lean
weaknesses: No formal, versioned semantic spec: meaning lives in naming conventions (GEOM_DIMENSION, CATEGORY strings, 'mat:' parsing); different tools disagree (e.g. GEOM_SENSE_2 created dense by DagMC and sparse by GeomTopoTool, mailing-list 2010/2011, which breaks tag lookup depending on load order)
Stringly-typed metadata (32-byte NAME/CATEGORY, DAGMC 'mat:xxx' strings) with no validation or units
Geometry layer is topology only; shape is not stored, so geometry/mesh association is one-way and lossy (no parametric position of mesh nodes on curves/surfaces; loop ordering lost)
No concept of non-conformal interface, hanging nodes, or mortar; conformity is implicit, so coupling is not detectable from the data
Polyhedron orientation conventions and high-order basis/curved-geometry info are not specified beyond node counts
Pre-C++17 style API, error-code return convention, large surface area; ITAPS standardization effort is deprecated (MOAB 5.6.0 PR #681), showing the interface-standard route did not take hold
Tag/set flexibility costs: sparse tags are hash maps, set membership of many entities is heavy unless range-compressed, and nothing enforces consistency between tags (no schema, no constraints)
DAGMC itself needs watertight triangulated surface, no curved surfaces, no volumetric overlap, so it is a faceted B-rep not a true CAD model
lessons_for_us: ADOPT the 'mesh is a database' stance, but make it typed: a small fixed core (entity kinds with dimension, connectivity, sets, relations) plus a SCHEMA-REGISTERED annotation mechanism, where each tag/field has name, type, unit, entity-kind domain and cardinality, so we get MOAB's flexibility without the stringly-typed ambiguity

ADOPT first-class sets that may contain sets and entities plus parent/child edges: this directly models our 3 layers (geometry B-rep sets, material/partition groups as sets of volumes, mesh entities as set members). DIFFER by giving each layer a named namespace and explicit typed cross-layer links (mesh entity -> owning geometric entity, geometric volume -> partition) instead of one flat set space distinguished by a CATEGORY string

ADOPT DAGMC's 'surface shared by two volumes with sense' (GEOM_SENSE_2) as the information-level imprint/merge representation: it is exactly 'imprinting at the information level'. Make it an explicit required field of the geometry layer (surface -> (volume_fwd, volume_rev)) and keep volumes empty of mesh, as DAGMC does
ADOPT dimension-in-handle / contiguous-sequence design: type-tagged IDs and Range-compressed sets give cheap bulk ops; in Rust use newtype IDs with kind + index and run-length ID ranges
ADOPT 'adjacency is derived, cached, not stored' for up-adjacency, and store explicit face entities (cell->face->vertex) for polyhedra with orientation sign, which MOAB leaves ambiguous

ADOPT h5m file layout ideas: one global ID space, CSR-style offsets (poly_indices, set 'list' end-index table, range-encoded set contents) in HDF5 chunked datasets; DIFFER by versioning the on-disk spec, putting a schema and layer manifest in the file, and defining it formally

DIFFER: store geometry association richly (parametric coords of boundary nodes on B-rep entities, loop ordering, curved-geometry references) since our own B-rep kernel exists; MOAB deliberately stores none of this

DIFFER: represent non-conformal interfaces explicitly, e.g. an interface record pairing two face sets (with tolerance/transform/mortar metadata), so solvers do not have to infer them; MOAB and DAGMC have no such concept
ADOPT parallel pattern of owner/shared/ghost status bits and shared-procs lists as per-entity tags, but make partition a first-class layer

Consider the DAGMC/OpenMC ecosystem as a neutron-transport target: write an exporter that emits triangulated surface sets with GEOM_DIMENSION, GLOBAL_ID, GEOM_SENSE_2, CATEGORY and 'mat:' group NAME strings so Cubit-free DAGMC/OpenMC works; likewise MOAB/h5m can be an interchange export rather than our native format
Lesson from ITAPS deprecation: do not make a C interface standard the product; make the on-disk, schema-defined data model the spec and generate bindings from it
Frame positioning as: 'conceptually MOAB (entities+sets+tags) with Exodus/Cubit semantics, but with a typed schema, versioned spec, explicit B-rep association and explicit non-conformal interfaces'

DAGMC 2010) were not fetched; iMesh/iGeom/iRel header text was not read directly; exact CATEGORY strings for Surface/Curve/Group sets other than 'Volume' were not confirmed in code I read.
spec_quality: Weak as a formal spec, strong as living practice. There is no versioned specification document; the contract is the C++ headers, Doxygen pages (h5m layout, 'metadata conventions' b_iometadata.h with a summary table), MBTagConventions.hpp, and the mhdf C API comments, which are actually quite precise for the file layout (set table columns, range bit, poly index lists). The DAGMC conventions are documented in the user guide and developer theory guide in prose but depend on string parsing ('mat:', 'boundary:', 'rho:'). ITAPS provided formal C interface specs (iMesh, iGeom, iRel, iMeshP) with a defined entity-set/tag model, but these are now deprecated in MOAB 5.6.0 and the standard did not achieve broad adoption.
storage: In memory: handle-indexed sequences with per-sequence arrays (struct-of-arrays), Range-compressed handle lists, hash-map sparse tags, adjacency vectors on demand. On disk: HDF5 (.h5m) under '/tstt' with nodes/elements/sets/tags groups, CSR-style offset tables, optional range-encoded set contents, MPI-IO parallel read/write via ReadHDF5/WriteHDF5 (files seen in src/io); also readers/writers for Exodus, VTK, Gmsh, Cubit .cub, netCDF climate formats (src/io listing). Performance characteristics beyond design intent (parallel I/O scaling numbers) were not measured and are unverified.
geometry_association: Via sets and tags only: GEOM_DIMENSION sets for vertex/curve/surface/volume, parent/child for topology, GLOBAL_ID for the CAD id, GEOM_SENSE_2 and GEOM_SENSE_N_* for orientation. The doc explicitly says MOAB does not represent shape; shape queries (arc length, normals) must go to CGM or another kernel (CGM was linked via iGeom, but MOAB 5.6.0 removed links to CGM per PR #681). Mesh-to-geometry link is by set membership (a mesh entity belongs to the set of the geometric entity that owns it), with no parametric coordinates stored. In DAGMC the 'geometry' is the faceted surface mesh itself, ray-traced via per-surface OBB trees, so geometry and mesh are the same data.
parallel: Distributed: each rank holds a local MOAB instance; ParallelComm resolves shared entities and tags them with __PARALLEL_STATUS bit flags (NOT_OWNED 0x1, SHARED 0x2, MULTISHARED 0x4, INTERFACE 0x8, GHOST 0x10), __PARALLEL_SHARED_PROC(S) and shared-handle tags, using GLOBAL_ID as the matching key; exchange_ghost_cells(ghost_dim, bridge_dim, num_layers, addl_ents,...) builds N-layer ghosting; partitions are represented as sets tagged PARALLEL_PARTITION; partitioning via Zoltan (auto-downloaded in 5.6.0) or mbpart tool; parallel HDF5 read does partition-on-read. iMeshP was the ITAPS parallel interface.

corrections.claim: DAGMC is integrated into OpenMC, MCNP5/6, Geant4, FLUKA, Tripoli4, Shift
corrections.correction: DAGMC's own repo doc gives maintenance status, not a flat list: OpenMC and MCNP6 implementations are actively maintained; Geant4 and FLUKA are 'occasionally updated'; the Shift implementation is 'still used internally at ORNL'; MCNP5 'is available'; Tripoli4 'was demonstrated in 2010, but not maintained'. For a transport-code target today, only OpenMC and MCNP6 are live.

corrections.claim: GLOBAL_ID (int, default 0) is the CAD id
corrections.correction: The header comment (MBTagConventions.hpp:85: 'default value = 0 // not -1 to allow gids stored in unsigned data types') and the code disagree: Core::globalId_tag() creates GLOBAL_ID as MB_TAG_DENSE, MB_TYPE_INTEGER (C int, 32-bit) with default -1 (Core.cpp:2683-2685). This header/code conflict is itself evidence for the 'no formal spec' weakness. h5m file IDs are `long` (mhdf_public.h:70) while the GLOBAL_ID tag stays C int; the 5.6.0 note about '64-bit global IDs' does not change the tag type in Core.cpp.

corrections.claim: Adjacency is derived data, not stored in the file / 'Adjacency is derived and cached on demand, not stored, keeping files lean'
corrections.correction: h5m has an optional `adjacency` dataset per node group and per element group (format: [entity id, count, adjacent ids...]). WriteHDF5::write_adjacencies persists whatever adjacency lists AEntityFactory holds at write time: explicit adjacencies plus vertex->element lists, which are off by default (mVertElemAdj=false) but are created for the whole mesh and kept on the first up-adjacency query. 'Not stored' describes default behaviour, not a format guarantee; files written after up-adjacency queries carry adjacency tables.

corrections.claim: Face orientation within a polyhedron is not described in the doc text I read (unverified how outward-orientation is conveyed)
corrections.correction: Confirmed, not merely unverified: MOAB stores no per-polyhedron face orientation. h5m polyhedron connectivity is a flat list of face IDs ('either polygons or 2D fixed-connectivity elements'); in-memory connectivity is unsigned face handles. ReadVtk resolves each VTK polyhedron face to an existing 2D entity by vertex set (get_adjacencies(connec, n, 2, false) -> adjFaces[0]), discarding VTK's winding, and caps faces at 20 vertices. A face shared by two polyhedra is referenced identically by both, so the outward side is undetermined; no orientation convention appears anywhere in src/ or doc/. This should be stated as a hard limitation for a polyhedral-first design.
