The spec page is inconsistent here: its size table uses the name NumberOfPolygonalFaces for the same quantity.

Temporal VTKHDF: a Steps group with Values, PartOffsets, NumberOfParts, PointOffsets, CellOffsets and ConnectivityIdOffsets (shape NSteps x NTopologies), {Point,Cell,Field}DataOffsets/{ArrayName}, FieldDataSizes, and polyhedron offsets (FaceConnectivityOffsets, FaceOffsetsOffsets, PolyhedronToFaceIdOffsets). Topology and geometry can therefore be static or per-step by pointing step offsets at the same ranges.

XML VTU: <UnstructuredGrid><Piece NumberOfPoints NumberOfCells><Points/><Cells> with DataArrays named connectivity, offsets, types, and for polyhedra faces and faceoffsets. The faces array is a face stream: per polyhedron, [nfaces, npts_f0, ids..., npts_f1, ids...]. Source: https://discourse.paraview.org/t/mixed-elements-including-polyhedron-in-vtu-file/4542 and a 2015 vtkusers post at https://public.kitware.com/pipermail/vtkusers/2015-May/090837.html. Per PyVista docs, VTK 9.4+ in-memory polyhedra moved to separate face-location and face-connectivity arrays rather than one padded stream (https://docs.pyvista.org/api/core/_autosummary/pyvista.unstructuredgrid.polyhedron_face_location_offsets). The reader and writer in 9.4+ are unverified. .pvtu is a master XML file listing one .vtu piece per rank.

XDMF: XML Xdmf > Domain > Grid (Uniform, Collection spatial or temporal, Tree, SubSet) with Topology, Geometry, Attribute and Set children. Topology types are Polyvertex, Polyline, Polygon, Triangle, Quadrilateral, Tetrahedron, Pyramid, Wedge, Hexahedron, the quadratic family (Edge_3, Tri_6, Quad_8, Tet_10, Pyramid_13, Wedge_15, Hex_20), Mixed, and structured types. In Mixed topology each cell is an integer type id plus its node list. Polyhedra (type 16) add a face count and then, per face, a node count and indices. Attribute Center is Node, Edge, Face, Cell, Grid or Other. There is also an ItemType FiniteElementFunction (ElementFamily CG/DG/Q/DQ/RT, ElementDegree, ElementCell) using DOF index plus value DataItems. Set has SetType Node, Edge, Face or Cell. For Face and Edge sets, the first DataItem gives cell indices and later ones give local face or edge indices. Source: https://xdmf.org/index.php/XDMF_Model_and_Format

Fides (ADIOS2): a JSON data model with data_sources, coordinate_system (array_type basic, uniform_point_coordinates, cartesian_product, composite), cell_set (structured, single_type, or explicit with connectivity, cell_types and number_of_vertices variables), fields (association points or cells) and step_information (time variable). Source: https://fides.readthedocs.io/en/latest/schema/schema.html. VTX is the ADIOS2 reader in VTK that interprets attributes in the VTK XML .vtu schema (class VTXvtkVTU). Sources: https://vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/VTXvtkVTU_8h_source.html and https://github.com/ornladios/ADIOS2/issues/3688 (older issue: only local-array variables supported for unstructured grids).
polyhedra: Yes, but as a bolt-on. VTK has an arbitrary-polyhedron cell type (VTK_POLYHEDRON, id 42, unverified against the type table). The legacy and XML form is a face stream appended in a separate faces/faceoffsets pair. The cell's own connectivity entry lists the unique points, and the stream gives each face as a count followed by point ids. VTK 9.4+ is reported (via PyVista docs) to hold faces in a shared face array, with per-cell face-location offsets and an empty slice for non-polyhedra. VTKHDF 2.5 makes this explicit with FaceConnectivity/FaceOffsets (a shared polygon table), PolyhedronToFaces, and PolyhedronOffsets. This is the closest of the VTK family to an actual face-cell adjacency table. Faces can be shared between cells, so interior faces can be stored once. There is no face-to-cell back-reference (no owner/neighbour), no orientation convention verified, and ordinary cells carry no explicit faces. XDMF encodes polyhedra only inside the Mixed topology (type 16 plus a face stream), not as a distinct TopologyType, and the page's capitalization is inconsistent. Fides lists no polyhedron cell type in its schema (single_type: vertex, line, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge, pyramid); explicit cell sets accept arbitrary type ids, so polyhedron support is unverified. Known pitfalls reported: writers dropping faces/faceoffsets when the input lacked face data, and readers failing on short faceoffsets arrays (https://discourse.vtk.org/t/vtk-polyhedron-difficulties/3545).
nonconformal: Nothing first-class. VTK/VTU/VTKHDF have no concept of an interface, mortar, or hanging-node relation. Non-conformal meshes are just cells whose coincident faces carry different point ids, so the information has to be inferred geometrically or carried in external arrays. The only structured exception is HyperTreeGrid (AMR via trees; Type HyperTreeGrid, Descriptors/Mask bitfields, BranchFactor), and OverlappingAMR (AMRBox per level, Spacing). Both are for Cartesian refinement, not general non-conformal unstructured meshes. XDMF offers Set (Face sets: cell index plus local face index), which could mark interface faces, and Collection grids for multi-domain pieces, but nothing says how two faces map to each other. Detection and projection would have to be user-defined metadata (e.g. FieldData or XDMF Information elements). I did not find any VTK-family mechanism for imprint records or face-pair maps (absence not exhaustively verified).
sets_and_partitions: Sets and labels are not first-class. Convention is a CellData integer array (e.g. material id or block id) and FieldData for names. Cell and Point arrays with Attribute tags exist. Composite types provide grouping: MultiBlockDataSet and PartitionedDataSetCollection with an Assembly group (hierarchy via nested groups or soft links to top-level blocks; PDC blocks need a globally unique Index attribute; creation-order tracking via H5P_CRT_ORDER_TRACKED and H5P_CRT_ORDER_INDEXED). So blocks per material or per partition are expressible as separate unstructured grids in an assembly tree, which is the nearest thing to a layer or partition concept. The format has no layer separation between geometry, partition and mesh: it only describes the mesh layer plus tags. XDMF has Set (Node/Edge/Face/Cell) as named entity subsets and Grid SubSet. Partitioning for parallel is by pieces: .pvtu lists pieces, VTKHDF concatenates partitions in each dataset with per-partition NumberOf* size arrays (n usually equals MPI ranks), and the reader computes its offset as the prefix sum. Ghost cells use the vtkGhostType array convention (this convention is from memory, unverified in the fetched pages). Source for the partition layout: https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/vtkhdf_specifications.html
high_order: Cell types exist for Lagrange and Bezier families (type ids in the 60s-70s in VTK, unverified from the fetched pages; the type table at docs.vtk.org returned 404), plus the old quadratic and biquadratic types. In VTKHDF the spec page mentions only the HigherOrderDegrees attribute value on arrays and a RationalWeights attribute name, with no dedicated high-order section found. Conventions for node ordering are defined in code, not in the spec (unverified). XDMF lists quadratic cells only (Edge_3, Tri_6, Quad_8, Tet_10, Pyramid_13, Wedge_15, Hex_20) but has a FiniteElementFunction attribute with family and degree, which is a field-level high-order mechanism. Fides: no high-order cell sets found in its schema.
geometry_association: None. No B-rep entity links, no classification of mesh entities against geometric model entities. Only convention: store a "GeometryId" or similar as a cell/point integer array, with names in FieldData. XDMF Information elements are free-form key/value metadata that the schema ignores, so they could carry such links, but nothing standardizes it.
parallel: VTKHDF: partitioned layout described above (concatenated arrays with per-partition counts, designed for parallel HDF5 I/O, with the stated aim of I/O performance and parallel I/O at https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/index.html). PVTU: master XML plus per-piece files. XDMF: Grid Collection (Spatial) of per-rank grids with HDF5 heavy data; Fides/ADIOS2: variables written per rank as local arrays or global arrays, with streaming (SST) engines for in-situ. Partition numbering is purely by piece; no shared-entity maps (no global ids shared across ranks except via GlobalIds attribute), no explicit halo/ghost layers in the spec text I read (ghost array convention unverified).
database_like_aspects: Weakly database-like. The model is flat columnar arrays with a few offset arrays (CSR-like: Connectivity plus Offsets, and for polyhedra a two-level CSR via PolyhedronOffsets -> PolyhedronToFaces -> FaceOffsets -> FaceConnectivity). VTKHDF's per-step offsets in Steps (PointOffsets, CellOffsets, ...) are effectively an index/pointer table that lets readers slice a time-versioned store without rewriting static parts. XDMF is explicitly a light/heavy split: an XML catalog (rank, dimensions, number type stored redundantly so tools can plan access) over bulk data in HDF5 or binary, with HyperSlab, Function and Coordinates DataItems that act as lightweight views or derived arrays. XDMF Set records are the closest thing to query results. There is no schema enforcement beyond conventions, no queries, no on-demand adjacency, and no entity tables for edges or faces (except polyhedra faces).
ecosystem: ParaView, VisIt, VTK (C++/Python/Java), PyVista, meshio (reads/writes VTU/VTK/XDMF), Gmsh and many solvers export VTU. XDMF is read by ParaView, VisIt and used by FEniCS/dolfinx and others. VTKHDF is natively read/written by VTK and ParaView (ParaView support for the newer subtype versions e.g. polyhedra in 2.5 and Table in 2.8 depends on version; unverified), with a Python examples repo (vtkhdf-scripts, h5py based). Fides and VTX are readers in ParaView and VTK for ADIOS2 BP output (Fides built on the Viskores toolkit, formerly VTK-m). Spec governance: VTKHDF specification is community-led through VTK Discourse proposals and GitLab issue #19243, maintained by Kitware people. VTKHDF version history: 1.0 UnstructuredGrid, ImageData, OverlappingAMR; 2.0 PolyData and temporal; 2.1 PDC and MultiBlock; 2.2 temporal AMR; 2.3 renames; 2.4 HyperTreeGrid; 2.5 polyhedra; 2.6 dataset attributes; 2.7 Rectilinear and Structured; 2.8 Table (https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/vtkhdf_changelog.html).
spec_quality: Mixed. VTKHDF has a versioned, public, changelogged spec (major bump for API breaks, minor for additions) and is the best specified of the VTK family, but the page is prose-and-table: dtypes are not tabulated, high-order is barely covered, and internal naming is inconsistent (NumberOfFaces vs NumberOfPolygonalFaces). The XML VTK format is documented but long-lived and quirky (the face stream; the docs URL I tried returned 404, so I could not read the primary XML spec page and relied on forum posts for the faces layout). XDMF's page is informal, with capitalization inconsistencies, and the XDMF3 development has been slow (unverified). Fides has readthedocs documentation with a JSON schema description but versions differ (stable 1.3.0 vs latest). The family is a visualization format spec, not a mesh semantic spec: no validity rules (orientation, conformity, manifoldness) are defined.
strengths: Near-universal read support in ParaView/VisIt/PyVista/meshio, so exporting to it gives instant visualization and debugging
VTKHDF is a modern, versioned, parallel-friendly HDF5 layout with partitions concatenated and per-partition counts, plus temporal slicing via Steps offsets
VTKHDF 2.5 gives a CSR-style shared-face table for polyhedra (faces can be shared between cells)
Composite assemblies (MultiBlock/PDC with Assembly tree) allow per-material or per-region grouping
XDMF's light/heavy split with redundant metadata in XML is a clean pattern: a small catalog describes large binary arrays so tools can plan access without reading them
Mixed cell types and a large catalog of cell types incl. high-order Lagrange/Bezier in VTK
Fides/ADIOS2 adds streaming and in-situ coupling for HPC workflows
weaknesses: Visualization model, not a simulation mesh: no explicit edge/face entities except polyhedron faces, no face-to-cell adjacency (owner/neighbour), no orientation or validity rules
Polyhedra are an add-on to a per-cell-type design (late addition: VTKHDF 2.5; legacy face stream is awkward and error-prone, with reported writer/reader bugs)
No non-conformal interface, hanging-node or mortar representation
No geometry (CAD/B-rep) association and no classification of entities
Sets/materials are only conventional integer arrays or separate blocks; no named entity sets with typed semantics (XDMF Set is partial)
High-order and ordering conventions live in code, not spec; VTKHDF high-order docs are thin
Fides schema lacks polyhedra (as far as the schema page shows) and the VTX path was reported as local-arrays-only
Spec text has internal naming inconsistencies; dtypes not tabulated
Three or four overlapping serializations (VTU, VTKHDF, XDMF, ADIOS2) with uneven feature parity, and ParaView version-dependent support
lessons_for_us: Adopt the CSR pattern everywhere (offsets with N+1 entries, concatenated partitions with per-partition count arrays); VTKHDF's two-level polyhedron chain (cell -> face ids -> face nodes) is the right shape, but make faces first-class tables for ALL cells, not just polyhedra, with face->(left,right) cell refs and orientation sign so adjacency is stored rather than rederived

Adopt VTKHDF as an export target (and XDMF+HDF5 as a secondary one) rather than as the IR: it gives free ParaView visualization, but our IR needs entity tables and relations it cannot express; define a lossy projection with documented drops (sets become CellData arrays or blocks, interfaces dropped or emitted as Sets)

Adopt XDMF's light/heavy idea: a small self-describing manifest (entities, dtypes, shapes, relation names, layer links) over bulk HDF5 or Zarr/Arrow-like arrays, with redundant shape/dtype in the manifest so readers can plan I/O without touching bulk data

Adopt VTKHDF's temporal trick (Steps offsets into shared arrays) for versioning: layers (geometry, partition, mesh) and mesh refinement states can reuse unchanged arrays by offset instead of copying; this is also an immutable, append-only-snapshot design akin to a database

Deliberately differ: treat the mesh as a set of typed entity tables (vertex, edge, face, cell) with explicit relation tables and tag columns, so adjacency is a join, not a cell-type special case; polyhedra become the general case and standard cells are just a 'type' column with a lookup

Deliberately differ: make non-conformal interfaces a first-class relation (face_pair or mortar table with imprint records: which sub-faces of A overlap which of B, area weights, projection frame), because no VTK-family format has it and the neutron transport use case needs it

Deliberately differ: store the three layers (geometry B-rep entities, partitions/materials, mesh) as separate tables connected by classification columns (mesh entity -> geometric entity id; geometric entity -> partition/material id) rather than overloading CellData integer arrays

Adopt VTKHDF's Assembly idea (hierarchical groupings with soft links) but for named entity sets (boundary sets, material regions) that reference entity ids in any tier (node/edge/face/cell) with typed semantics, as XDMF Set partially does

Fix the spec-quality gap: ship a machine-readable versioned schema (JSON Schema or similar) with dtypes, invariants (orientation, closedness, conformity flags) and a validator, versioned with major/minor bump rules like VTKHDF
Treat partition/ghost info as first-class (shared-entity maps with global ids and owner rank), which VTKHDF does not specify

corrections.claim: XML VTU polyhedra: Cells carries DataArrays 'faces' and 'faceoffsets' holding a per-polyhedron face stream [nfaces, npts, ids...] (the only XML layout described).
corrections.correction: That is the legacy layout, read only for XML file version < 2.3. Current VTK (vtkXMLUnstructuredDataWriter.cxx, master) writes four CSR arrays when any VTK_POLYHEDRON is present: 'face_connectivity', 'face_offsets', 'polyhedron_to_faces', 'polyhedron_offsets' (vtkNeedsNewFileVersionPolyhedronV2 forces the newer file version; the reader branches on major.minor < 2.3 to choose faces/faceoffsets vs the four new arrays). The docs page still documents only the legacy form. Consequence: the report's 'VTKHDF 2.5 is the closest of the family to a face table' is no longer a VTKHDF distinction; .vtu and VTKHDF now carry the same four-array structure. Exact version number emitted by the writer and the release that introduced the 2.3 bump were not read (storage change itself is 9.4).

corrections.claim: The legacy and XML form is a face stream appended in a separate faces/faceoffsets pair.
corrections.correction: Wrong for the legacy .vtk format: vtkUnstructuredGridWriter emits only CELLS and CELL_TYPES and serializes each polyhedron's face stream inline into the CELLS connectivity (expandedCells->InsertNextCell(it->GetSerializedCellFaces())). There is no separate FACES section. The legacy docs page is stale (says current version 3.0; writers emit 5.x with OFFSETS/CONNECTIVITY blocks).

corrections.claim: VTKHDF 2.5: faces as polygons, which may be shared between polyhedra; interior faces can be stored once.
corrections.correction: The spec only says faces are 'defined using a separate array of surfacic (2D) cells' and that PolyhedronOffsets repeats for non-polyhedral cells; it says nothing about sharing, orientation, or a sign/flip mechanism. Sharing by index is structurally possible but unspecified. The Jan-Mar 2024 Discourse design thread explicitly proposed signed face indices for orientation, an OpenFOAM-style owner/neighbour array and a boundary-first COMPACT layout; none of these appear in the spec. Inference (verify): since vtkPolyhedron requires every face CCW-from-outside with outward normal, a face shared by index between two cells cannot satisfy both unless the reader re-orients.

corrections.claim: No orientation or validity rules are defined; no orientation convention verified.
corrections.correction: VTK defines cell-level validity for polyhedra in vtkPolyhedron: faces must be consistently wound with outward normals ('vertices of each face must be ordered counter-clockwise when viewed from outside'), watertight, manifold (each edge adjacent to exactly two faces), planar; convexity not required but concave support 'currently limited'. vtkCellValidator exists (9.6 adds automatic per-polyhedron tolerance; vtkPolygon/vtkPolyhedron report more defects). What is absent is mesh-level conformity/manifoldness rules, not cell validity.

corrections.claim: Lagrange and Bezier type ids in the 60s-70s (unverified); VTK_POLYHEDRON = 42 unverified.
corrections.correction: Verified from vtkCellType.h: VTK_POLYHEDRON = 42. Lagrange = 68-74 (curve, triangle, quadrilateral, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge, pyramid), Bezier = 75-81, VTK_NUMBER_OF_CELL_TYPES = 82. 60-67 are the older VTK_HIGHER_ORDER_* family (several deprecated in 9.7). Design-relevant: VTK_HIGHER_ORDER_PYRAMID (66), VTK_LAGRANGE_PYRAMID (74) and VTK_BEZIER_PYRAMID (81) are 'Not Implemented yet, kept as placeholder' - VTK has no arbitrary-order pyramid; pyramids cap at VTK_QUADRATIC_PYRAMID (27, 13-node) and VTK_TRIQUADRATIC_PYRAMID (37, 19-node). Mixed hex/tet high-order meshes with pyramid transitions cannot be expressed above that.

corrections.claim: XDMF lists quadratic cells only (Edge_3, Tri_6, Quad_8, Tet_10, Pyramid_13, Wedge_15, Hex_20).
corrections.correction: The wiki TopologyType table lists only those, but the wiki Mixed table and the Xdmf3 library also define Quadrilateral_9 (35), Wedge_18 (41), Hexahedron_24 (49), Hexahedron_27 (50), and Lagrange-style Hexahedron_64 ... Hexahedron_1331 (0x33-0x40) plus Hexahedron_Spectral_64 ... _1331 (0x41-0x48), i.e. hex orders 3-10. However VTK's xdmf3 reader (vtkXdmf3DataSet.cxx) maps only up to 27-node cells; Hexahedron_64+ and Spectral types sit in a commented-out TODO and fall through to VTK_EMPTY_CELL, and the VTK->XDMF direction refuses biquadratic/triquadratic cells ('I do not know how to make that xdmf cell type'). Effective high-order XDMF via VTK/ParaView caps at 27 nodes and does not round-trip. A 2024 VTK issue (19088) also reports Hexahedron_27 read with a wrong node count.

corrections.claim: XDMF encodes polyhedra only inside the Mixed topology (type 16), not as a distinct TopologyType.
corrections.correction: Xdmf3 defines Polyhedron = 0x10 (16) as a TopologyType in the library (XdmfTopologyType.cpp), and VTK maps XdmfTopologyType::Polyhedron() <-> VTK_POLYHEDRON in both directions; only the wiki's TopologyType attribute table omits it. The per-cell encoding (nfaces, then per face npts + ids) is as the report states. VTK 9.4 also added arbitrary polyhedra to the older Xdmf2 reader.

corrections.claim: Fides appears not to support polyhedra; explicit cell sets accept arbitrary type ids so polyhedron support is unverified.
corrections.correction: Now firm: Fides maps to Viskores datasets, and Viskores' CellShape enum has only EMPTY, VERTEX, LINE, POLY_LINE, TRIANGLE, POLYGON, QUAD, TETRA, HEXAHEDRON, WEDGE, PYRAMID - no polyhedron shape. So an 'explicit' cell set cannot carry polyhedra regardless of type id. Fides single_type list (vertex, line, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge, pyramid) and the three cell_set_type values are confirmed. Fides also has an XGC data model; vtkFidesWriter (ADIOS2 BP output) was added in VTK 9.5.

corrections.claim: ADIOS2 with Fides and VTX is a streaming and HPC-IO route; VTX interprets the VTK XML .vtu schema (older issue: local arrays only).
corrections.correction: VTX is not a streaming route. ADIOS2 docs: vtk.xml support 'Only supports BP Files, streams are not supported', 'only works with MPI builds of VTK and Paraview', ImageData with Global Arrays only, UnstructuredGrid 'with ADIOS2 Local Arrays Variables only' (so a mesh written on N ranks is awkward to read on M). Issue 3688 asking for global arrays was auto-closed 'not planned' in May 2025 with no code change. Streaming/in-situ is Fides' role, not VTX's.

corrections.claim: VTKHDF spec version 2.8; ParaView support for newer subtype versions (polyhedra in 2.5, Table in 2.8) is version dependent, unverified.
corrections.correction: Spec 2.8 is the docs' latest (changelog confirmed: 2.4 HTG, 2.5 polyhedra, 2.6 dataset attributes, 2.7 Rectilinear/Structured, 2.8 Table). But implementation lags: VTK 9.4 (2024-11-22) introduced vtkHDFWriter; VTK 9.5 (2025-06-20) states 'VTKHDF Specification is now version 2.4'; VTK 9.6 (2026-02-09) is the first release whose vtkHDFReader reads polyhedra - writer polyhedron support is not stated anywhere (release notes, status page). Rectilinear/Structured/Table, HTG writer and 'proper distributed support in vtkHDFReader' are 9.7 (unreleased/nightly) items. Which ParaView ships the 9.6 reader is unverified (ParaView 6.1.0, 2026-03-31, is the first plausible one; its kitware.com notes do not mention VTKHDF).

corrections.claim: VTK 9.4+ in-memory polyhedra moved to separate face-location/face-connectivity arrays (per PyVista docs); reader and writer in 9.4+ unverified.
corrections.correction: Verified from VTK 9.4 release notes: Faces and FaceLocations became vtkCellArray objects ('non-interleaved storage'), Connectivity unchanged, layout 'much closer to how Conduit store its polyhedral cell information'; SetCells(types, cells, faceLocations, faces) deprecated for SetPolyhedralCells; GetFaces/GetFaceLocations now serve a cached legacy-layout copy and should be treated read-only. Non-polyhedral cells get an empty FaceLocations entry. VTK 9.7 fixes SetCells(types, cells) misreading point lists as a legacy face stream and dropping faces. The XML writer uses GetPolyhedronFaces/GetPolyhedronFaceLocations (new layout) - see the .vtu correction above.

corrections.claim: The XML VTK format docs URL returned 404; relied on forum posts for the faces layout.
corrections.correction: Primary pages exist: https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkxml_file_format.html (documents connectivity/offsets/types plus legacy faces/faceoffsets with a type-42 example; does not document the 2.3 four-array layout, HigherOrderDegrees, RationalWeights or vtkGhostType) and https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtk_legacy_file_format.html. The spec-quality weakness should therefore read: the XML page is behind the writer.

corrections.claim: Ghost cells use the vtkGhostType array convention (from memory, unverified).
corrections.correction: Convention confirmed at the API level: vtkDataSetAttributes defines cell ghost bits DUPLICATECELL=1, HIGHCONNECTIVITYCELL=2, LOWCONNECTIVITYCELL=4, REFINEDCELL=8, EXTERIORCELL=16, HIDDENCELL=32 and point bits DUPLICATEPOINT=1, HIDDENPOINT=2, stored in the array named by GhostArrayName() (conventionally 'vtkGhostType'; the literal string was not read on the page). The XML writer bumps the file version when both point and cell ghost arrays are present. VTKHDF spec does not mention ghosts; they travel as ordinary CellData/PointData.

missing_important: vtkCellGrid (VTK 9.4, 2024-11-22) is the one VTK-family data model built for the first consumer's likely discretization and is absent from the report: a vtkDataObject subclass for 'higher order Galerkin cells' where vtkCellAttribute objects map 1:1 to mathematical fields, reference arbitrary arrays, and carry their own function space (H(Grad), H(Curl), H(Div)) and CG or DG formulation, decoupled from the shape attribute (non-isoparametric allowed). I/O: vtkCellGridReader/Writer in JSON or binary MessagePack (.dg; three sections arrays / attributes / cell-types), vtkLegacyCellGridReader/Writer embedding MessagePack in legacy .vtk, vtkIOSSCellGridReader reading Exodus (.exdg) as cell grids; ParaView 5.13.1+ CompositeCellGridReader. Motivated by Sandia's EMPIRE DG solver (Nedelec/Raviart-Thomas DOFs on edges/faces). Limits: shape attribute H(Grad) only; JSON format described as 'for debugging purposes'; vtkCellGridToUnstructuredGrid is lossy (all attributes to point data, linear geometry); no polyhedra; per the Feb-Sep 2025 ParaView thread the Exodus info_records mechanism is being phased out and the newer IOSS spec for Lagrange coefficients/shared DOFs is unfunded. Sources: https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/release_details/9.4/cell-grid-changes.html , https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/modules/vtk-modules/IO/CellGrid/README.html , https://discourse.paraview.org/t/discontinuous-galerkin-support-in-paraview/16132 , https://www.paraview.org/paraview-docs/v5.13.0/python/paraview.simple.CompositeCellGridReader.html

The VTKHDF polyhedron design thread (Jan 2024 - Mar 2025) shows face->(owner, neighbour) arrays with -1 for boundary, signed face indices for orientation (with the index-0 sign problem), 1-based vs 0-based indexing, and a boundary-first COMPACT layout were proposed and NOT adopted into spec 2.5; Kitware noted 'VTK does not store face-sharing information' and that it can be recomputed with GetCellNeighbors. This is direct evidence that owner/neighbour adjacency is a real gap the VTK community considered and shelved - useful as the baseline for the 'deliberately differ' lesson. https://discourse.vtk.org/t/vtkhdf-add-support-for-polyhedron-cells/13089

High-order conventions in the XML format: mixed-degree Lagrange/Bezier cells use a 3-component CellData array with Attribute HigherOrderDegrees; rational Bezier weights use a PointData array with Attribute RationalWeights, and ParaView only honours it when the Attribute is on the <PointData> element (VTK issue 18723). Lagrange cells date from VTK 8.1 (orders up to 10 by default, Kitware blog 2018); Bezier cells were contributed by Coreform with Kitware (~2020). Node ordering for these cells is documented only in the Kitware blog and source, not in any file-format page. Sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/issues/18723 , https://www.kitware.com/modeling-arbitrary-order-lagrange-finite-elements- , https://www.kitware.com/implementation-of-rational-bezier-cells-into-vtk/

VTK 9.5 removed vtkHDFReader's MergeParts option (now a no-op): the reader no longer merges file partitions into one UnstructuredGrid; consumers get partitioned output and must merge (vtkMergeBlocks) themselves. 9.5 also added parallel MPI read/write of composite temporal VTKHDF. 9.7 (nightly) adds 'Proper distributed support in vtkHDFReader' and 'Better support for partitioned data writing in vtkHDFWriter'; extent-based parallel writing is not supported for ImageData/Rectilinear/Structured per the status page. https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/release_details/9.5.html , https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/vtkhdf_status.html

VTKHDF spec/implementation gap to state explicitly: the status page tracks reader/writer support per dataset type but has no polyhedron row and gives no VTK versions; the Type attribute list in the spec omits RectilinearGrid, StructuredGrid and Table even though their sections define them; 'Static' temporal mode is only partially supported by the reader and unsupported by the writer. https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/vtkhdf_status.html

Conduit Mesh Blueprint is a lead the report should check as an alternative baseline: VTK's 9.4 polyhedral layout was explicitly modelled on 'how Conduit store its polyhedral cell information', and VTK 9.7 adds vtkFidesReader support for reading Conduit nodes. Not verified here beyond those two release-note sentences. https://docs.vtk.org/en/v9.4.1/release_details/9.4/vtk-polyhedral-cells-storage.html , https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/release_details/9.6.html (sidebar 9.7 entries)

Confirmed as stated (no change needed): VTKHDF Offsets has NumberOfCells[i]+1 entries per partition; PolyhedronOffsets repeats the previous value for non-polyhedral cells; NumberOfFaces vs NumberOfPolygonalFaces naming inconsistency is real; Steps group dataset names incl. FaceConnectivityOffsets/FaceOffsetsOffsets/PolyhedronToFaceIdOffsets; Attribute values (Scalars, Vectors, Normals, TCoords, Tensors, GlobalIds, PedigreeIds, EdgeFlag, Tangents, RationalWeights, HigherOrderDegrees, ProcessIds); governance via Discourse then GitLab issue #19243, maintainers Gombert/Givord/Westphal; XDMF Set encoding (Face/Edge sets: cell ids then local face/edge ids), FiniteElementFunction families CG/DG/Q/DQ/RT, Information element, XDMF3 'current version 3.0' with examples still tagged 2.0.

summary: Two mature, widely used mesh containers with opposite philosophies. MED (EDF/CEA, HDF5-based, C library MEDfile 4.x; docs seen at 4.2.0; MEDCoupling 9.14-9.16 in SALOME) stores meshes per entity-type with a per-entity "family" integer; groups are named sets of families. It supports polygons and polyhedra, multiple computing steps, and subdomain joints. MEDCoupling is the in-memory companion: UMesh with nodal connectivity plus index arrays, and a remapper/intersection kernel (INTERP_KERNEL) that computes sparse weight matrices between independent, possibly non-conformal meshes. Gmsh MSH 4.1 is a flat, block-structured ASCII/binary file serialising Gmsh's model: an optional $Entities B-rep with signed boundary lists, nodes/elements classified on those entities, physical groups as a separate tag overlay, partitioned entities, periodic links, ghost elements and post-processing data. MSH 4.1 has a formal versioned spec but no polyhedral element types (polygon/polyhedron ids 9/10 appear only in $InterpolationScheme). Neither format has a first-class non-conformal interface object, and neither stores face/edge adjacency. Nothing was run locally; claims come from the cited pages and gaps are marked unverified.
data_model: MED file (HDF5): per a forum HDF5 dump (https://discourse.salome-platform.org/t/med-file-format-specification-and-group-tree-definitions/1340), ENS_MAA/<mesh>/ holds MAI (cells) with one subgroup per geometry type (HE8, QU4, SE2...) each with datasets FAM, NOD, NUM; NOE (nodes) with COO, FAM, NUM; FAS/<mesh>/FAMILLE_ZERO for families. Full tree beyond that is unverified. C API: MEDmeshNodeCoordinateRd/Wr, MEDmeshEntityFamilyNumberWr(fid, mesh, numdt, numit, entitype, geotype, nentity, number), MEDfamilyCr(fid, mesh, famname, famnumber, ngroup, groupnames) (https://docs.salome-platform.org/med-4.2.0-documentation/a03168.html). Entities are addressed by (entity type, geometry type) and time step (numdt, numit). Family 0 is the default (no groups); by convention node families are >0 and element families <0. Each entity carries one family id; a group is the union of families listing that group name. MEDCoupling in memory: MEDCouplingUMesh has a coordinates array, _nodal_connectivity and _nodal_connectivity_index (CSR-like, half-open ranges), MED node ordering but 0-based C indexing; all cells must have dimension == meshDim, space dim separate (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/developer/MEDCouplingUMeshPage.html). MEDFileUMesh adds relative mesh levels (0 cells, negative for faces/edges via meshDimRelToMaxExt), a family-id array per level, and group<->family maps. MEDCoupling1SGTUMesh (single geometry type) and MEDCoupling1DGTUMesh (dynamic type, connectivity+index) exist. Gmsh MSH 4.1 (https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html section 10.1): $MeshFormat (4.1, file-type 0/1, data-size=sizeof(size_t), endianness int in binary); $PhysicalNames (dim, tag, name<=127 chars); $Entities: counts of points/curves/surfaces/volumes then per entity tag(int), bbox (points: X Y Z only), numPhysicalTags+tags, and for curves/surfaces/volumes numBounding+bounding tags whose sign encodes orientation; $Nodes: numEntityBlocks, numNodes, minNodeTag, maxNodeTag, then per block (entityDim, entityTag, parametric, numNodesInBlock, all node tags as size_t, then all x y z [u v w]); $Elements: same block layout (entityDim, entityTag, elementType, numElementsInBlock, then elementTag + node tags per element). Every node and element is classified on exactly one model entity block. Tags must be >0, may be sparse/unordered but sparse tags degrade performance (map instead of vector). Other sections: $Periodic, $GhostElements, $PartitionedEntities, $Parametrizations, $NodeData/$ElementData/$ElementNodeData, $InterpolationScheme; unknown sections are kept as model attributes.
polyhedra: MED: first-class. MED_POLYHEDRON is read via MEDmeshPolyhedronRd(fid, mesh, numdt, numit, entitype, cmode, faceindex, nodeindex, connectivity): faceindex (npoly+1 entries) points into nodeindex (one entry per face, +1), which points into connectivity (node numbers per face); 1-based. Sizes come from MEDmeshnEntity with MED_INDEX_FACE / MED_INDEX_NODE / MED_CONNECTIVITY (https://docs.salome-platform.org/med-4.2.0-documentation/a03170.html). This is a two-level CSR (cell->faces->nodes) with faces not deduplicated across cells, so face adjacency must be recomputed. Polygons use a single index+connectivity (MEDmeshPolygonWr, seen via search result of https://docs.salome-platform.org/med-4.2.0-documentation/a03124.html). MEDCoupling: NORM_POLYHED in one connectivity array; the tutorial example shows faces separated by -1 (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/tutorial/medcoupling_umesh1_en.html); the formal rule page was not found, so the separator semantics are verified only via the example. Volume intersection splits target polyhedra into sub-tetrahedra upstream; hex SplittingPolicy PLANAR_FACE_5 (default), PLANAR_FACE_6, GENERAL_24, GENERAL_48 (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/developer/intersec-specifics.html). Gmsh MSH 4.1: no polygon or polyhedron element type in the listed element types (verified: list runs from 1-node/2-node lines up to 64/125-node hexes; topology ids 9 polygons and 10 polyhedra appear only for $InterpolationScheme). The list ends with '...' and defers to GmshDefines.h, so hidden types are unverified.
nonconformal: Neither format has a first-class non-conformal interface object (verified by absence in the specs read). MED: a non-conformal interface is just two face/cell sets (families/groups) that do not share nodes; the consuming code (e.g. code_aster mortar contact, validation case PERF018 with incompatible meshes, https://ericca.uqtr.ca/fr14.4/man_v/v1/v1.01.397.pdf) pairs them using group names plus geometry; nothing flags them as non-conformal. MEDCoupling holds the machinery: MEDCouplingRemapper.prepare(src, target, method) builds a sparse matrix (getCrudeMatrix = vector of map<id,double>, one row per target entity) for P0P0, P0P1, P1P0, P1P1; transfer/partialTransfer/reverseTransfer apply it (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/developer/classMEDCoupling_1_1MEDCouplingRemapper.html). 2D P0->P0 IntersectionType: Triangulation (default), Convex, Geometric2D (any 2D cell, incl. non-convex), PointLocator (non-conservative); precision default 1e-12 scaled by mesh size. 3D surface intersection projects both polygons on a common plane (MedianPlane, Orientation, DoRotate, BoundingBoxAdjustment, MaxDistance3DSurfIntersect). 3D volume uses Grandy 1999 tetra/polyhedron clipping. Code_Saturne wrapper also lists Barycentric, BarycentricGeo2D, MappedBarycentric (https://www.code-saturne.org/documentation/9.0/doxygen/src/cs__medcoupling__remapper_8h.html). UMesh also has static Intersect2DMeshes(m1,m2,eps,cellNb1,cellNb2), conformize2D/3D(eps), mergeNodes(precision); only signatures were seen, behaviour is unverified. The intersection doc page does not discuss how non-conformity is detected. Gmsh MSH 4.1: conformity across entities is by shared node tags; a non-conformal mesh could be written as separate nodes at equal positions, but nothing flags it (inference, unverified). $Periodic is the only explicit relation between two distinct entities: entityDim, entityTag, entityTagMaster, numAffine+values (affine transform may be empty), numCorrespondingNodes with nodeTag/nodeTagMaster pairs. It is a node-level correspondence for conformal periodic pairs, not general mortar-style imprinting. In the user's terms, imprinting is an upstream step in both ecosystems and the formats can only store its result as shared nodes.
sets_and_partitions: MED: the single mechanism is family (one int per entity per type) -> group names on the family. It is compact and O(1) per entity, natural for disjoint partitions such as materials, awkward for overlapping sets (needs combinatorial families). Legacy MED 2.3 family 'attributes' exist; a 2009 Gmsh list post said they should be deprecated, current status unverified. Parallel: joint API MEDsubdomainJointCr, MEDsubdomainCorrespondenceWr (per local/remote entity-type pair and computing step), MEDnSubdomainJoint, MEDsubdomainJointInfo (https://docs.salome-platform.org/med-4.2.0-documentation/a00698_source.html); MEDCoupling tools split a MED file into subdomains (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/developer/tools.html). Mesh name is the unique key linking fields to meshes (https://docs.salome-platform.org/latest/dev/MEDCoupling/developer/med-file.html). Gmsh MSH 4.1 makes two layers explicit: (a) elementary model entities (dim, tag) form the geometric B-rep in $Entities; mesh entities are classified on them; (b) physical groups are a separate overlay, a (dim, physicalTag) with optional name, attached as lists to entities, many-to-many. This is the closest existing baseline to the user's geometry / partition / mesh layers, although the partition layer is only a tag list, not a first-class object. By default only elements in physical groups are saved unless Mesh.SaveAll=1. Mesh.SaveTopology and Mesh.SaveParametric control writing B-rep and parametric coordinates. $PartitionedEntities stores per partition entity parentDim/parentTag, partition tag list, bbox, physical tags, boundary, plus numGhostEntities with ghostEntityTag/partition. $GhostElements: elementTag, partitionTag, ghostPartitionTags (the authors say it will be reworked for IO efficiency). Mesh.PartitionCreateGhostCells creates per-partition ghost entities with elements connected to neighbouring partitions by at least one node.
strengths: MED families give compact O(1) membership, long industrial track record (code_aster, Code_Saturne, TrioCFD, SALOME), HDF5 features (chunking, compression, parallel I/O), multi-timestep meshes, native polygons/polyhedra and joints for distributed meshes
MEDCoupling remapper is the only widely available open mesh-on-mesh kernel returning an explicit sparse matrix, decoupling discretisation transfer from file format
Gmsh MSH 4.1 is formally documented with change log, block-structured so a block reads with one fread, and keeps mesh-to-geometry classification explicit
$Entities carries a real B-rep with signed boundary tags and bounding boxes so the mesh can be re-linked to CAD
Physical groups cleanly separate geometry from application-level partitions, with overlap allowed
Partitioned entities, ghost entities, periodic links are in the spec; unknown sections are preserved
Many readers/writers exist for both (ParaView, meshio, SALOME, code_aster, Gmsh)
weaknesses: MED: documentation is French-first and tied to a C library and HDF5 tree; a standalone on-disk spec was not located (unverified); overlapping groups are awkward; no B-rep in the file; polyhedra faces duplicated per cell so no adjacency; non-conformal interfaces are an implicit convention; mesh-on-mesh lives only in MEDCoupling, not in the file

MEDCoupling: cells must all have dim == meshDim; geotype-prefixed CSR connectivity is not SoA-friendly; many intersection options with robustness tied to a global tolerance (1e-12 scaled); 3D surface intersection needs projection heuristics; no non-conformal detection described

Gmsh MSH 4.1: no polyhedra or polygons; no face/edge entities or adjacency; each node belongs to one entity; sparse tags force maps; ghost and data sections flagged by the authors for rework; high-order only through enumerated element-type ids; no non-conformal object; physical groups are only tag lists; the format mirrors one program's data model
lessons_for_us: Adopt: classify every mesh entity onto a geometric-model entity (Gmsh $Entities + block-per-entity), keeping B-rep boundary lists with signed orientation; this gives layer (1) -> layer (3) directly

Adopt: partition layer as an overlay of named groups independent of geometry (Gmsh physical groups, many-to-many), optionally with a MED-style dense family id per entity plus family->groups table for the common disjoint-material case

Adopt: struct-of-arrays blocks so a Rust core can mmap columns; use two-level CSR (cell->face, face->node) like MED polyhedra but with SHARED deduplicated faces and signed face refs, so polyhedra, interfaces and boundary sets are all face sets with adjacency
Adopt: version and size_t width in header, min/max/count density hints for ids (Gmsh), and opaque preservation of unknown sections

Adopt: MEDCoupling's idea that non-conformal coupling is a sparse matrix between two entity sets; our IR should have an 'interface' object = pair of face sets + relation kind {conformal, imprinted (shared nodes), non-conformal with cached overlap/weights, periodic + affine}; no format has this and a transport code needs it

Deliberately differ: do not make the file the data model; use an in-memory typed relation store (entities with stable ids, CSR relations, attribute columns, sets/partitions as tables) and treat MED, MSH, VTK, Exodus as backends, matching the user's LLVM-IR framing

Deliberately differ: record periodic/non-conformal/hanging relations as declared relations with tolerance and detection provenance, rather than implicit convention (MED) or node-pair list only (Gmsh $Periodic)
Deliberately differ: represent high-order as (reference element, polynomial order, node layout) instead of enumerated type ids, with a lookup table to MED/Gmsh ids at export
Model 'imprint' (information-level link, no node change) separately from 'conformize' (physical modification, cf. MEDCoupling conformize2D/3D) as distinct DAG nodes
Parallel: combine Gmsh partitioned entities (parent links, ghost entities) with MED joints (explicit local/remote correspondence arrays); make owner rank and ghost layer columns
Verify before committing: exact MED HDF5 layout, status of MED attributes, hidden Gmsh polyhedron ids in GmshDefines.h, robustness of MEDCoupling 3D polyhedron intersection with non-planar faces
sources: https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html (section 10.1 MSH file format; Mesh options)
storage: MED: HDF5 container (a specialisation of HDF5 per the docs) with hierarchical groups per mesh / entity type / geometry type and datasets (FAM, NOD, NUM, COO); multiple time steps; parallel via joints. Performance is that of HDF5 (chunking, compression, parallel I/O); exact chunking choices unverified. Gmsh MSH 4.1: single text or binary file with $Name/$EndName sections; binary writes raw ints/size_t/doubles with an endianness check; block structure allows one read per block for tags and coordinates (4.1 un-mixed int and float data); no built-in compression or parallel I/O; sparse tags force map-based access.
geometry_association: Gmsh MSH 4.1 is the stronger example: $Entities holds a B-rep (points XYZ; curves/surfaces/volumes with bbox and signed bounding-entity tags), every node and element block is tagged (entityDim, entityTag), $Nodes can store parametric u,v,w on the entity, and $Parametrizations stores a discrete parametrisation of curves/surfaces. The link to CAD is integer tags only; the geometry itself is not stored. MED has no B-rep in the file; association is by family/group names and optional numbering (verified only by absence in what was read, so treat as unverified for MED 4.x extensions). MEDCoupling has no geometric-entity association.
high_order: Gmsh MSH 4.1 encodes order in element-type ids: line3 (8), tri6 (9), quad9 (10), tet10 (11), hex27 (12), prism18 (13), pyramid14 (14), quad8 (16), hex20 (17), prism15 (18), pyramid13 (19), triangles to order 5 (20-25), edges to order 5 (26-28), tets order 3-5 (29-31), hexes order 3 and 4 (92, 93); node ordering in section 10.2 of the manual. Not parametric in (family, order). MED/MEDCoupling have quadratic types (NORM_TRI6, NORM_QUAD8, etc., and convertQuadraticCellsToLinear(); signature seen); anything above quadratic in MED 4.x is unverified. Both treat high-order as extra nodes in connectivity, not as curved geometry tied to the B-rep.
parallel:
MED: file-level joints (MEDsubdomainJointCr, MEDsubdomainCorrespondenceWr for node-node / node-cell correspondences per computing step) for meshes split across subdomains; MEDLoader tools split a MED file into subdomains. MEDCoupling's parallel coupling classes (ParaMESH, DEC) were not read: unverified. Gmsh MSH 4.1: partitioning is in the data model via $PartitionedEntities (parentDim/parentTag, partition list, ghostEntityTag/partition), $GhostElements (elementTag, partitionTag, ghostPartitionTags), and option Mesh.PartitionCreateGhostCells (ghost cells = elements connected to neighbouring partitions by at least one node). The authors say ghost and data sections will be reworked for IO efficiency. Post-processing integer tags include a partition index (0 = none).</parallel>
<parameter name="database_like_aspects">MED: per-(entity type, geometry type) tables with columns (coords, connectivity, family, optional user number), a family table (family id -> group names), fields keyed by mesh name (the unique key linking field to mesh); group queries are set lookups via families. Adjacency is derived on demand: MEDCoupling buildDescendingConnectivity(desc, descIndx, revDesc, revDescIndx) builds descending/reverse tables like a join, and buildFacePartOfMySelfNode / getCellIdsLyingOnNodes are topological queries. Gmsh: the file is organised like normalised tables: entities (with boundary relation), nodes (FK to entity), elements (FK to entity, FK list to nodes), physical-group join (entity <-> physicalTag), periodic link table, partition tables. Tags act as primary keys and may be sparse; min/max/count header fields behave like index statistics. Neither has a schema language or typed attribute columns (Gmsh stores unknown sections opaquely), neither supports queries beyond tag lookup, and adjacency is never stored. This supports the user's database framing and suggests the gap is a schema'd relation store with derived-adjacency views.
spec_quality: Gmsh MSH 4.1: formal, versioned, field-by-field grammar, explicit change log 4.0 to 4.1 and announced future changes (https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html section 10.1); good for a single-program format. Weak points: no polyhedra, under-specified ghost/data sections, element-type list truncated with '...' (full list in GmshDefines.h). MED: the authoritative spec is the MEDfile C library Doxygen documentation (4.2.0 seen) plus a French reference manual shipped with SALOME (${MEDFILE_ROOT_DIR}/share/doc/html/index.html per med-file.html); the on-disk HDF5 layout is effectively defined by the library, and no standalone spec was located (unverified). MEDCoupling has good Doxygen API docs and tutorials, but intersection docs are brief and do not discuss non-conformal detection.
ecosystem: MED: SALOME (SMESH/ParaVis), code_aster, Code_Saturne (via cs_medcoupling_remapper), TrioCFD (LireMED), Gmsh MED export (2009 list post), ParaView; bindings: C and Fortran (MEDfile), C++ and Python via SWIG (MEDCoupling/MEDLoader), generic HDF5 tools. Gmsh MSH: native format of Gmsh (C++ with C/Python/Julia API), meshio, ParaView via plugins or meshio; many FEM codes read it (unverified per code). The format is easy to hand-parse. Neither is governed by a neutral standards body.

corrections.claim: Gmsh MSH 4.1 has no polyhedral element types; polygon/polyhedron ids 9/10 appear only in $InterpolationScheme; hidden types in GmshDefines.h unverified.
corrections.correction: Correct for the released format, but the gap is now closable and the picture is changing. GmshDefines.h has long defined MSH_POLYG_=34 and MSH_POLYH_=35 (and TYPE_POLYG=9/TYPE_POLYH=10); the released Gmsh 4.15.2 (24 Mar 2026) manual says 'current revision: version 4.1', default Mesh.MshFileVersion=4.1, and its GModelIO_MSH4.cpp contains no POLYG/POLYH handling, so polytopes have no 4.1 file encoding. The master branch (CHANGELOG '5.0.0 (Work-in-progress)') defines MSH 4.2 with a $Polytopes section: blocks of elementType 34/35 with per-record offsets (random access), polygon = node list, polyhedron = list of faces each as node list, plus optional sub-triangulation/sub-tetrahedralization whose extra nodes are 'the hanging or interior nodes of the polytope'; polytopes share the element tag space; master $Elements reader errors on type 34/35. The 'new polytope implementation ... replaces the old polygon/polyhedron elements, levelset commands and Plugin(CutMesh)'. Treat 4.2 as unreleased.
corrections.source: gmsh.texi (master) section 'MSH file format'; gmsh.texi at tag gmsh_4_15_2; opt_mesh.texi (4.15.2 default 4.1, master default 4.2); CHANGELOG.txt (live-clones/gmsh mirror); src/common/GmshDefines.h; src/geo/GModelIO_MSH4.cpp at master and gmsh_4_15_2

corrections.claim: Neither format stores face/edge adjacency; MED polyhedra faces are duplicated per cell so face adjacency must be recomputed; lesson 'no format has shared deduplicated faces with signed refs'.
corrections.correction: Two counter-examples. (a) MED has a second connectivity mode, MED_DESCENDING, with entity types MED_DESCENDING_FACE / MED_DESCENDING_EDGE: faces/edges are written once as their own entities (with FAM/NUM/names), and cells reference them by number. In the MED test6.c example, edges are written as MED_DESCENDING_EDGE/MED_SEG2 in MED_DESCENDING mode and triangles as MED_CELL/MED_TRIA3 in MED_DESCENDING mode with connectivity {1,2,-5,-5,3,-4}, i.e. signed edge ids; the sign is presumably orientation but no doc text states the convention and the example's signs are not a consistent loop, so treat 'sign = orientation' as inferred. MEDmeshPolyhedronWr also has a MED_DESCENDING branch (connectivity size = nodeindex size, i.e. one face id per face). Unverified: whether MEDCoupling/MEDLoader, SMESH or code_aster read/write descending mode; MEDCoupling's UMesh is nodal-only and derives faces via buildDescendingConnectivity (desc/descIndx/revDesc/revDescIndx CSR, result not type-sorted). (b) MSH 4.2 (WIP) adds $Edges (edgeTag + 2 node tags) and $Faces (blocks by node count: 3, 4, more for polygons; faceTag + node tags), produced by createEdges()/createFaces(); these carry tags but no explicit cell->face list in the file. The report's nodal-mode description of MED polyhedra (faceindex -> nodeindex -> connectivity, 1-based) is correct for MED_NODAL.
corrections.source: docs.salome-platform.org/med-4.2.0-documentation/a02994.html (test6.c); a01859.html and MEDmeshPolyhedronWr.c source listing; a03170.html; gmsh.texi master; MEDCouplingUMesh.cxx (buildDescendingConnectivity doc)

corrections.claim: $GhostElements: elementTag, partitionTag, ghostPartitionTags (the authors say it will be reworked for IO efficiency).
corrections.correction: Accurate for 4.1: the 4.15.2 manual says 'The $GhostElements, $NodeData, $ElementData and $ElementNodeData will be reworked for greater IO efficiency, with separation of entries by type and a block structure with predictable sizes.' In MSH 4.2 (master, unreleased) this is done: $GhostElements = numBlocks numGhostElements, then per block partitionTag ghostPartitionTag numElementsInBlock elementTag...; $NodeData/$ElementData/$ElementNodeData store blocked records with size_t tags first then values; $Entities/$PartitionedEntities records end with embedded entities of all dimensions (4.1 stored only curves embedded in surfaces, tag-offset). CHANGELOG 5.0 also lists 'support for partition overlaps' and 'save only the local partitioned Brep'.
corrections.source: gmsh.texi at gmsh_4_15_2 (lines ~5266-5274) and master ('The 4.2 revision ... modifications'); CHANGELOG.txt

corrections.claim: MED: C library MEDfile 4.x; docs seen at 4.2.0.
corrections.correction: MED 4.2.0 was the version bundled in SALOME 9.15.0 (Sep 2025). MED 5.0.0 exists (tar.bz2 on files.salome-platform.org/Salome/medfile; packaged by openSUSE 2025-03-25, Fedora 43 'med-5.0.0-7', OpenBSD 5.0.0p2; packagers patch it to accept HDF5 >= 1.12.1 up to 1.14). Please note that, by default, exported MED files with version 9.16 cannot be imported with previous versions of branch 9' — i.e. an on-disk compatibility break. No 5.x/6.x changelog or documentation was located (docs.salome-platform.org/med-5.0.0- and med-6.0.1-documentation return 404), so what changed is unknown. Also: 'Med library (medfichier) can read only MED files of version 2.2 and newer.'

corrections.claim: Mesh.SaveTopology and Mesh.SaveParametric control writing B-rep and parametric coordinates.
corrections.correction: Mesh.SaveTopology: 'Save model topology in MSH2 output files (this is always saved in MSH3 and above)'. In MSH4 the $Entities section is always written when a model exists (it is 'optional' only from the reader's side). Mesh.SaveParametric ('Save parametric coordinates of nodes', default 0) is correctly described. Also relevant: Mesh.SaveWithoutOrphans (skip entities not connected to any highest-dim entity, MSH4 only); Mesh.SaveAll in MSH2 discards physical groups.
corrections.source: opt_mesh.texi (gmsh_4_15_2 and master); gmsh.texi 'Elementary entities vs. physical groups'

corrections.claim: MED HDF5 tree: ENS_MAA/<mesh>/ holds MAI (cells) ... NOE (nodes) ...; FAS/<mesh>/FAMILLE_ZERO.
corrections.correction: The cited forum dump has a computing-step group between the mesh and MAI/NOE: ENS_MAA/Mesh_1/-0000000000000000001-0000000000000000001/MAI/{HE8,QU4,SE2}/{FAM,NOD,NUM} and .../NOE; FAS/Mesh_1/FAMILLE_ZERO sits at mesh level (not per step); there is also a top-level INFOS_GENERALES group. The forum thread has no replies, so it gives no spec pointer.

corrections.claim: Legacy MED 2.3 family 'attributes' exist; a 2009 Gmsh list post said they should be deprecated, current status unverified.
corrections.correction: Status is determinable: the MED >= 3 write API MEDfamilyCr(fid, mesh, famname, famnumber, ngroup, groupnames) has no attribute arguments; attributes are reachable only through MEDfamily23Info, documented as reading family information (name, attribute numbers/values/descriptions, number, groups) 'from a mesh created with MED 2.3'. So attributes are read-only legacy, not a live feature.

corrections.claim: MED/MEDCoupling have quadratic types; anything above quadratic in MED 4.x is unverified.
corrections.correction: MEDCoupling's NormalizedCellType enum (master) is: POINT1, SEG2, SEG3, SEG4 (cubic edge), POLYL (polyline), TRI3, QUAD4, POLYGON, TRI6, TRI7, QUAD8, QUAD9, QPOLYG (quadratic polygon), TETRA4, PYRA5, PENTA6, HEXA8, TETRA10, HEXGP12 (hexagonal prism), PYRA13, PENTA15, PENTA18, HEXA20, HEXA27, POLYHED. MED file codes (SMESH MEDWrapper enum) are 100*dim + nnodes: POINT1=1, SEG2=102, SEG3=103, TRIA3=203, QUAD4=204, TRIA6=206, TRIA7=207, QUAD8=208, QUAD9=209, TETRA4=304, PYRA5=305, PENTA6=306, HEXA8=308, TETRA10=310, OCTA12=312, PYRA13=313, PENTA15=315, PENTA18=318, HEXA20=320, HEXA27=327, POLYGONE=400, POLYGON2=420 (quadratic polygon), POLYEDRE=500. The SMESH wrapper enum has no SEG4, so a MED-side cubic edge is unverified. Net: complete-quadratic (TRIA7/QUAD9/PENTA18/HEXA27) and quadratic polygons are first-class; no cubic or higher 2D/3D cells in either; MED separately supports arbitrary polynomial interpolation definitions for fields via MEDinterp (see missing facts).

corrections.claim: UMesh also has static Intersect2DMeshes, conformize2D/3D(eps), mergeNodes; only signatures were seen, behaviour is unverified.
corrections.correction: Behaviour is documented in source. conformize2D(eps): 2D-in-2D only; where an edge of a cell can be split into entire existing sub-edges it replaces it by them; adds no nodes for linear edges; modified cells become NORM_POLYGON/NORM_QPOLYG; order/orientation preserved; returns subdivided cell ids; nodes closer than eps must be merged first. conformize3D(eps): 3D-in-3D, 'Only polyhedron cells are supported' (convertAllToPoly first); 'only works for partition-like non-conformities. When joining adjacent faces, the set of all small faces must fit exactly into the neighboring bigger face. No real face intersection is actually computed'; throws otherwise; eps is absolute. Intersect2DMeshes(m1, m2, eps): partitions m1 using m2 as a tool, result is polygons with all m1 nodes plus new nodes, returns cellNb1/cellNb2 provenance (-1 = m1 part not covered by m2); requires both meshes oriented and 'clean (no un-merged nodes, no non-conformal cells)'. orientCorrectlyPolyhedrons() fixes polyhedron face ordering so all facet normals point outward (the MEDCoupling polyhedron face-orientation convention).

corrections.claim: Code_Saturne wrapper also lists Barycentric, BarycentricGeo2D, MappedBarycentric.
corrections.correction: These are enumerators of INTERP_KERNEL::IntersectionType itself (Triangulation, Convex, Geometric2D, PointLocator, Barycentric, BarycentricGeo2D, MappedBarycentric), not Code_Saturne additions. The intersec-specifics page also notes Convex and the 3D-surface intersectors support only mixed tri/quad meshes, PLANAR_FACE_5/6 assume planar hex faces while GENERAL_24/48 do not, and the page itself is inconsistent (SPLIT_NODES_5/6 vs PLANAR_FACE_5/6 naming; PrintLevel range).

corrections.claim: MEDCoupling 9.14-9.16 in SALOME.
corrections.correction: SALOME 9.16.0 (Jul 2026) ships MEDCoupling 9.16.0, which adds CFEMDEC: an MPI parallel P1P1 interpolation engine (n source ranks to p target ranks, reverse transfer, ghost cells) that locates target nodes in source elements and uses shape functions, following a Code_Aster algorithm (MEDCouplingFieldDiscretizationOnNodeFE.cxx); the notes say the 9.16 version is not memory/CPU optimised (aggregated source meshes stored on every target rank). 9.16 also adds MEDConverter.py importing Systus, ANSYS (CDB), Abaqus (INP), Aster, Zset (GEOF), Tetgen into MEDFileUMesh. The GitHub mirror SalomePlatform/medcoupling is active (pushed 2026-10-20). A mirror README's 'v10 refactoring' remark was not verified.

corrections.claim: code_aster mortar contact, validation case PERF018 with incompatible meshes (ericca.uqtr.ca v1.01.397.pdf).
corrections.correction: Verified and slightly sharpened: V1.01.397 'PERF018 - Contact entre une sphère incluse dans une sphère' (21/04/2017): 'valider la méthode de type Mortar pour les problèmes de contact. Les maillages sont incompatibles afin de démontrer la robustesse de la méthode' — 3D MORTAR pairing (appariement) for a contact zone in CONTINUE formulation. It is a contact validation case, not a general non-conformal-mesh mechanism; the MED file carries only the two group names.

missing_important: Convergence on how non-conformity is encoded: both ecosystems resolve a non-conformal (hanging-face) interface by emitting conformal POLYHEDRA rather than an interface object. MEDCoupling conformize3D turns 'partition-like' non-conformities (small faces exactly tiling a big face) into polyhedra with split faces, computing no intersections; MSH 4.2 $Polytopes stores a polyhedron as face node-lists plus an optional sub-tetrahedralization whose extra nodes are explicitly 'the hanging or interior nodes of the polytope'. The report's conclusion that neither has a first-class interface object still holds; the baseline to beat is 'non-conformal = polyhedral cell with hanging nodes', and a transport code (DG/SN) may actually prefer that representation to a mortar object.

The report's 'adopt shared deduplicated faces with signed refs, which no format has' must be revised: MED_DESCENDING mode (faces/edges as MED_DESCENDING_FACE/EDGE entities referenced by signed ids from cells, including a descending branch in the polyhedron writer) and MSH 4.2 $Faces/$Edges both exist. The differentiator is not existence but (i) consumer support (MEDCoupling/MEDLoader are nodal-only; descending-mode uptake by SMESH/code_aster unverified) and (ii) a documented orientation/sign convention, which MED's docs do not state.

MED file 6.0.1 breaks backward compatibility: SALOME 9.16 warns MED files it exports cannot by default be read by earlier 9.x; MED 5.0.0 (2024/25) also exists. If MED is an export target, pin the on-disk MED major version and offer the older format as an option; no changelog for 5.x/6.x was found, so the actual format change is unknown.

MED has an interpolation API (MEDinterpCr(name, geotype, cellnode, nbasisfunc, nvariable, maxdegree, nmaxcoef) + MEDinterpBaseFunctionWr(powers, coefficients) and readers MEDinterpInfo/MEDinterpBaseFunctionRd) that stores arbitrary polynomial basis functions per geometry type for fields. This is closer to the report's proposed '(reference element, order, layout)' model than enumerated element ids, and is a precedent for a high-order/DG field description independent of the mesh element enumeration. Seen only via API reference snippets; MEDCoupling support for it was not checked.

Gmsh release state matters for the baseline: latest release 4.15.2 (24 Mar 2026) writes MSH 4.1 (default Mesh.MshFileVersion 4.1) with no polytope support; MSH 4.2, $Polytopes, $Edges/$Faces, blocked ghost/data sections, embedded entities of all dimensions, partition overlaps, and the API calls mesh/addPolyhedra, getPolyhedra, get/set/createPolytopeSimplices, Mesh.CreateEdges/CreateFaces, Mesh.Algorithm3D=11 (parallel Delaunay) are all in the 5.0.0 work-in-progress branch. Design against 4.2 only as a moving target; export to 4.1 for compatibility.

MSH 4.2 $Polytopes block layout is a useful IR precedent for variable-size records: a block starts with numPolytopesInBlock+1 offsets (in size_t values) so 'any range of records can be located and read without reading the ones before it' — i.e. CSR-style random access for variable-arity cells inside a sequential format.

MEDCoupling 9.16's CFEMDEC adds a parallel P1P1 node-to-element-localisation remapper distinct from the existing dual-mesh node-to-node method, with reverse transfer and ghost-cell support; the report's remapper section covers only the serial MEDCouplingRemapper (P0P0/P0P1/P1P0/P1P1). ParaMESH/DEC classes remain unexamined.

MEDCoupling polyhedron face orientation is a convention enforced by orientCorrectlyPolyhedrons(): facet normals point out of the cell; the -1 separator rule is confirmed only by the tutorial example (no formal page found).

buildDescendingConnectivity's result mesh is not sorted by geometric type and must be sortCellsInMEDFileFrmt()'d before MED export; likewise conformize2D/3D 'lead to have a non geometric type sorted mesh (for MED file users)'. MED files require cells grouped by geometry type — a constraint any exporter from a free-order IR must handle.

Documentation access note: docs.salome-platform.org blocks non-browser clients (cPanel 'badbots' 403 to curl) and gitlab.onelab.info is behind Anubis; the GitHub mirrors live-clones/gmsh and SalomePlatform/{medcoupling,smesh} are the practical primary sources for automated checks.

topic: Finite-volume CFD mesh formats: OpenFOAM polyMesh, Fluent .msh/CFF, UGRID (NASA/AFLR3), SU2
summary: These four formats show a spectrum for cell-centred finite-volume solvers. OpenFOAM polyMesh and Fluent .msh/CFF are face-based: faces are first-class, each face stores its two adjacent cells (owner/neighbour in OpenFOAM, c0/c1 in Fluent), and cells are implicit or derived. That makes arbitrary polyhedra native. UGRID and SU2 are cell-based, element-type-limited (tet/pyr/prism/hex, plus tri/quad/line in SU2) interchange formats with boundary tags. They have no polyhedra, and SU2 derives its dual control volumes at read time (unverified here). The key finding for non-conformal interfaces: OpenFOAM stores an AMI interface as an ordinary pair of boundary patches whose coupling is recomputed at runtime. Only the patch type, neighbour name, transform and AMI tuning parameters are stored, and the weights are never stored. Fluent stores the non-conformal intersection (child) faces explicitly in separate zones, with bc-type offset by +1000, plus a parent-face map (section 61). Both are mature and widely used but have only informal, doc-based specs. All four support conformal-by-construction connectivity as the baseline, with non-conformity expressed as metadata plus a derived projection operator.
data_model: OpenFOAM polyMesh (constant/polyMesh/): five core files. `points` is a list of vectors (index = position, from 0). `faces` is a list of faces, each an ordered list of point labels (faceList; may be warped). `owner` is a labelList of length nFaces, giving the owner cell per face. `neighbour` is a labelList of length nInternalFaces only (boundary faces have no neighbour). `boundary` is a list of patch dictionaries with `type`, `nFaces`, `startFace` (verified at doc.cfd.direct mesh-files). Cells are NOT stored: a cell is an unordered list of faces, derived by inverting owner/neighbour (cells()/cellCells() are computed on demand in primitiveMesh; derived-on-demand is from memory, unverified in source). Invariants (user-guide mesh-description): cells are contiguous and non-overlapping; each cell is geometrically closed (outward face-area vectors sum ~0) and topologically closed (every edge shared by exactly two of the cell's faces); internal face normal points from owner to the higher-numbered neighbour cell; boundary face normal points out of the domain. Ordering rules (OpenFOAM wiki Write_OpenFOAM_meshes, and a comment in DelaunayMeshIO.C): the owner is the lower-numbered cell; internal faces come first, sorted by owner ascending then neighbour ascending (the 'upper triangular' order, which is the face-order of the strictly upper triangle of the cell-cell adjacency matrix, hence a free CSR/LDU matrix layout); boundary faces follow, grouped contiguously per patch in patch order. `renumberMesh` and checkMesh fix/detect violations. Optional: pointZones/cellZones/faceZones files (faceZone has a labelList of face indices plus a flipMap of booleans for orientation; doc.cfd.direct mesh-zones). Sets (cellSets etc.) live in constant/polyMesh/sets. Fluent .msh (legacy ASCII, S-expression, hex indices; ANSYS Fluent UG appendix B.3): `(10 (zone-id first last type ND))` nodes; `(12 (zone-id first last type element-type))` cells with element-type 0 mixed, 1 tri, 2 tet, 3 quad, 4 hex, 5 pyramid, 6 wedge, 7 polyhedral; `(13 (zone-id first last bc-type face-type))` faces; body line `n0 n1 .. c0 c1` for fixed face type, or `x n0..nf c0 c1` for mixed (0) and polygonal (5) with leading node count. Right-hand rule on node order points toward c0; c0 or c1 = 0 on a boundary face. Zone-id 0 declares total counts. bc-type examples: 2 interior, 3 wall, 4 pressure-inlet, 5 pressure-outlet, 7 symmetry, 8 periodic-shadow, 10 velocity-inlet, 12 periodic, 24 interface, 31 parent (hanging node), 37 axis. `(18 (first last periodic-zone shadow-zone))` pairs periodic faces. Polyhedral cells need no cell body: the cell is defined implicitly by the faces that reference it via c0/c1. Fluent CFF (.cas.h5/.dat.h5; Fluent UG B.1): HDF5; /meshes/<id>/{faces,cells,nodes} groups, heavy data as 1D/2D datasets, min/max IDs and counts as attributes; case 'settings' group holds BC/model settings as formatted strings; data file has /results per mesh id. Forum evidence shows /meshes/1/faces/nodes/1 has `nnodes` and `nodes` datasets (CSR-like per-face node counts + flat node list); c0/c1 dataset layout is not documented on the pages I could fetch (unverified). UGRID AFLR3 .b8.ugrid (NASA HiLiftPW README): big-endian unformatted stream (no record markers), 7 int header `nnodes ntface nqface ntet npyr nprz nhex`, then coords, boundary tri node-pointers, boundary quad node-pointers, one surface tag per boundary face (tris then quads), then tet(4), pyramid(5), prism(6), hex(8) node-pointers. Companion `.mapbc` maps surface tag to BC id. Full spec at simcenter.msstate.edu (not retrieved; orientation/node-order conventions unverified). SU2 .su2 (SU2 docs Mesh-File): text; `NDIME=`, `NELEM=` followed by lines `<VTK-type> n0 n1 ... [index]` (VTK ids: 3 line, 5 tri, 9 quad, 10 tet, 12 hex, 13 prism, 14 pyramid), `NPOIN=` then coordinates, `NMARK=`, per marker `MARKER_TAG=` and `MARKER_ELEMS=` with boundary elements (VTK id + nodes). Periodic markers and polyhedra not described on that page.
polyhedra: OpenFOAM: native, unlimited faces per cell and nodes per face (user-guide mesh-description). It is the main reason the format is face-based; a polyhedron is just whatever faces point to it via owner/neighbour. No element-type tag exists at all (hex/tet are detected geometrically by cellModeller on demand, unverified detail). Fluent: native polyhedral cell type 7 and polygonal face type 5 / mixed face type 0 with per-face node count; cell content implicit from faces. Fluent explicitly requires NN and NF 'vary' per polyhedral cell. UGRID/AFLR3: no polyhedra; only tet/pyr/prism/hex volume elements plus tri/quad boundary faces (hard-coded header counts). SU2 .su2: only the 7 VTK element ids listed (line, tri, quad, tet, hex, prism, pyramid); no general polyhedra in the file format per the docs page; SU2 builds its vertex-based dual control volumes internally (unverified from this research). Design consequence: face-based is the minimal representation that makes polyhedra free, but it makes a cell's node set, shape and orientation derived rather than stored.
nonconformal: OpenFOAM AMI/ACMI: the mesh stores NO intersection. A non-conformal interface is two ordinary boundary patches in `boundary`, each with `type cyclicAMI` (or `cyclicACMI`), `neighbourPatch <name>` (or `coupleGroup`), a `transform` (none/rotational/translational via cyclicTransform), `matchTolerance` (default 1e-4 from coupledPolyPatch), AMI method (default `faceAreaWeightAMI`), `requireMatch` (default true: patches must fully match/overlap), `lowWeightCorrection` (threshold weight below which interpolation is deactivated, default -1), all per cpp.openfoam.org v10 cyclicAMIPolyPatch/AMIInterpolation docs. At run time AMIInterpolation (based on Farrell & Maddison 2011 conservative local Galerkin projection) computes `srcAddress`/`tgtAddress` (labelListList) and `srcWeights`/`tgtWeights` (scalarListList), plus srcMagSf/tgtMagSf and weight sums for normalisation. Face-area-weighted: for each source face it finds overlapping target faces (processSourceFace/calcAddressing in faceAreaWeightAMI) and weights by overlap area. Projection/overlap is therefore detected geometrically at runtime on the pair of patches, within matchTolerance, after applying the transform; nothing in the file marks 'imprinted-ness'. ACMI (cyclicACMIPolyPatch, derived from cyclicAMIPolyPatch, verified at api.openfoam.com 2506 source): handles partial overlap. It uses `nonOverlapPatch <name>` pointing at a separate uncoupled patch holding the unmatched area; `mask()` field is 1 = coupled/overlap, 0 = non-overlap; optional `scale` (time-dependent PatchFunction1) scales the mask to open/close the interface; face areas are scaled so physical area is conserved. So a partially-overlapping interface is stored as two patches per side (couple + blockage) whose face sets are expected to be the same faces. Fluent: non-conformal grid interface is stored explicitly. The intersection faces (child faces) are written into separate face zones with bc-type + 1000 (e.g. 1003 wall); section `(61 (face-id0 face-id1))` lists 'Interface Face Parents' (each child refers to at least one parent); bc-type 24 = interface; bc-type 31 = parent (hanging node). Reading a non-conformal mesh saved in solution mode into meshing mode skips section 61 and the interface must be recreated (Fluent UG B.3). Hence Fluent materialises the imprinted/intersected faces in the file ('physical' imprint), OpenFOAM keeps the information-level pairing and recomputes weights each time (including on mesh motion). UGRID: no concept; interfaces must be conformal or handled by the solver outside the file. SU2: the page fetched doesn't describe non-conformal/sliding interface storage in the mesh file (SU2 does support sliding/fluid-structure interface via config markers, MARKER_ZONE_INTERFACE, from memory, unverified).
sets_and_partitions: OpenFOAM: boundary patches partition boundary faces by contiguous ranges (startFace, nFaces), so a boundary face belongs to exactly one patch, and patch membership is positional, not a tag. Patch groups via `inGroups` (unverified detail). Cells/faces/points can additionally be grouped by zones (cellZones, faceZones with flipMap, pointZones: labelLists, may overlap unlike patches is unverified) and sets. Zones are used for MRF, porosity, regions, and baffles; multi-region is done as separate polyMesh directories per region (constant/<region>/polyMesh), unverified detail. Fluent: everything is a zone by integer zone-id and contiguous index range (first-index..last-index), with a zone-type; cell zones have type 1 fluid, 17 solid, 0 dead; face zones have bc-type; names/mapping are in section 45 (zone section; not retrieved, unverified). Material is thus a cell-zone attribute, boundary type is a face-zone attribute. UGRID: boundary faces carry an integer surface tag; the `.mapbc` sidecar file maps tag to BC type and name; there are no volume tags/regions in the base format. SU2: boundary elements grouped under MARKER_TAG names; interior elements have no region/zone tag in the base format (multi-zone is by multiple mesh files, unverified).
strengths: Face-based owner/neighbour is minimal and exactly the data a finite-volume solver needs: face areas, centroids, volumes and the flux graph fall out directly; polyhedra cost nothing extra (OpenFOAM, Fluent type 7/5).
Upper-triangular face ordering (owner ascending, then neighbour ascending) gives the LDU/CSR matrix pattern for free and cache-friendly assembly (OpenFOAM wiki).
Strong invariants (closed cells, consistent orientation: normal owner to neighbour, right-hand-rule to c0) are checkable by a validator (checkMesh) and make bugs detectable.

OpenFOAM's non-conformal handling is a clean separation of concerns: the mesh stores topology and pairing metadata (neighbourPatch, transform, tolerances); the projection operator (addresses + weights) is derived data, recomputable and valid under mesh motion.
ACMI's mask plus scale elegantly models partial overlap and open/close interfaces without altering the mesh.
Fluent stores explicit child (intersection) faces and parent map (section 61), so downstream consumers need no intersection code, and hanging nodes (bc 31) are representable.

Zones as (id, contiguous range, type) in Fluent and name-based dictionaries in OpenFOAM give simple region/BC labelling; Fluent's mixed cell/face sections with count-prefixed lines allow heterogeneous element types in one section.
CFF uses HDF5 with counts as attributes and CSR-like per-face node lists (nnodes + nodes) for fast, parallel-friendly binary I/O.
weaknesses: No formal, versioned, machine-readable spec for any of them: OpenFOAM is defined by its source and docs; legacy Fluent .msh by a help-page appendix; UGRID by a web page and README conventions; SU2 by a docs page. CFF's c0/c1 layout was not found in documentation at all.

Cells are implicit in face-based formats: cell-node membership, cell type and local node/face ordering must be derived, and vertex-based or FE codes (and high-order, DG with reference elements) cannot get what they need without reconstruction.

No high-order or curved element support in any of the four (all linear; OpenFOAM faces are straight polygons possibly warped, unverified for curved), and no explicit geometry/CAD association; the only link to geometry is names/tags.

OpenFOAM requires strict ordering (upper-triangular, boundary contiguous), making writers/converters fragile and mesh editing costly (renumbering required); patch membership is positional, so a face cannot belong to two groups.

OpenFOAM's AMI weights are recomputed at runtime so pairing is not inspectable in the file; imprint status or mismatched faces are only discovered through tolerance-based geometry tests at solve time. Fluent's explicit intersection is solver-algorithm-specific and gets lost on cross-mode reads (section 61 skipped).

UGRID and SU2 lack polyhedra, fixed set of element types, boundary-only tags (UGRID) with side-car mapping file; UGRID's header hard-codes seven counts, is big-endian stream, and the format has no versioning or metadata; SU2's interior elements have no region labels.
ASCII legacy Fluent and SU2 are slow for large meshes; hex-indexed S-expression syntax is awkward to parse in parallel.

Parallel is handled outside the file (OpenFOAM processorN/ directories with processor patches; details unverified in this research); no standard distributed-mesh/ghost description in the format itself.
lessons_for_us: ADOPT a face-based core as the canonical connectivity: faces with (owner, neighbour) cell ids and an explicit orientation convention (normal from owner to neighbour; boundary normal outward). That makes polyhedra and mixed cells first-class and provides a flux graph for transport sweeps.
