But ALSO store optional cell->face and cell->node/shape-tag relations as first-class derived-and-cacheable indexes, so FE/DG/high-order and Monte Carlo (which needs cell->surfaces) consumers do not have to reconstruct them. In database terms: faces table + cells table + materialised indexes.

ADOPT OpenFOAM's canonical ordering as an optional, validated 'normal form' (internal faces sorted by owner then neighbour, boundary faces grouped), with a checker, but do not make it a required invariant of the logical model; ordering is a physical-layout/index property, not part of identity.

ADOPT the OpenFOAM separation for non-conformal interfaces: the stored model is pairing metadata (face-set A, face-set B, transform, tolerance, match-mode/required-match flag, ACMI-style mask/blockage set), and weights/overlaps are derived. DIFFER by also allowing an optional materialised, versioned 'imprint' relation (Fluent's child faces + parent map, section 61) with provenance, so the consumer can choose conformal-by-imprint (exact child faces, area conservation by construction) or projection-at-solve. This answers the user's imprinting question: at the information level an imprint is a relation parent_face -> child faces with geometric overlap data, not a modification of geometry.

DIFFER from positional patch membership (startFace/nFaces) and from zone-id ranges: use many-to-many named sets/labels over any entity dimension (vertex/edge/face/cell) so geometry layer, material/partition layer and boundary conditions are separate label spaces attached to the same entities; keep contiguity as an optional storage optimisation (run-length encoded ranges) not a semantic constraint. Fluent's integer zone ids with typed zones (fluid/solid/dead; wall/interface/periodic) are a good starting schema for typed label spaces.

ADOPT Fluent's explicit pattern for hanging nodes/parents (bc 31 'parent', section 61 parent map) as a general 'derived-from' entity relation, and OpenFOAM's flipMap pattern (set membership with per-member orientation sign) for oriented face sets such as baffles and interfaces.

ADOPT CFF's storage idea (HDF5-style: counts as attributes, CSR (offsets + flat indices) arrays for variable-length relations, mesh id groups, separate 'other' group for solver-private data) but add what all four lack: a formal versioned schema (e.g. a JSON-Schema/Arrow-like type description of each array and relation), stable entity ids, units, and extension slots, so that the IR can be exported to polyMesh, Fluent .msh/CFF, UGRID, SU2 as lossy views. Document explicitly what each exporter drops (e.g. UGRID drops polyhedra, SU2 drops zones).

Include layer links in the schema: each mesh entity has an optional `geom` association (B-rep vertex/edge/face/volume id + parametric coords), each cell has a partition/material label, so the three layers coexist coherently; none of the four formats provides this, only tag-based names, so it is an area where we can differ for a concrete advantage.

Plan for high-order and curved geometry from the start (these formats are all linear): store geometric order and node ordering convention per cell/face-type table rather than hard-coding VTK ids (SU2) or header counts (UGRID).

Specify parallel as part of the model (partition id, ghost/halo layers, shared-entity global ids) rather than as a side-effect of separate directories; OpenFOAM's processor patches are a de facto precedent (details unverified), but ours should be explicit and versioned.

Provide a validator (closed cells, normal consistency, interface match within tolerance, ordering) as part of the spec, like checkMesh, so every exporter/importer can be tested against the same invariants.
spec_quality: Weak across the board. None of the four has a formal, versioned, machine-checkable specification. OpenFOAM's polyMesh is documented by the user guide plus the source (the implementation is the spec; the OpenFOAM Foundation and ESI/openfoam.com forks diverge in details such as AMI code and docs); invariants are enforced by checkMesh. Legacy Fluent .msh is the best-documented textual spec (a numbered-section appendix with headers, element-type and bc-type tables, orientation rule) but is legacy and incomplete for modern needs; the HDF5-based CFF is described only at the group/dataset-naming level in the help (no c0/c1 layout found; unverified beyond forum evidence). UGRID is specified by a MSU SimCenter web page and README conventions (binary stream layout is clear; orientation and node ordering not confirmed). SU2's .su2 is a short docs page; periodic and polyhedra not covered there. None carries a version number in a schema sense.
storage: OpenFOAM: per-file ASCII (default) or binary with FoamFile header (`format ascii|binary`), one file per array (points, faces, owner, neighbour, boundary), optionally compressed (.gz); large meshes in ASCII are slow but usable; parallel cases replicate the structure under processorN/ directories (unverified detail). Faces are stored as list-of-lists. Fluent legacy .msh: ASCII or binary variants of S-expression sections with hex indices; CFF .cas.h5/.dat.h5: HDF5 (heavy data in 1D/2D datasets, metadata in attributes), supports fast parallel binary I/O. Variable-length data use two 1D arrays: one for sizes and one for values. UGRID: C-style big-endian unformatted stream (.b8.ugrid), also ASCII and little-endian variants (unverified), a flat sequential array layout good for mmap-like reads but with no index or metadata. SU2: ASCII text, no binary variant on the docs page; slow at scale.
database_like_aspects: OpenFOAM polyMesh is effectively a small relational schema: tables points(id,xyz), faces(id,[point_id]), cell-face relation as an edge list (owner, neighbour) per face, boundary(patch,startFace,nFaces), zones as sets with optional per-member attribute (flipMap). Cells, cell-cell adjacency (cellCells), point-cell and edge tables are derived views computed on demand and cached, as in a database with materialised views; its upper-triangular ordering is a clustered index producing the sparse matrix layout. Fluent is closer to typed tables with a zone dimension: node, face, cell tables each partitioned into zones; a face row is (nodes, c0, c1), a zone is a typed range with attributes; counts are declared up front (zone-id 0). CFF turns this into HDF5 datasets with attributes. AMI weights (addressing + weights as labelListList/scalarListList) are effectively a sparse-matrix join table between two face sets, derived on demand with a tolerance-based spatial join. UGRID and SU2 are flat element lists with tag columns: the least database-like. None offers queries, schemas, or ids beyond array position, so identity is positional and fragile under renumbering.
ecosystem: OpenFOAM: written by blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, cfMesh, gmshToFoam/fluentMeshToFoam/ideasUnvToFoam/other converters, Salome/Pointwise/Cadence exporters, read by OpenFOAM solvers, ParaView (OpenFOAM reader, foam), PyVista, meshio (read/write); C++ only natively (libOpenFOAM), Python via fluidfoam/Ofpp style readers (unverified). Fluent: written by Fluent Meshing, ICEM, Pointwise, Gmsh (msh export), meshio, PETSc DMPlex reader (plexfluent.c reads index 13 faces/12 cells), and read by Fluent, CFD-Post (limited msh.h5 support), STAR-CCM+ and others. CFF is read via h5py/other HDF5 tools (forum), with limited public documentation. UGRID (AFLR3): written by AFLR/VGRID/Pointwise/Gridgen, read by FUN3D, NSU3D, USM3D, TetrUSS-family codes, pyNastran converters, and used heavily in NASA workshops (HiLiftPW, Drag Prediction); `.mapbc` or `.mapbc`-like side files accompany it. SU2: native .su2 read by SU2; also supports CGNS; produced by meshio, Gmsh, Pointwise, ICEM, etc.
geometry_association: None in any of the four as a first-class structure. OpenFOAM stores only patch names/types and zones; a link back to CAD faces is lost (snappyHexMesh may use STL regions during meshing and the patch name is the sole remnant; an optional projection surface `surfPtr_`/`surfDict_` exists on cyclicAMIPolyPatch for AMI projection, verified in class docs, but this is a solver-time construct, not CAD association). Fluent: zone ids/names (and BC types) only; no B-rep ids. UGRID: integer surface tag per boundary face, mapped via `.mapbc` to BC; the tag is typically a CAD surface/patch group but nothing is stored about parametric coordinates or geometry. SU2: MARKER_TAG names only. Conclusion: geometry association is by label, not by reference, in all four.
high_order: None of the four supports high-order or curved elements in the file format as far as the retrieved documentation shows. OpenFOAM: points + straight (possibly warped) polygon faces only; Fluent .msh element-type table is limited to linear tri/tet/quad/hex/pyramid/wedge/polyhedral; UGRID: linear tet/pyramid/prism/hex only; SU2: the VTK ids listed are the linear ones (line 3, tri 5, quad 9, tet 10, hex 12, prism 13, pyramid 14). Higher-order meshing is handled by other codes' formats (CGNS, Gmsh, Exodus) per general knowledge, not verified here. Therefore any IR targeting DG or curved geometry needs its own per-cell order/node-layout schema.
parallel: OpenFOAM: domain decomposition (decomposePar) writes processorN/ subdirectories each with its own polyMesh and processor boundary patches (type processor, with myProcNo/neighbProcNo, and shared point/face addressing files such as faceProcAddressing, cellProcAddressing, pointProcAddressing, boundaryProcAddressing mapping local to global ids); this is from memory and NOT verified in this research. Coupled patches (cyclic, cyclicAMI, processorCyclic) exist as patch types; the cyclicAMI code references parallel 'AMIs_' per interpolator (cpp.openfoam.org v10 class docs; parallel logic not examined). Fluent: partitioning is done in-solver (zone partitions, 'interface zones' between partitions); the file format itself has no parallel/ghost representation that I verified (unverified). UGRID/SU2: no partition info in the mesh file; the solver partitions at read time (SU2 uses ParMETIS/METIS, unverified). Takeaway: no format here standardises distributed meshes, global ids, or ghost layers in the interchange file."

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM AMI/ACMI: 'the mesh stores NO intersection'; OpenFOAM keeps the information-level pairing and recomputes weights each time; contrast with Fluent which materialises intersected faces.
corrections.correction: True only for ESI OpenFOAM (api.openfoam.com 2506 still has cyclicAMI/cyclicACMI) and for Foundation versions <= 10. The OpenFOAM Foundation replaced AMI with Non-Conformal Coupling (NCC) in v10 (July 2022): NCC 'creates new faces at the intersections of overlapping faces on the coupled patches' which 'become part of the finite volume meshes on both sides'; conservation then holds by construction (cfd.direct measured ~0.1% AMI conservation error that never converges away). ACMI and repeat-AMI were removed in v10; AMI was retained for v10 only and v11 release notes state NCC 'replaces AMI'; cpp.openfoam.org v11, v12 and v13 return 404 for cyclicAMIPolyPatch and AMIInterpolation (consistent with the announced removal). Representation: nonConformalPolyPatch 'is a placeholder and must have no faces' and is linked to an 'original' patch; nonConformalCyclic patches appear in constant/polyMesh/boundary with zero faces and are populated by fvMeshStitcher connect()/disconnect() at run time ('the poly mesh is considered non-coupled whilst the finite volume mesh is considered coupled'); every owner-side original patch must have an associated nonConformalError patch (holds construction errors / non-overlap); created with createNonConformalCouples. So the report's contrast is inverted: both Fluent and current Foundation OpenFOAM materialise cut faces; Fluent persists them (zones +1000, section 61), OpenFOAM derives them at load from zero-face placeholders. Lesson 3 ('adopt OpenFOAM separation') should be re-read in this light.

corrections.claim: None of the four supports high-order or curved elements in the file format; SU2 VTK ids are the linear ones only.
corrections.correction: SU2's DG-FEM reader (CSU2ASCIIMeshReaderFEM.cpp, master) decodes the NELEM element-type integer as VTK_Type = type % 100, nPolyGrid = (type % 10000)/100 + 1, and if type > 10000, nPolySol = type/10000 - 1 (i.e. type = VTK + 100*(nPolyGrid-1) [+ 10000*(nPolySol+1)]); surface elements use VTK + 100*(nPolyGrid-1). A plain VTK id is the linear case. So the .su2 text format does carry high-order (curved) elements and a separate solution polynomial degree, but only for the FEM-DG path; it is undocumented on the Mesh-File docs page and the standard FV reader uses linear ids only.

corrections.claim: SU2: interior elements have no region/zone tag in the base format (multi-zone is by multiple mesh files, unverified).
corrections.correction: SU2's default is a single multizone .su2 file: MULTIZONE_MESH= YES (default) requires 'the keywords NZONE= and IZONE=' in the mesh file; separate per-zone files are used only with MULTIZONE_MESH= NO plus MESH_FILENAME in each sub-config (CONFIG_LIST order must match mesh-file zone order). Zones are therefore a first-class mesh-file concept in SU2 (per-zone blocks), though still without per-element material tags inside a zone.

corrections.claim: Fluent: partitioning is done in-solver; the file format itself has no parallel/ghost representation that I verified.
corrections.correction: Fluent case files have a Partitions section, index 40: '(40 (zone-id first-index last-index partition-count)( p1 ... pn ))', storing each cell's partition id (0..partition-count-1) for partitioned grids. No ghost/halo layer is stored, but per-cell partition assignment is.

corrections.claim: Right-hand rule on node order points toward c0.
corrections.correction: ANSYS documentation disagrees with itself across versions. 2024 R2 UG (tgd_user_format_gridsect): 'if you curl the fingers of your right hand in the order of the nodes, your thumb will point toward c0'. Fluent 12.0 UG (same section): 'your thumb will point toward c1' (and a 2D cross-product rule that exists only in the older text). The Fluent UDF manual states interior face area normals point from c0 to c1 and boundary normals point out of the domain, with boundary faces having c0 only. OpenFOAM's working importer fluent3DMeshToFoam reads the first listed cell as neighbour and the second as owner and flips only when needed ('Pre-filtering: flip owner boundary or wrong oriented internal faces'), i.e. it assumes the stored node-order normal points toward the first-listed cell (c0), consistent with the 2024 R2 text. Treat the convention as version/writer-dependent: an importer should verify orientation geometrically (cell volumes / closedness) rather than trust the rule. Medium confidence on which is 'true'; high confidence that the docs conflict.

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM: hex/tet are detected geometrically by cellModeller on demand.
corrections.correction: Shape recognition is topological, not geometric: the cellMatcher family (hexMatcher, tetMatcher, prismMatcher, pyrMatcher, wedgeMatcher, tetWedgeMatcher) matches on face-size counts (a 'hash value of all face sizes' for quick recognition) and a connectivity walk over faces/edges; inputs are faces, faceOwner and the cell's face labels, with no point coordinates.

corrections.claim: cyclicAMI stores a `transform` (none/rotational/translational via cyclicTransform).
corrections.correction: In Foundation v10 cyclicTransform the primary keyword is `transformType` (values unspecified/none/rotational/translational); `transform` is only a backwards-compatible alias. Rotational requires `rotationAxis` and `rotationCentre` (`rotationAngle` optional, needed for a 'complete' transform); translational requires `separation` (legacy alias `separationVector`). ESI uses `transform` with a different value set (e.g. coincidentFullMatch).

corrections.claim: the cyclicAMI code references parallel 'AMIs_' per interpolator.
corrections.correction: In v10 cyclicAMIPolyPatch, `AMIs_` is a PtrList<AMIInterpolation> paired with `AMITransforms_` ('AMI transforms (from source to target)', a List<transformer>), which indicates one interpolator per transform (repeated/periodic copies of the neighbour patch), not per processor. Parallel handling is separate (e.g. singlePatchProc()). This is an inference from the paired containers; the page does not say so explicitly.

corrections.claim: Fluent names/mapping are in section 45 (zone section; not retrieved, unverified).
corrections.correction: Verified: zone sections are index 39 or 45 with four header fields '(39|45 (zone-id zone-type zone-name domain-id)( ... ))'; 'When only zone-id, zone-type, zone-name, and domain-id are specified, the index 45 is preferred'. Note PETSc's plexfluent.c parses 39 (not 45) for zone labels.

corrections.claim: Fluent cell zones have type 1 fluid, 17 solid, 0 dead.
corrections.correction: Matches the 2024 R2 UG ('fluid (type = 1) or solid (type = 17)', 0 = dead). The Fluent 12.0 UG instead defines 0 = dead, 1 = active, 32 = inactive ('currently only parent cells resulting from hanging node adaption') and says solid vs fluid 'is now determined by properties (i.e., material type)'. An importer should accept 0/1/17/32.

corrections.claim: UGRID: orientation/node-order conventions unverified.
corrections.correction: Now checkable. UG_IO/AFLR3 requires only that boundary faces on each closed surface be consistently oriented ('normals all point out of or into the surface'); each closed surface may use its own orientation, and consistency is not even required if all surfaces are simply connected. So UGRID carries no reliable inward/outward boundary normal convention. Pyramid node ordering is non-VTK: nodes 1,2,5,4 form the quad base and node 3 is the apex (meshio permutes ugrid->VTK as [1,0,3,4,2] on read, [1,0,4,2,3] on write). Header order confirmed: nnodes, ntri, nquad, ntet, npyr, nprism, nhex; one integer tag per boundary face after the quad connectivity.

missing_important: OpenFOAM Foundation NCC (v10+, 2022) is the closest existing precedent for the user's 'imprinting at the information level': the stored polyMesh geometry is untouched (placeholder patches with zero faces + an 'original patch' link + a mandatory error patch per owner-side original patch), and the intersection faces are generated into the FV mesh at load/motion by fvMeshStitcher, giving conservation by construction and natural partial overlap. v11 added `checkMesh -allGeometry` NCC coverage output and 'stitched' output for visualisation. The two OpenFOAM forks now embody the two design options the report contrasts (ESI: AMI projection weights; Foundation: materialised cut faces).

Fluent's hanging-node machinery is the general parent->child relation the report should cite alongside section 61: Cell Tree index 58 and Face Tree index 59, syntax '(59 (face-id0 face-id1 parent-zone-id child-zone-id) ( number-of-kids kid-id-0 ... ))', children in a separate zone, parent cells moved to an inactive zone (type 32 in 12.0 docs). Section 61 (Interface Face Parents) only covers non-conformal intersection children ('each child refers to at least one parent'; skipped when read into meshing mode).

OpenFOAM polyMesh::faces_ is a faceCompactIOList: binary output writes a CompactListList ('packed storage ... using an offset table'), i.e. CSR offsets + flat point labels; ASCII is list-of-lists. polyMesh also persists `tetBasePtIs` (per-face base point for tet decomposition) - a materialised derived index. Both support the 'database with materialised views' framing.

OpenFOAM treats ordering as an invariant, not a recommendation: primitiveMesh::checkUpperTriangular returns error-level ('***Faces not in upper triangular order') for owner >= neighbour on any internal face and for per-cell non-increasing face labels vs sorted neighbours; it does not check a single global owner sort, and 'internal faces first' is structural (neighbour has nInternalFaces entries). LDU addressing assumes this.

Fluent UDF-level conventions (needed by any exporter targeting Fluent consumers): interior face area normals point from c0 to c1, boundary face normals point out of the domain, boundary faces have c0 only (c1 = 0).

UGRID file-name suffix semantics (from meshio's reader table, secondary source, consistent with the HiLiftPW README): .ugrid ASCII; .b8/.lb8 C-stream big/little-endian 8-byte reals + 4-byte ints; .b4/.lb4 4-byte reals; .r8/.lr8/.r4/.lr4 Fortran unformatted with record markers; .b8l/.lb8l 8-byte ints. UG_IO also describes optional per-node initial-normal-spacing / BL-thickness arrays, per-face BC and reconnection flags, and a separate SPLIT file for split-face hexes; whether every optional trailing array lives in .ugrid proper was not confirmed, so the report's 'no volume tags' stays unconfirmed rather than confirmed.

Ecosystem caveat for polyhedra: meshio's Fluent reader discards c0/c1 ('Cut off the adjacent cell data'), does not read mixed binary faces, and has no support for element type 7 or face type 5 (writer has 'polyhedral: 7' commented out); PETSc plexfluent.c parses sections 2/10/12/13/39, derives cell type from face count and reorders only tri/quad/tet/hex/prism ('Celltype %s is unsupported' otherwise, pyramids included), reads binary as 32-bit ints, and carries the comment 'How could Fluent define the outward normal differently?'. So 'read by meshio/PETSc' holds only for element (non-polyhedral) meshes.

SU2's interface machinery is entirely config-side (mesh file carries only marker names): MARKER_ZONE_INTERFACE (every two consecutive markers form a pair; interface type chosen automatically from SOLVER), MARKER_FLUID_INTERFACE, MARKER_CHT_INTERFACE, KIND_INTERPOLATION in {NEAREST_NEIGHBOR, WEIGHTED_AVERAGE, ISOPARAMETRIC, RADIAL_BASIS_FUNCTION}, CONSERVATIVE_INTERPOLATION= YES/NO, MARKER_PERIODIC (periodic marker, donor marker, rotation centre, rotation angles, translation), MARKER_MIXINGPLANE_INTERFACE/MARKER_TURBOMACHINERY; docs state 'All zones can be discretized independently and do not need to be matching at the interfaces'. CGNS input is ADF-based only and embedded CGNS BCs are ignored.

Zone overlap in OpenFOAM remains unresolved (Foundation ZoneMesh source pages 404'd): ESI 2506 ZoneMesh has whichZone (single) and whichZones (all zones of an object), implying multi-zone membership is representable; but snappyHexMesh baffle creation fails with a 'face in multiple zones' error. Storage tolerates overlap, some tools reject it.

Fluent CFF: the c0/c1 dataset layout under /meshes/<id>/faces is still undocumented publicly (forum guidance points to the UDF manual and to inspecting a tiny case with h5py); CFF files are 'always binary', compressed, the default since at least 2024 R2, and CFD-Post cannot read CFF written before 2020 R2. The 2019 R3 introduction date could not be confirmed.

topic: FE-library native mesh formats: MFEM mesh (v1.x, NC v1.0, v1.3), libMesh XDR/XDA + CheckpointIO, deal.II Triangulation, Netgen .vol
summary: These are application-driven formats built around the host library's in-memory mesh, not neutral IRs. MFEM is the most relevant: a small sectioned text spec with explicit versions (v1.0 conforming/high-order, v1.2 parallel, v1.3 named attribute sets, separate "MFEM NC mesh v1.0"). Its high-order geometry is a 'nodes' vector grid function in a named FE space, and nonconformity is stored as a refinement tree plus vertex_parents, with hanging faces derived at load time as master/slave lists with point matrices. libMesh XdrIO/CheckpointIO serialize the element tree (parent/child, remote_elem links) with version-gated features. deal.II has Boost-archive save/load of a Triangulation with a one-irregular hanging-node rule and no neutral on-disk spec. Netgen .vol is a keyword-block text format limited to tet/prism/pyramid/hex, with curved elements and CAD (u,v) parametric info. None supports arbitrary polyhedra and none is a generic IR. Pages were read via WebFetch (some summarized by a small model; libMesh Doxygen on mooseframework returned 403). Items not directly seen are marked unverified.
data_model: MFEM (mfem.org/mesh-format-v1.0, mesh-format-v1.x): text file, header 'MFEM mesh v1.0' (v1.3 adds named sets). Sections: 'dimension' d; 'elements' n, then lines '<attribute> <geom-type> <vertex ids...>'; 'boundary' n, lines '<bdr-attribute> <geom-type> <vertex ids>'; 'vertices' n (in v1.x only the count: vertices imply topology and coordinates are not used); 'nodes' = a serialized vector GridFunction with 'FiniteElementSpace', 'FiniteElementCollection: H1_2D_P2' (or L2_T1_2D_P1 for discontinuous/periodic), 'VDim: 2', 'Ordering: 1', then global dof values (vertex, edge, face, interior dofs). Geometry ids in the file comments: POINT=0, SEGMENT=1, TRIANGLE=2, SQUARE=3, TETRAHEDRON=4, CUBE=5 (prism/pyramid ids exist in code; unverified here). Attributes are positive ints (material/subdomain). Periodicity: vertices are topologically fused, geometry carried by a discontinuous L2 nodes space. In-memory adjacency tables (element-edge/face) are derived on demand (unverified: Connectivity page not fetched). NCMesh in memory (ncmesh.hpp): Node (Hashed2; vert_refc/edge_refc ref counts, vert_index, edge_index, scale), Element {geom, ref_type bitmask X/Y/Z, attribute, index (Mesh idx or -1 if refined), rank, union{node[8] | child[10]}, parent (-1 root, -2 freed)}, Face (Hashed4 keyed by 4 vertex nodes; attribute -1 internal; elem[2]). Edges and faces are implicit hash-table entries keyed by endpoint nodes.
polyhedra: None of the four supports arbitrary polygons/polyhedra. MFEM geometry is a fixed enum of reference cells. Netgen ELEMENT_TYPE (meshtype.hpp): SEGMENT=1, SEGMENT3=2, TRIG=10, QUAD=11, TRIG6=12, QUAD6=13, QUAD8=14, TET=20, TET10=21, PYRAMID=22, PRISM=23, PRISM12=24, HEX=25, HEX20=26, PRISM15=27, PYRAMID13=28, HEX7=29; ELEMENT_MAXPOINTS=20, ELEMENT2D_MAXPOINTS=8. libMesh Elem subclasses are fixed types (max_n_nodes=27). deal.II docs read do not mention polyhedra (ReferenceCell covers simplices/mixed). Cell types are enum-indexed reference cells everywhere; nothing models face-lists-per-cell.
nonconformal: MFEM NCMesh is the key reference. Nonconformity is stored as refinement history, not as two unimprinted faces: roots + per-element ref_type bitmask + child ids, plus 'vertex_parents' ('<vertex id> <parent1> <parent2>' with optional scale for anisotropic splits, default 0.5; every refinement-created vertex has exactly two parents; top-level vertices not listed). Hanging vertices have no stored coordinates ('coordinates' lists only top-level vertices, or 'nodes' for curved). File layout 'MFEM NC mesh v1.0': dimension; optional rank; elements (active: '<owner rank> <attribute> <geom> 0 <vertex ids>'; refined: '<owner rank> <attribute> <geom> <ref_type> <child ids>'); boundary; vertex_parents; optional root_state; coordinates|nodes; mfem_mesh_end (mfem.org/mesh-format-v1.0; ncmesh.cpp). Detection: NCMesh::BuildFaceList (3D) visits leaf faces; a face with elements on both sides goes to NCList.conforming; otherwise TraverseQuadFace/TraverseTriFace recurse down the tree from an identity point matrix, and if split sub-faces exist the face becomes a MASTER and the sub-faces SLAVES. NCList = {conforming MeshIds; masters with [slaves_begin,slaves_end); slaves {master idx, matrix idx into point_matrices[geom], edge_flags}}. Point matrices map slave reference coords into the master face frame, deduplicated by hash (MatrixMap::GetIndex); degenerate matrices handle tet/prism edge-face constraints. QuadFaceIsMaster/TriFaceIsMaster test midpoint-node existence; LimitNCLevel bounds level difference. The FE space builds a conforming prolongation from these constraints. Limitation: only element-hierarchy nonconformity; arbitrary mismatched interfaces (separately meshed parts, sliding/mortar) are not representable. libMesh: AMR tree with parent/child, active()/ancestor()/subactive(), neighbor pointers across levels; hanging-node constraints at DOF level (function names not verified from fetched pages). deal.II: has_hanging_nodes(); faces subdivided at most once (one-irregular); MeshSmoothing flags. Netgen .vol: conforming only; periodic/glue via 'identifications' block (point pairs + identification number + types/names).
sets_and_partitions: MFEM: integer 'attribute' per element and per boundary element; v1.3 adds 'attribute_sets' after elements and 'bdr_attribute_sets' after boundary, lines '"<name>" <count> <attr...>' (named, overlappable; domain and boundary numbers cannot mix in one set). Parallel: optional 'rank' section and per-element owner rank in NC files. libMesh: subdomain_id per Elem (children inherit), subdomain names; BoundaryInfo holds sideset (elem,side,id), nodeset, edge and shell-face BCs with names (XDR 0.9.2 names/nodesets, 1.1.0 edge/shell-face BCs). deal.II: material_id on cells (inherited by children), boundary_id on faces (internal faces get numbers::internal_face_boundary_id), subdomain_id for partitioning, manifold_id for geometry, one user flag + (user index or user pointer) per object. Netgen: per-volume-element 'index' (domain) with 'materials' name block; surface elements carry face descriptor (surfnr+1, bc property, domain in, domain out) with 'bcnames' and 'face_colours'/'face_transparencies' (RGB per face, close to colour-as-material idea).
high_order: MFEM is the best model: geometry is a vector GridFunction 'nodes' in any FE collection (H1_2D_P1/P2/P3, L2_T1 for discontinuous), so curvature is a field on the mesh and v1.x vertex coordinates are ignored; NURBS has a separate format (NCMesh has LoadVertexToKnotSpan); curved NC meshes use 'nodes' in place of 'coordinates'. libMesh: higher-order Elem types with extra nodes as Node pointers; p_level per element for p-refinement. deal.II: geometry via Manifold objects attached by manifold_id and Mapping classes at assembly; manifolds are not serialized. Netgen: TET10, PRISM15, HEX20 etc. plus curved-element data at the end of .vol (layout unverified); Element has only is_curved flag, no explicit order field.
parallel: MFEM: ParMesh; NC files carry 'rank' and per-element owner rank; NCMesh Element.rank supports ghosts; root_state affects leaf ordering for partitioning. libMesh CheckpointIO (checkpoint_io.h): XDR/XDA binary or ASCII, ids as largest_id_type, header uint64_t; versions 1.5 (extra integer data), 1.6 (runtime element topology), 1.7 (disjoint neighbor boundary pairs with translation); split files in directory '<name>-split<n>'; split_mesh(mesh, nsplits) and current_processor_ids()/current_n_processors() support M-to-N restarts; remote_elem links stored; elements written sorted by level. XdrIO has serial and parallel writers ('libMesh-0.7.0+ parallel'). deal.II: parallel::distributed::Triangulation (p4est) and shared; Boost-archive save/load (p4est details unverified). Netgen .vol is serial.
geometry_association: Weak except Netgen. Netgen (meshtype.hpp, meshclass.cpp Save): surface elements carry per-vertex PointGeomInfo {trignum (STL), u, v (OCC)}; segments carry EdgePointGeomInfo (PointGeomInfo + dist); face descriptors give surfnr, domin, domout (explicit volume/surface/region topology); .vol appends geometry after 'endmesh'; blocks 'surfaceelementsgi' (STL) / 'surfaceelementsuv' (OCC/ACIS) / 'surfaceelements' and 'edgesegmentsgi3' (gi2 is legacy, read only). deal.II: manifold_id on cells/faces/edges links to code-level Manifold objects (not serialized). MFEM and libMesh: only integer attributes/boundary ids; CAD association external.
spec_quality: MFEM best: public versioned prose spec on mfem.org (mesh-format-v1.0 page also hosts NC v1.0 and v1.3 sets), explicit loaders ('Load deprecated MFEM mesh v1.1 for backward compatibility', legacy NC v1.1 with coarse_elements replaced by NC v1.0). libMesh: no standalone spec; defined by xdr_io.C/checkpoint_io.h with version gates (XDR 0.9.2, 0.9.6, 1.1.0, 1.3.0 fixed 64-bit writes, 1.8.0 extra integers). deal.II: no neutral spec; Boost serialization tied to library version. Netgen: informal, defined by Mesh::Save/Load; keyword blocks mesh3d, dimension, geomtype, surfaceelements*, volumeelements, edgesegmentsgi3, points, identifications, materials, bcnames, face_colours, face_transparencies, endmesh.
storage: MFEM: text (optionally gzip), slow for large meshes. libMesh: XDR (portable binary) or ASCII, parallel split files. deal.II: Boost archives (binary/text); p4est distributed save details unverified. Netgen: plain text, coordinates in fixed 16-digit notation in 22-char fields. None uses a chunked random-access container (HDF5/netCDF).
database_like_aspects: Mostly implicit. MFEM stores minimal primary data (element->vertex, boundary->vertex) and derives edges/faces and adjacency tables on demand; NCMesh keeps edges/faces as hash-table entities keyed by endpoints (Hashed2/Hashed4) with reference counts, a lazily indexed entity store. Named attribute sets act like named selections. libMesh BoundaryInfo is effectively a relation table (element, side) -> ids and node -> ids separate from the cell array. Netgen face descriptors are a side table joining surface number, domain in/out, bc, colour. Common pattern: topology + attribute tables + derived adjacency, matching the geometry-database framing, but no one exposes a schema or query layer.
ecosystem: MFEM: C++ library with GLVis, PyMFEM, Gmsh import (physical tag -> attribute), used widely in LLNL codes. libMesh: C++ FE library underlying MOOSE; reads/writes Exodus, Gmsh, Nemesis, VTK; XDR/Checkpoint are internal restart formats. deal.II: C++ FE library with GridIn (Abaqus, UCD, Gmsh, Netgen, others; unverified list) and GridOut. Netgen/NGSolve: Python/C++, OCC geometry, .vol and neutral formats. None is a general-purpose IR; each is the serialization of its host library.
strengths: MFEM: versioned, sectioned, human-readable spec with extension points (v1.3 named sets) and backward-compatible loaders
MFEM: curvature as a field (nodes GridFunction in any FE collection), same mechanism for NURBS and discontinuous periodic geometry
MFEM NCMesh: stores minimal generative data (tree + vertex parents) and deterministically derives masters/slaves/point matrices; hanging vertices need no stored coordinates
MFEM NCList master/slave with deduplicated point matrices is a compact reusable interface-constraint representation
libMesh: separate boundary relation table with names; M-to-N split checkpoints with explicit remote_elem links
deal.II: separate material_id / boundary_id / subdomain_id / manifold_id make partition layers explicit
Netgen: face descriptor (surfnr, domin, domout, bc, colour) links surface mesh to geometry faces and regions on both sides; per-vertex CAD (u,v) parameters
weaknesses: No polygon/polyhedron support in any; cell types are a closed enum
Nonconformity limited to refinement-hierarchy hanging nodes; no arbitrary non-matching interfaces or mortar/sliding
Formats tied to host library in-memory model and version; not neutral
Text/XDR serialization; no chunked random-access container, poor for very large meshes
Weak or absent CAD association except Netgen; deal.II manifolds not serialized
Integer-only attributes for materials in MFEM until v1.3 name sets; no layered geometry/partition/mesh model
MFEM v1.x has two sources of coordinates (vertices ignored vs nodes), a surprising double-truth for readers
Netgen format informal; optional block order defined only by code
lessons_for_us: Adopt MFEM's high-order geometry as a field (nodes in a named basis/collection); keep linear vertex coordinates only as topology carrier and make the high-order field authoritative when present; avoid MFEM's duplicate-truth.
Adopt named, overlappable attribute sets for the partition layer (MFEM v1.3), but let sets be defined by B-rep entity references (volumes/faces) and by query, not only cell ids.

Represent non-conformal interfaces as explicit INTERFACE entities: master face set + slave face set + mapping (point matrices, or intersection polygons/weights for general overlap), modelled on NCList but generalized beyond refinement trees; this is 'imprinting at information level'. MFEM's derive-from-history approach cannot express arbitrary mismatches, so deliberately differ.

Keep generative history optional: store refinement tree / vertex_parents when the mesh came from AMR (cheap, deterministic), and also store explicit interface tables so consumers need not rebuild them.

Adopt Netgen's face-descriptor idea as the glue between layers: every boundary face carries (geometry face id, region on side A, region on side B, bc id, colour); add optional per-vertex/edge parametric (u,v,t) CAD coordinates.
Adopt libMesh-style boundary relation table (element, local side) -> ids, but key by stable face ids to avoid local-side-index fragility.
Deliberately differ on cell topology: face-list (cell->faces->edges->vertices with orientations) as primary polyhedral connectivity, with reference-cell enums as a cached fast path.

Deliberately differ on storage: chunked columnar container (HDF5/Zarr/Arrow-like) with version + required/optional feature flags header for random access and parallel partial reads; provide a human-readable text projection like MFEM for debugging.
Copy MFEM/libMesh numeric versions with per-feature gates and legacy loaders; add required-vs-optional feature flags so old readers fail safely.
Derive adjacency lazily (MFEM Table pattern) and treat edges/faces as hash-keyed entities; expose them as query views of the database-like IR.
Everything needed to reproduce geometry must live in the file (deal.II manifold pointers are lost on load).

corrections.claim: "None of the four supports arbitrary polygons/polyhedra" and "libMesh Elem subclasses are fixed types (max_n_nodes=27)"
corrections.correction: libMesh master has face-list polyhedra: enum_elem_type.h defines C0POLYGON = 39 ("arbitrary polygon with N EDGE2 sides") and C0POLYHEDRON = 40 ("arbitrary polyhedron with C0POLYGON sides"); cell_polyhedron.h (author Roy Stogner, 2025) builds a Polyhedron from a vector<shared_ptr<Polygon>> of pre-constructed faces, n_nodes() is runtime (_nodelinks_data.size()), Elem::runtime_topology() is a virtual hook. max_n_nodes=27 still exists but applies only to fixed-topology types. Status: Polygon added 2025-03-04, Polyhedron 2025-05-06 (git history); present in tag v1.9.0-rc2, absent (404) from v1.8.4, which is the current 'Latest' release. Caveats that matter for design: hierarchical refinement of polyhedra is "Not implemented ... indefinitely"; XDR/XDA cannot carry them (xdr_io.C: type_to_n_nodes_map == invalid_uint -> libmesh_not_implemented()); only CheckpointIO >= 1.6 ("runtime topology": n_nodes, n_sides, per-side node lists), ExodusII (NSIDED/NFACED blocks) and VTK (face stream) do.
corrections.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/include/enums/enum_elem_type.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/include/geom/cell_polyhedron.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/src/mesh/checkpoint_io.C ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/src/mesh/xdr_io.C ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/src/mesh/exodusII_io_helper.C ; GitHub commits API for include/geom/cell_c0polyhedron.h and face_c0polygon.h

corrections.claim: "legacy NC v1.1 with coarse_elements replaced by NC v1.0" and "vertex_parents ... with optional scale for anisotropic splits, default 0.5"
corrections.correction: Three distinct headers exist in mesh.cpp Loader (lines 5123-5132): "MFEM mesh v1.1" is the LEGACY NC format (v1.0 + vertex_parents + optional coarse_elements, CHANGELOG 'new version(1.1)'); "MFEM NC mesh v1.0" replaced it (CHANGELOG: fixes inconsistencies of legacy v1.1, works in serial and parallel); "MFEM NC mesh v1.1" is a NEWER variant emitted by NCMesh::Print only when using_scaling is true. The scale is not optional per line: LoadVertexParents reads 'id p1 p2' and then 's' iff the header is NC v1.1. The mfem.org NC v1.0 spec shows only '<vertex> <parent1> <parent2>'. Legacy 'MFEM mesh v1.1' cannot be loaded into a ParMesh.

corrections.claim: deal.II GridIn supports "Abaqus, UCD, Gmsh, Netgen, others"
corrections.correction: GridIn::Format enum is: Default, unv, ucd, abaqus, dbmesh, xda, msh, tecplot, vtk, vtu, assimp, exodusii (plus read_comsol_mphtxt). There is no Netgen reader. GridIn also states the input 'must not contain hanging nodes' or internal cracks result, i.e. deal.II has no interchange representation for non-conforming meshes at all.

corrections.claim: deal.II: "Boost-archive save/load of a Triangulation" / "parallel::distributed::Triangulation (p4est) ... Boost-archive save/load (p4est details unverified)"
corrections.correction: Boost serialization applies to the serial Triangulation (stores vertices, connectivity, boundary/subdomain/material ids; NOT signals or Manifold pointers). parallel::distributed::Triangulation::save/load is a different mechanism: p4est writes 'a number of files' with the given basename prefix on a shared filesystem; load requires 'the same coarse mesh that was used in save()' but 'you do not need to load with the same number of MPI processes' (it repartitions). p::d::Triangulation 'does not support anisotropic refinement, because it relies on the p4est library'. Cell data survives only if registered via register_data_attach().

corrections.claim: Netgen .vol: "plain text"; "curved-element data at the end of .vol (layout unverified)"
corrections.correction: Mesh::Save(path): '.vol.bin' -> BinaryOutArchive; '.vol.gz' -> gzip stream; only an exact '.vol' extension yields plain text; any other name gets '.vol.gz' appended. Curved data is a named 'curvedelements' block written via Archive serialization of CurvedElements (only when IsHighOrder()), located BEFORE 'endmesh'; geometry is appended AFTER 'endmesh' via geometry->SaveToMeshFile. Blocks omitted by the report: pointelements, cd2names, edgedescriptors, singular_points/singular_edge_left/right/singular_face_inside/outside. Coordinate claim (precision 16, fixed, width 22) is confirmed.

corrections.claim: Geometry ids: "POINT=0 ... CUBE=5 (prism/pyramid ids exist in code; unverified here)"
corrections.correction: Confirmed from geom.hpp: enum Type { INVALID=-1, POINT=0, SEGMENT, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, TETRAHEDRON, CUBE, PRISM, PYRAMID } i.e. PRISM=6, PYRAMID=7. The mfem.org v1.0 page lists PRISM=6 as well; PYRAMID is only in code. NCMesh::CheckSupportedGeom accepts segment, triangle, square, cube, prism, pyramid, tetrahedron.

corrections.claim: "Nonconformity limited to refinement-hierarchy hanging nodes; no arbitrary non-matching interfaces or mortar/sliding" (as a statement about MFEM)
corrections.correction: True of the FILE FORMATS, but MFEM the library has runtime non-matching mechanisms that are never in the mesh file: ParMortarAssembler via ParMoonolith ('parallel non-conforming, non-matching, variational, volumetric mesh information transfer ... between arbitrarily distributed and unrelated finite element meshes'), Tribol mortar-based contact constraints (contact miniapp, MFEM 4.10), and SubMesh/TransferMap. I.e. in MFEM the interface is detected/intersected at solve time, not stored.

corrections.claim: Netgen FaceDescriptor is a struct with surfnr, bcprop, domin, domout
corrections.correction: In current meshtype.hpp FaceDescriptor is an alias for FaceRegion = Region<2>; members: surfnr, domin, domout, tlosurf, bcprop, surfcolour (Vec<4>), firstelement, domin_singular, domout_singular; the bc name lives in base RegionBase. Netgen now has a unified per-dimension Region<N> table (faces, edges via 'edgedescriptors', 'cd2names'), which is closer to the user's layered-database framing than the report conveys.

corrections.claim: "MFEM mesh v1.2 parallel" (described only as adding parallel meshes)
corrections.correction: Mesh::Print writes 'MFEM mesh v1.2' by default even for serial meshes (v1.0 only under a legacy flag; v1.3 when attribute sets exist). v1.2's mechanism is the mandatory 'mfem_mesh_end' tag so a ParMesh section can follow; the parallel section (pmesh.cpp) has 'communication_groups', 'total_shared_vertices/edges/faces', then per-group 'shared_vertices', 'shared_edges', 'shared_faces'. CHANGELOG at v1.2 introduction: NC meshes 'currently supported only in serial' (later fixed by NC mesh v1.0).

missing_important: libMesh is the one FE library in this set with first-class face-list polyhedra (C0Polygon/C0Polyhedron, 2025, v1.9.0-rc only) and it exposes exactly the design tension the user cares about: the native XDR format cannot serialize them, CheckpointIO had to add a 'runtime topology' record (n_nodes, n_sides, per-side node lists) in version 1.6, ExodusII maps them to NSIDED/NFACED, and h-refinement of polyhedra is declared 'not implemented ... indefinitely'. A closed cell-type enum plus a fixed node-count table is the thing that breaks; smart-mesh's face-list-primary connectivity avoids this.

MFEM NC meshes do NOT enforce 2:1 level balance by default; LimitNCLevel(max_nc_level) is an optional post-step. deal.II/p4est enforce one-irregularity always (GridIn additionally refuses hanging nodes). This is a real axis of difference between the two refinement-history representations.

MFEM 4.10 (released Sep 1, 2026) added 'MFEM NURBS NC-patch mesh v1.0': element-wise conforming but nonconforming PATCH topology (plus 'MFEM NURBS mesh v1.1'). It is a third flavor of nonconformity in MFEM alongside AMR hanging nodes and runtime mortar transfer.

MFEM has an in-format non-conformity story (NC file + NCMesh master/slave) and a runtime-only one (ParMoonolith/ParMortarAssembler volumetric intersection transfer; Tribol mortar contact). For the user's question 'how is a non-conformal interface detected so the solver can project': in MFEM the file never says; the library intersects the meshes at assembly time.

MFEM current version is 4.10 (Sep 2026; 4.9 Dec 2025, 4.8 Apr 2025, 4.7 May 2024, 4.6 Sep 2023). Named attribute sets (format v1.3) arrived in 4.7 (May 2024), not 4.6. libMesh 'Latest' release is v1.8.4 with v1.9.0-rc2 both dated Oct 06; polyhedra are in the rc only.

Netgen FaceDescriptor/Region<2>/RegionBase: Netgen now keeps a per-dimension region table (faces: surfnr, domin, domout, tlosurf, bcprop, surfcolour; edges: 'edgedescriptors'; codim-2 names: 'cd2names') and the FaceDescriptor is referenced from each surface element as an index. This is the closest existing analogue of the user's 'partition layer joined to the mesh layer by a side table' and should be the stated baseline for the glue-table idea.

Netgen Save supports three containers from one API: '.vol' text, '.vol.gz' (default when the extension is anything else), and '.vol.bin' via BinaryOutArchive (the same Archive serialization that handles the 'curvedelements' block and Python pickling).

deal.II also has parallel::fullydistributed::Triangulation (built from a TriangulationDescription::Description, supports pre-refined/hanging-node coarse meshes without a p4est forest) and parallel::shared::Triangulation; the report lists only distributed and shared.
libMesh CheckpointIO version 1.7 text says only 'disjoint neighbor boundary pairs'; the report's 'with translation' qualifier is not in the fetched header and should be treated as unverified.

topic: Database-native and columnar approaches to meshes (Arrow/Parquet/GeoArrow, DuckDB/SQLite, ECS, OpenVolumeMesh, CGAL CMap/LCC, Topologic, Mangrove, MOAB/HDF5)
summary: No mainstream, versioned, specified mesh format is columnar- or relational-native. I found no evidence of Arrow/Parquet/DuckDB-based meshes for FEM/CFD/transport (my searches for it returned nothing). The database-like ideas that actually exist are: (a) MOAB, a mesh "database" API with entities, handles, sets and tags, stored in HDF5 (.h5m) and read in parallel up to 16K processes; (b) OpenVolumeMesh (RWTH, IMR 2012), an index-based half-face structure for heterogeneous 3D polytopal complexes with a property system; (c) the topological-data-structure literature (CGAL combinatorial maps/LCC, Mangrove TDS, IA*) that stores only a subset of relations and derives the rest on demand; (d) Topologic, a non-manifold B-rep-style hierarchy on OpenCASCADE. GeoArrow shows how to lay out ragged geometry columnarly (offset buffers, struct-of-arrays coordinates) but has no volumetric or mesh types, and DuckDB spatial is 2D-only. The practical takeaway: a "database IR" is best realised as a logical relational schema (entities, relations, attributes/tags, sets) with a columnar physical layout (CSR offset+index arrays, SoA coordinates), not as an actual SQL engine in the hot path. That combination is not offered by an existing spec, so it is a legitimate gap. Several details below could not be fetched (OVM docs and paper hit ECONNRESET/Anubis) and are marked unverified.
data_model:
OpenVolumeMesh: per the paper abstract (HAL hal-00762280 via search snippet), 3D polytopal complexes with top-down incidences stored in arrays and accessed by index handles; each face is a pair of oriented half-faces, each half-face is defined by its incident half-edges, each cell by its set of half-faces; entities are shared, not duplicated per valence; can represent non-manifolds with little overhead. Vertex-to-edge, edge-to-face etc. are derived on demand, and local adjacency is not stored per half-edge (OpenFlipper docs snippet). Properties (attributes) attach per entity type. Exact C++ class names (VertexHandle, EdgeHandle, HalfFaceHandle, CellHandle) are from memory: unverified.
CGAL Combinatorial_map: the only element is the dart; d+1 pointers beta_0..beta_d (beta_0 = inverse of beta_1; beta_2..beta_d are involutions); i-cells are orbits of darts under all betas except beta_i; attributes attach to cells and dart refers to its cell attribute, with merge/split functors; handles are indices or pointers; only orientable quasi-manifolds (no two cells sharing only a vertex, no partial face gluing); generalised maps need roughly 2x the darts but allow non-orientable; Linear_cell_complex adds a point per vertex (https://doc.cgal.org/latest/Combinatorial_map/index.html).
MOAB: four types: Interface instance, Entities (referenced by handles, not pointers), Sets (contain entities and other sets, with separate parent/child links), Tags (named, fixed size/type: int, double, handle, opaque; on mesh, entities or sets). h5m layout: HDF5 group /tstt with subgroups nodes, elements, sets, tags; node coordinates are a dataset; each element type group has a connectivity dataset; sets store list/contents/parents/children; tags store type, id list, values; positive unique integer IDs, optional max_id attribute.
GeoArrow v0.2: Polygon = List<List<Coordinate>>, one offset buffer per nesting level; coordinates either separated Struct<x,y,[z,[m]]> (recommended) or interleaved FixedSizeList; mixed types via dense union with WKB type ids; bbox as Struct. 
Topologic: Topology superclass with Vertex, Edge, Wire, Face, Shell, Cell, CellComplex, Cluster (any nesting), built on OpenCASCADE 7.8 (AGPL-3.0).
Mangrove TDS / IA*: IA* encodes only top simplices plus a subset of adjacency relations, for manifold, non-manifold and non-regular simplicial complexes in any dimension; Mangrove expresses any structure as a graph of relations ("a mangrove").
ECS (Flecs/Unity DOTS/EnTT): archetype ECS stores entities with the same component set in dense columnar tables/chunks; sparse-set ECS keeps a dense array per component plus a sparse id-to-index map. No source found applying this to meshes; the mapping nodes/cells/faces as entities with SoA components is my design inference, not an existing practice.
polyhedra: OpenVolumeMesh: first-class heterogeneous polyhedral cells, defined as a set of half-faces, each bounded by half-edges (from paper abstract). CGAL CMap/LCC: arbitrary polyhedra expressible as darts but restricted to orientable quasi-manifold; no hanging-face gluing. Topologic: Cell bounded by Shell of arbitrary Faces, CellComplex shares faces between cells. MOAB: has polygon and polyhedron entity types (from memory, unverified), stored with variable-length connectivity. GeoArrow: no polyhedral or volumetric types (confirmed on format page); polygon rings only. Columnar suggestion for us: cell->face CSR (offsets + face_ids with orientation sign bit) and face->node CSR; same layout as Arrow ListArray offsets/values, so Arrow-compatible by construction.
nonconformal: None of these structures models non-conformal interfaces natively. CGAL maps explicitly forbid partial face gluing (a cell glued to part of another cell's face), so a non-conformal mesh cannot be a valid map without imprinting/splitting first. OpenVolumeMesh and Topologic are conformal complexes in which faces are shared; non-conformality would be an extra layer (unverified that OVM has any). MOAB handles it only through tags/sets by convention (unverified). Implication for us: represent non-conformal interfaces as an explicit relation table, e.g. a Mortar/Interface entity set linking face A to face B with overlap segments (area, projection), rather than as an absence of sharing. This makes detection cheap (a face with no neighbour and an entry in the interface table) and keeps "imprinting" (information-level merge) distinct from physical conformalization.
sets_and_partitions: MOAB is the strongest precedent: Sets (can nest, with parent/child links distinct from containment) plus Tags (typed key-value on mesh/entity/set) express blocks, materials, boundary sets and CAD association uniformly; Exodus-style blocks/sidesets/nodesets are conventions on top (convention names from memory, unverified). CGAL attributes attach per cell via dart, so a region label is an attribute on the 3-cell. OpenVolumeMesh uses per-entity properties. Topologic's Cluster is a free nesting grouping. For our three layers (geometry B-rep, partition/material, mesh): model the partition layer as sets over geometry entities, and the mesh layer as sets/tags over mesh entities, with an explicit "origin" association table from mesh entity to geometry entity, as in MOAB-style tags that reference entity handles.
strengths: MOAB proves the 'mesh as database' idea at scale: entities + handles + sets + tags on HDF5 with parallel reads reported to 16K processors (sigma.mcs.anl.gov/moab-library).
Index-based, array-stored incidence (OpenVolumeMesh, CGAL index handles) is cache-friendly and serialises trivially.
Storing only a minimal relation subset and deriving the rest on demand (IA*, OVM top-down incidences) trades memory for compute and is consistent with a 'relations as tables' view.
Arrow/GeoArrow layouts give a ready, language-neutral zero-copy layout (offset buffers, separated coordinate columns) readable from Rust, C++, Python without a custom parser.
Dimension-independent models (CGAL maps, Mangrove, Topologic CellComplex) cover non-manifold or multi-dimensional entities in one framework.
Typed property/tag systems let new data (metrics, materials, solver fields) be added without changing the core schema.
weaknesses: No existing columnar/relational mesh spec: GeoArrow has no volumetric or polyhedral types and DuckDB spatial's GEOMETRY has no Z/M or 3D mesh support and is described as early-stage.

Parquet and generic SQL are poor for random, pointer-chasing adjacency queries; a column scan wins on bulk analytics, not on neighbour traversal. A Geant4 forum thread warns that columnar layout hurts event-by-event access unless buffered (analogous to cell-by-cell mesh algorithms).
CGAL combinatorial maps only represent orientable quasi-manifolds and cannot represent partial gluing, so unsuitable as-is for non-conformal or general non-manifold CAD-derived meshes.
Darts cost memory (generalised maps about 2x darts) and are conceptually heavy for solver developers.
MOAB's file layout is documented in API docs/wiki, but I found no formal versioned spec; OVM has no file-format standard I could verify.
Topologic is AEC/B-rep oriented, AGPL-3.0, depends on OpenCASCADE, and is not designed for million-cell meshes (unverified performance).
ECS-for-meshes has no found precedent; archetype moves cost copies when component sets change.
lessons_for_us: Adopt a two-level IR: a logical relational schema (entity tables: Vertex, Edge, Face, Cell, plus relation tables, Set tables, Tag/attribute columns, Association tables) and a physical columnar layout (CSR offsets+values, SoA coordinates). This is 'database-like' where it matters (schema, queries, adjacency derivable on demand) without an SQL engine in the hot path.

Use Arrow-compatible buffers (offset arrays + flat values, separated x/y/z) as the in-memory and mmap-able on-disk layout, so Python/DuckDB/pandas can read it zero-copy for analysis, while a Rust API provides handle-based traversal. Parquet can be an optional interchange/archival export, not the native format (my judgment, not sourced).

Copy MOAB's tag + set + handle triad as the extensibility mechanism: sets can nest, tags are typed and can hold entity handles; materials, boundary conditions, geometry associations and partition membership are all sets/tags rather than special fields.

Make the three layers separate sets of tables joined by explicit association tables (mesh entity -> partition region -> geometry entity), with each layer independently versioned; the partition layer references geometry ids, never copies geometry.

Store only primary relations (cell->face, face->node, with orientation bits, as in OVM's half-face idea) and compute inverse relations (node->cell, face->cells) lazily or as cached optional tables; mark which derived tables are materialised in the file header.

Deliberately differ from CGAL maps: allow non-manifold and partial gluing, because non-conformal interfaces are a requirement; model them as explicit Interface/mortar relation entities rather than forcing imprinting.
Handle ids: stable, typed, index-based u32/u64 with a per-entity-type id space (OVM/CGAL), plus MOAB-style persistent IDs in the file so partial reads and ghosting remain consistent.
Treat ECS as an implementation analogy only: our 'components' are typed attribute columns keyed by entity id; avoid archetype migration, since mesh entities rarely change component sets.
Define a formal, versioned schema with conformance tests from day one; none of the surveyed systems did, and that is a concrete advantage over MOAB/OVM as a baseline.
sources: https://hal-univ-tlse3.archives-ouvertes.fr/INRIA/hal-00762280 (access denied on fetch; abstract via search snippet only)
database_like_aspects: Most database-like: MOAB (entity handles, sets, typed tags, queries by tag/type, HDF5 tables per entity type). CGAL attributes and OVM properties act like columns keyed by entity. IA*/Mangrove treat topology as a set of relations of which only a subset is stored, the rest derived (like views). Gaps: I found no system with a declared schema language, query language, or indexes over mesh relations; DuckDB/SQLite spatial support only 2D geometry (stated in DuckDB docs), so volumetric topology would have to be plain integer tables. Adjacency-on-demand is the closest analogue to materialised views.
ecosystem: MOAB: DOE SIGMA project (Argonne), used by DAGMC/CAD-based neutronics and MeshKit; h5m is its native format. CGAL: widely used C++ library (combinatorial maps and LCC). OpenVolumeMesh: C++ library from RWTH Aachen, used in OpenFlipper. Topologic: C++/Python (pybind11) with topologicpy, AEC users, AGPL-3.0. Mangrove TDS: C++ research library on SourceForge. GeoArrow/Arrow: broad bindings (Rust, C++, Python) in geospatial; DuckDB spatial reads GDAL formats. ParaView/VTK compatibility for these is not verified in this research.
geometry_association: MOAB links mesh to geometry through sets plus tags (typical CAD-linked meshes tag sets with geometry dimension and id; DAGMC uses this, from memory, unverified) and through parent/child set links forming volume-surface-curve hierarchies. CGAL attributes and OVM properties could carry a geometry id but have no native B-rep notion. Topologic is B-rep native (OpenCASCADE shapes) so geometry and topology coincide. Pattern to copy: an explicit association table from mesh entity to geometry entity (dimension + id), not a field baked into elements.
high_order: Not addressed by any source I verified: CGAL maps and OVM are topological (linear LCC points only, straight edges per CGAL docs), GeoArrow is linear. MOAB higher-order support (extra mid-nodes in connectivity) is from memory, unverified. For us: keep topology separate from a per-cell 'geometry map' attribute (node count, basis type, optionally curved-edge/face parameterisation) stored as tag/column, so high-order stays a property layer and not a topology change.
parallel: MOAB: parallel HDF5 read, with parallel loading reported to 16K processors (sigma.mcs.anl.gov/moab-library); ghosting/shared-entity handling is in MOAB's ParallelComm (from memory, unverified). SeisSol (unstructured-mesh seismic code) reports HDF5+MPI-IO write bandwidth rising from 832 MiB/s to 6.7 GiB/s with aggregation on 2048 nodes (TUM portal snippet), evidence that HDF5-style chunked columnar datasets work for large mesh-related output. Parquet row groups and column chunks (third-party description) suit partition-per-row-group layout, but I did not find a mesh code that does it. OVM/CGAL/Topologic: no distributed support found (unverified). Our design should store per-partition tables plus global-id and owner-rank columns and a ghost-layer relation table.
spec_quality: Weak across the board. GeoArrow has a real versioned spec (v0.2 format page) but it is not for meshes. MOAB documents the h5m layout via Doxygen/wiki and version numbers (5.5.1/5.6.0 docs) but I found no standalone formal spec. OVM has a paper and API docs, no file-format spec verified. CGAL maps are rigorously defined mathematically but in-memory only. Topologic has no stated version in its repo page. Arrow/Parquet have formal specs but not mesh schemas.

corrections.claim: MOAB h5m 'read in parallel up to 16K processes' (summary, strengths, parallel), attributed to sigma.mcs.anl.gov/moab-library
corrections.correction: The cited sigma page could not be retrieved (HTTP 403, also via curl); the Bitbucket README (same project text) gives no processor count. The only source mentioning 16K is a Jan-2014 petsc-dev post saying MOAB parallel HDF5 I/O was 'iffy above ~16k procs and 32M-64M hex/tet elements'; a 2013 MOAB-dev Blue Gene thread reports reads scaling 'up to 8k mpi processors' only after ROMIO hint tuning, and a 2015 thread shows a 30M-node load hanging 45 min on 500 ranks until the file was reordered by partition (mbpart -R). Treat 16K as a dated pain threshold, not a demonstrated ceiling; file ordering dominates MOAB parallel read performance.

corrections.claim: DuckDB spatial is 2D-only; 'GEOMETRY has no Z/M or 3D' and is 'early-stage' (summary, weaknesses, database_like_aspects)
corrections.correction: That text comes from the 2023-era extension page. Current docs: GEOMETRY is a built-in core DuckDB type since DuckDB 1.5 with Z, M and ZM vertex dimensions (consistent per geometry), CRS as a type parameter, 7 OGC types. Still true and design-relevant: no POLYHEDRALSURFACE/TIN/volumetric types, binary storage format 'not yet stabilized', most ST_ functions still need the spatial extension. Conclusion (volumetric topology would be plain integer tables) stands.

corrections.claim: 'DuckDB/SQLite spatial support only 2D geometry' (database_like_aspects)
corrections.correction: The SQLite half was never checked. Indirect evidence (GDAL ticket #4877, FME docs) shows SpatiaLite 4.x stores XYZ, XYM and XYZM geometries. Neither engine has volumetric/mesh types, which is the point that matters.

corrections.claim: OpenVolumeMesh: 'Vertex-to-edge, edge-to-face etc. are derived on demand'
corrections.correction: README: bottom-up incidences are optional, 'computed explicitly' and maintained, and 'can be disabled to reduce memory use'. They are cached inverse tables you switch on/off, not lazily derived per query.

corrections.claim: OpenVolumeMesh 'can represent non-manifolds with little overhead'
corrections.correction: The 2012 IMR abstract does say non-manifold meshes 'without heavy overhead', but the current README states 'Manifold volumetric meshes' with 'limited support for non-manifold configurations', self-adjacent entities supported, exact allowed configurations marked TODO. Do not plan on OVM-style structures for general CAD-derived non-manifold meshes without defining the allowed configurations yourself.

corrections.claim: 'OVM has no file-format standard I could verify' / 'no file-format spec verified' (weaknesses, spec_quality)
corrections.correction: OVM ships two native formats: .ovm (ASCII, 'OVM ASCII' header, Vertices/Edges/Faces/Polyhedra sections) and .ovmb (binary, recommended, supports custom property (de)serialization), plus .vtk export. Correct residual point: there is no standalone official spec (a ParaView thread notes this; a meshio fork reads .ovm). License is LGPL v3.

corrections.claim: OVM handle class names 'from memory: unverified'; orientation proposed as a 'sign bit'
corrections.correction: Verified in Handles.hh: VertexHandle/VH, EdgeHandle/EH, HalfEdgeHandle/HEH, FaceHandle/FH, HalfFaceHandle/HFH, CellHandle/CH, MeshHandle/MH, all wrapping a signed int (-1 = invalid). Orientation is a parity bit, not a sign bit: half-face of face i is 2i or 2i+1, face = idx/2, opposite = idx ^ 1. This is the cheaper encoding for a CSR cell->face table.

corrections.claim: MOAB 'has polygon and polyhedron entity types (from memory, unverified), stored with variable-length connectivity'
corrections.correction: Verified, with a design-relevant detail: MBPOLYHEDRON connectivity is a list of FACE handles (MBPOLYGON or fixed 2D types), not node handles; MOAB does no planarity/orientation checks and intentionally allows duplicate faces with identical connectivity. In h5m, poly groups store a concatenated ID list plus a 'poly_indices' end-index dataset (CSR with end offsets); polyhedron IDs are face IDs, polygon IDs are node IDs. Adjacency for polyhedra has open bug reports (#117, #133).

corrections.claim: MOAB tag types: 'int, double, handle, opaque'; h5m layout details 'from memory'
corrections.correction: Verified layout: root '/tstt/' with nodes/coordinates, elements/<type>/connectivity, sets/{list,contents,children,parents}, tags/<name>/{id_list,values,var_indices}, attributes start_id/max_id, element_type, is_handle, variable_length. Set metadata row = [contents_end, children_end, parents_end, flags]; flags 0x1 owner, 0x2 unique, 0x4 ordered, 0x8 range-compressed contents. Tag storage classes: sparse, dense (one table per element group), and BIT tags (omitted in report); dense tags align row-for-row with the entity table. Range-compressed set contents and the owner/ordered flags are directly reusable for a sets-as-tables design.

corrections.claim: MOAB geometry association via tags 'from memory, unverified'; Exodus convention names 'from memory, unverified'; higher-order 'from memory, unverified'
corrections.correction: All verified. Geometry: each CAD vertex/edge/face/volume is an entity set tagged GEOM_DIMENSION (int), GLOBAL_ID, CATEGORY (32-char string), linked by parent/child set relations; GEOM_SENSE_2 on a surface set holds two handles (forward volume, reverse volume; same volume twice if non-manifold in one volume) and GEOM_SENSE_N_ENTS/GEOM_SENSE_N_SENSES for curves. Sets contain only mesh entities they own (a FACE set excludes vertices owned by bounding EDGEs). Exodus mapping: MATERIAL_SET = element block, DIRICHLET_SET = nodeset, NEUMANN_SET = sideset; HAS_MID_NODES is int[4] indexed by dimension; MOAB README states quadratic elements supported. GEOM_SENSE_2 is a ready model for the partition layer's 'material on each side of a surface' relation.
corrections.source: https://web.cels.anl.gov/projects/sigma/docs/moab/metadata.html (via search snippets; page 403 on direct fetch) ; https://web.cels.anl.gov/projects/sigma/docs/moab/MBTagConventions_8hpp.html ; https://bitbucket.org/fathomteam/moab/raw/master/README.md

corrections.claim: 'That combination [logical relational schema + columnar CSR physical layout] is not offered by an existing spec, so it is a legitimate gap' and 'Columnar suggestion for us: cell->face CSR ... face->node CSR'
corrections.correction: Overstated. The proposed physical layout is already the de facto standard for polyhedral meshes in versioned specs: VTKHDF >= 2.5 (HDF5; Connectivity/Offsets/Types plus FaceConnectivity/FaceOffsets/PolyhedronToFaces/PolyhedronOffsets, one oriented face shareable by several polyhedra, per-partition NumberOf* arrays, temporal offsets; changelog at 2.7), CGNS NGON_n/NFACE_n with ElementStartOffset (face->node and cell->face CSR, optional ParentElements face->cell), MOAB h5m poly_indices, OpenFOAM polyMesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour: face->node CSR plus face->cell pair, faces oriented owner->neighbour), Exodus nfaced/nsided face blocks. The real gap is narrower: a declared logical schema, typed sets/tags, CAD association, a first-class non-conformal relation, and Arrow-buffer compatibility in one spec.

corrections.claim: 'None of these structures models non-conformal interfaces natively' and the proposal to 'represent non-conformal interfaces as an explicit relation table ... rather than as an absence of sharing' is presented as a differentiator
corrections.correction: True for the surveyed set, but the proposed pattern has spec-level prior art: CGNS GridConnectivity_t type Abutting (mismatched) for any zone type, with CellListDonor + InterpolantsDonor (full), CellListDonor only (partial), or ZoneDonorName only (minimal); PointListDonor is restricted to Abutting1to1. OpenFOAM Foundation NCC declares coupled patches as nonConformalCyclic with zero faces in the boundary file and materializes faces at run time from the intersection (exactly 'absence of sharing + explicit declaration'). Differentiation must be stated relative to these.

corrections.claim: Topologic 'has no stated version in its repo page'
corrections.correction: Confirmed no GitHub Releases, but the repo has tags; AGPL-3.0 and OpenCASCADE 7.8 dependency confirmed; CellComplex is explicitly non-manifold; Python wheels via pybind11 for 3.8-3.14.

corrections.claim: CGAL combinatorial maps: 'beta_2..beta_d are involutions; only orientable quasi-manifolds; no partial face gluing; generalised maps need roughly 2x the darts; handles are indices or pointers'
corrections.correction: All confirmed by the CGAL manual; one precision: handles are the default (Compact_container), indices are opt-in via Use_index=Tag_true with std::uint32_t default. Attribute OnMerge keeps the first attribute and removes the second; OnSplit duplicates. No correction to substance.

corrections.claim: GeoArrow v0.2 details (Polygon = List<List<Coordinate>>, separated Struct recommended, union with WKB type ids, bbox Struct)
corrections.correction: Confirmed (format version 0.2 is current). Precision: union type ids equal WKB only for 2D (1-7); Z/M/ZM add 10/20/30 (WKB-conceptual, must be < 128); GeometryCollection is List<DenseUnion> with no recursive collections; WKB/WKT serialized encodings also allowed (Binary/BinaryView, Utf8/Utf8View). No mesh/volumetric types confirmed.

missing_important: PETSc DMPlex is the strongest existing 'mesh as relational/graph database' precedent and is absent from the report: every entity (vertex, edge, face, cell) is a 'point' in one consecutive numbering with each dimension a contiguous stratum; cone (downward) and support (upward) relations stored as CSR-style arrays; purely topological, with PetscSection mapping points to data offsets; cones ordered, supports unordered when auto-symmetrized. Non-conformal meshes are supported natively via a tree (parent/child point) structure plus a 'reference tree' describing allowed interface types (Isaac & Knepley 2015, arXiv:1508.02470), used to convert p4est forests. Parallel HDF5 I/O exists (arXiv:2004.08729). Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02470 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.08729

OpenFOAM fork caveat for any statement about AMI: the Foundation (openfoam.org) fork removed AMI/ACMI after v10 (July 2022) in favour of NCC (nonConformalCyclic, released 18 May 2022); the ESI fork (openfoam.com) still ships cyclicAMI/ACMI (api.openfoam.com v2512), with Aguerre et al. 2017 supermesh method and optional createAMIFaces 1-to-1 topology update. Sources: https://cfd.direct/openfoam/free-software/using-non-conformal-coupling/ ; https://api.openfoam.com/2512/cyclicAMIPolyPatch_8H_source.html

CGNS non-conformal interpolation gap worth targeting: InterpolantsDonor is defined only for linear BAR_2, TRI_3, QUAD_4, TETRA_4, PYRA_5, PENTA_6, HEXA_8 donors, i.e. no spec-level support for polyhedral or high-order donor cells at a non-matching interface. GridConnectivity1to1_t is structured-only; unstructured 1-to-1 must use GridConnectivity_t/Abutting1to1 with PointList/PointListDonor. Source: https://cgns.org/standard/SIDS/multizone.html

VTKHDF (Kitware, HDF5, versioned 2.x) already combines: polyhedra by faces, per-partition NumberOf* arrays for parallel reads, temporal appends with Steps offsets, and point/cell data arrays. Polyhedron support added in 2.5; current changelog 2.7. It is the closest existing 'versioned columnar polyhedral mesh file' and should be the export target and the baseline for the 'conceptually similar to X' statement. Source: https://docs.vtk.org/en/latest/vtk_file_formats/vtkhdf_file_format/vtkhdf_specifications.html

Exodus II supports arbitrary polyhedra via nfaced element blocks referencing faces in nsided (or fixed-type) face blocks by file-implicit face id; faces may come from any face block (not one per element block); the Exodus lead describes this capability as sparsely documented (ParaView issue 16062, VTK MR 2187). Source: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/issues/16062

MFEM has a native non-conforming mesh format ('MFEM NC mesh v1.0', with vertex_parents and coarse_elements sections in later versions; hanging vertex stored with parent edge/face as a vertex pair). Existence confirmed via NCMesh class docs; exact section layout per version not verified. Source: https://docs.mfem.org/4.5/ncmesh_8hpp_source.html

MOAB h5m parallel read performance depends on element ordering in the file matching the partition (mbpart -R reorder) and on the PARALLEL_PARTITION set convention used to build HDF5 hyperslab selections per rank; store cells partition-contiguous if partial reads matter. Sources: https://lists.mcs.anl.gov/pipermail/moab-dev/2015/007164.html ; https://bssw.io/items/experiences-with-the-scalable-integration-of-moab-and-visit

SeisSol I/O figures confirmed (Rettenberger & Bader, IEEE Cluster 2015): 832 MiB/s to 6.7 GiB/s with aggregation on 2048 SuperMUC nodes, meshes > 1 billion cells, mesh init in 35 s from their optimized mesh format. Source: https://portal.fis.tum.de/en/publications/optimizing-io-for-petascale-seismic-simulations-on-unstructured-m/

Report sections never reached a primary source and should stay flagged: OVM paper body (only bib/abstract via search), sigma.mcs.anl.gov MOAB pages (403), DuckDB spatial function list (ST_Z etc. unverified), CGNS NFACE_n orientation-by-sign convention (not confirmed), ECS-for-meshes claims (unchecked, low design impact).

topic: Polyhedral meshing and formats in practice (OpenFOAM, Fluent, Code_Saturne, libMesh/MOOSE, OpenMC, CGNS, Exodus, VTK, meshio)
summary: Solvers that treat polyhedra as first-class (OpenFOAM, Code_Saturne, Fluent/STAR-CCM+) all converge on a face-based (half-edge-free) topology: points, faces as ordered vertex lists, and a face-to-cell owner/neighbour pair. Cells are derived, not stored as primary entities. Of the interchange formats, only CGNS (NGON_n/NFACE_n) is a formal, versioned, standard way to carry polyhedra losslessly; Exodus has face blocks/NFACED but is poorly specified for it and rarely supported by readers; VTK has VTK_POLYHEDRON. meshio is the de-facto Python hub, but its polyhedron support is a stub (ragged lists, no sets/zones semantics beyond flat arrays). The Monte Carlo/transport consumers I checked (OpenMC unstructured mesh via MOAB/libMesh) accept only linear tets/hexes, and MOOSE/libMesh has only a recent, limited Polyhedron class. So for our neutron-transport first consumer, polyhedra support in downstream codes is much weaker than in CFD; the IR should be a face-based polyhedral superset with lossless down-conversion exporters. Unverified: STAR-CCM+ internals (proprietary, not researched), Fluent .msh/.cas exact polyhedral encoding, VTK XML polyhedron array layout, Exodus NFACED spec text.
data_model: OpenFOAM polyMesh (verified, v9 guide): files points (list of vec3, 0-based, no duplicates, each point used by a face), faces (list of ordered point-label lists, may be warped), owner (cell label per face), neighbour (cell label per internal face; internal faces first, boundary faces after, patches given as contiguous face ranges via boundary {type, nFaces, startFace}). Internal-face normal points from lower-label cell (owner) to higher-label cell (neighbour); boundary-face normal points out. Cells are not stored: they are "a list of faces in arbitrary order", derived from owner/neighbour. Validity constraints: cells geometrically closed (sum of outward area vectors = 0) and topologically closed (each edge used by exactly two faces of the cell). The cellShape/cellModels (hex, wedge, prism, pyr, tet, tetWedge) exist only for blockMesh/import, not storage. Code_Saturne cs_mesh_t (verified, 9.2 doxygen): i_face_cells (cs_lnum_2_t, interior face -> 2 cells), b_face_cells (boundary face -> 1 cell), i_face_vtx_idx/i_face_vtx_lst and b_face_vtx_idx/b_face_vtx_lst (CSR face->vertex), global_cell_num/global_i_face_num/global_b_face_num/global_vtx_num, halo (cs_halo_t), n_ghost_cells, vtx_interfaces, periodicity fields; interior and boundary faces are separate arrays. Fluent grid file (verified from ANSYS doc via search): face records carry c0/c1 cell ids; boundary face has one of them 0; indices positive; reportedly cell type 7 = polyhedral (inferred from OpenFOAM's fluentFvMesh writer, unverified in ANSYS docs) and for polyhedral grids the cell list is not used - faces carry the topology. CGNS (verified, SIDS Grid section): Elements_t with NGON_n (face -> node list) and NFACE_n (cell -> face list; negative face id = normal pointing inward for that cell); ElementConnectivity + ElementStartOffset (required for MIXED, NGON_n, NFACE_n; offsets array length n+1, last = ElementDataSize); optional ParentElements (2 per face) and ParentElementsPosition. An older CPEX 0041 v0.16 draft used inline per-face node counts instead of offsets (sources disagree; the current form is offsets). libMesh Polyhedron (verified): runtime-topology Cell with _sidelinks_data (shared_ptr<Polygon> per side + inward-normal flag + side-to-element node map), _elemlinks_data, _nodelinks_data, an internal tetrahedral _triangulation for quadrature/mapping; no refinement, no flip(), no master element. meshio Mesh (verified, source): points ndarray; cells = list of CellBlock(type, data, tags); point_data dict; cell_data dict name -> list of per-block arrays; field_data; point_sets dict; cell_sets dict name -> per-block index arrays; gmsh_periodic; info. 67 named cell types in num_nodes_per_cell incl. Lagrange high-order families.
