polyhedra: OpenFOAM: native and the only model (every cell is a face list). Code_Saturne: native, face-based, any polyhedron; the Preprocessor converts input to this. Fluent/STAR-CCM+: native polyhedral (Fluent can convert tets to polyhedra by dual agglomeration around nodes, per ANSYS guide); STAR-CCM+ not researched (unverified). CGNS: lossless via NGON_n+NFACE_n, officially specified; readers: VTK/ParaView support both offset layouts (per GitLab MRs). Exodus: face blocks + element blocks of type NFACED, faces referenced by file-implicit ids depending on face-block order (quote from Exodus lead in ParaView issue 16062); ParaView reader had bugs assuming one face block per element block; ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra exists in exodusII.h (SEACAS 9.06, Aug 2025); NFACED spec text not verified. VTK: VTK_POLYHEDRON cell type (id 42) with a faces stream, exact layout unverified. meshio: any cell type string starting with 'polyhedron' is given dim 3 and its data kept as a Python list (cannot be numpy because ragged); no real semantics - effectively a pass-through stub. libMesh/MOOSE: Polyhedron class exists but with restrictions (no refinement, no flip, convexity assumed in some methods). OpenMC: UnstructuredMesh via MOAB (.h5/.vtk) or libMesh (.exo, since 0.12.2); element_type() classifies by node count (4 = LINEAR_TET, 8 = LINEAR_HEX, else UNSUPPORTED) and HDF5 output skips non-linear-tet/hex elements with a warning; MOAB path warns on non-tets and the KD-tree requires triangular faces. So polyhedra are effectively unsupported in OpenMC unstructured meshes (verified from mesh.cpp, partial read).
nonconformal: Not the primary focus here. Observed: OpenFOAM polyMesh itself is strictly conformal-by-topology (each internal face has exactly two cells); non-conformal interfaces are handled by separate coupled patch types (AMI/cyclicAMI, mapped) declared in the boundary file - a patch pair is a labeled set of boundary faces, and the weights are computed at runtime from geometry (from memory; unverified here). Code_Saturne cs_mesh_t has no non-conformal fields; its approach is mesh joining at preprocessing (the 'join' step creates conformal faces by actually imprinting/splitting faces), plus periodicity fields (verified absence of join fields in cs_mesh_t; join behaviour from memory, unverified). Fluent supports non-conformal interfaces as interface zones (unverified detail). CGNS has GridConnectivity_t with GridConnectivityType 'Abutting' vs 'Abutting1to1' and 'Overset' (from memory, not checked here). Takeaway: in practice the mesh stores two boundary face sets plus a declared pairing; the projection/intersection is computed by the solver, and the format only needs to carry the pair labels and tolerance/transform.
sets_and_partitions: OpenFOAM: boundary patches are contiguous face ranges (startFace, nFaces); cellZones/faceZones/pointZones and sets (cellSet, faceSet) are separate files (zones not covered by the page I read; unverified). Code_Saturne: group names attached to cells/faces handled at the Preprocessor/selection level (unverified); global numbering arrays + halo for parallel. CGNS: Zone_t -> Elements_t sections (region = element range), plus ZoneBC_t/BC_t with PointList/PointRange, FamilyName_t/Family_t for material/BC grouping (from memory; Family concept is the closest existing 'partition layer' idea, unverified here). Exodus: element blocks, node sets, side sets, face blocks. meshio: flat cell_sets/point_sets dicts keyed by name, cell_sets stored per cell block as index arrays, with helper conversions cell_sets_to_data/cell_data_to_sets - i.e., sets and integer data are interchangeable and there is no separation of geometric/partition/mesh layers or hierarchy. Parallel: Code_Saturne = global ids + halo + vertex interfaces; OpenFOAM decomposed case = processorN directories with processor patches (from memory).
strengths: Face-based (owner/neighbour or face->cells) topology is compact, handles any polyhedron, and gives solvers exactly what finite-volume/DG face loops need; verified in OpenFOAM and Code_Saturne.
CGNS NGON_n/NFACE_n is a standardized, offset-based CSR encoding with signed face orientation and optional ParentElements, and is the one formally specified lossless polyhedral interchange path.
meshio proves the value of a hub: a tiny data model (points, cell blocks, point/cell data, sets) with many readers/writers, easy Python access.
Exodus has an established block/set model well suited to FE and neutronics codes (and the SEACAS toolchain, 9.06 in 2025 is actively maintained).
VTKHDF (spec v2.8) offers HDF5-based parallel I/O with a path to ParaView visualization.
weaknesses: Owner/neighbour ordering constraints in OpenFOAM (internal faces first, upper-triangular ordering, patches as contiguous face ranges) tie the storage to solver convenience and make editing awkward.
meshio's polyhedron support is a stub: ragged Python lists, no validation, sets unvalidated, no high-order polyhedra, no geometry association, no versioned spec.
Exodus polyhedra rely on file-implicit face ids dependent on face-block order; reader bugs reported (ParaView issue 16062); NFACED is lightly used.
Neutron transport consumers (OpenMC) accept only linear tets/hexes; libMesh Polyhedron has no refinement or flip and limited mapping, so polyhedra reach few transport codes.
Fluent/STAR-CCM+ formats are proprietary or weakly documented for polyhedra; Fluent polyhedral encoding could not be verified from primary ANSYS docs.
Different formats disagree on conventions (face orientation sign, 0 vs 1 based, offsets vs inline counts - CGNS draft vs current), a recurrent source of silent errors.
lessons_for_us: Adopt face-based topology as the canonical core: points, faces (CSR vertex lists), cell->face CSR with signed (oriented) face refs like CGNS NFACE_n, plus face->(left,right) cell pairs (OpenFOAM owner/neighbour, CGNS ParentElements). Keep both directions as derived/cached 'indexes' rather than file layout constraints.

Do NOT bake solver-friendly ordering (OpenFOAM upper-triangular, patches as contiguous face ranges) into the IR; store ordering-free entities with stable ids and provide export-time renumbering passes per target format (the LLVM-style 'lowering' step).

Treat meshio as the baseline hub but differ: typed entity sets and layers (geometry, partition, mesh) instead of flat cell_sets/point_sets keyed by name; ragged polyhedra as first-class CSR, not Python lists; validated invariants (closure checks like OpenFOAM's geometric/topological closure).

Make cell-shape (tet/hex/prism/pyramid) a derived classification of polyhedra with a fast path, so exporters to OpenMC (linear tet/hex only, by node count 4/8), Exodus, VTK can down-convert losslessly when possible and refuse/warn explicitly otherwise.

Represent non-conformal interfaces explicitly as paired face sets with transform/tolerance metadata (the solver does projection), and offer an optional 'imprint' operation that produces conformal faces (the Code_Saturne joining approach) - both views of the same data.

Use CGNS Family_t-like groups for the partition layer (material/region labels referencing geometry entities and mesh entities), but separate from block structure so one cell has one material while sets may overlap.
Define explicit conventions in the spec (0-based ids, face orientation sign, normal direction rule) and ship a conformance test suite; CGNS offset-vs-inline-count history shows the cost of ambiguity.

Plan exporters in priority: CGNS (lossless polyhedra), Exodus (tets/hexes + face blocks if the transport code uses it), VTKHDF (viz/parallel), OpenFOAM polyMesh (round-trip test of polyhedral capability), meshio-compatible Python object for the long tail.

Because the first transport consumer may only accept tets/hexes (OpenMC) or Exodus (MOOSE/libMesh), keep a hard requirement: every IR mesh must be able to report 'is_exportable_to(format)' with reasons.
high_order: Mostly unverified for polyhedra. meshio lists Lagrange families (e.g. tetra10/20/..., hexahedron27/64/..., wedge15/18, up to order ~11 for several shapes) as named cell types, but only for canonical shapes, not polyhedra. Exodus and CGNS element lists include second-order types (CGNS HEXA_27 etc. from memory, unverified). libMesh Polyhedron has no master element and is first-order polygon-faced; OpenMC only supports linear tet/hex. No surveyed format carries high-order polyhedra with a defined basis; the IR must define its own (e.g. per-face curved geometry maps).
parallel: Code_Saturne (verified): global numbering arrays for cells, interior faces, boundary faces and vertices; cs_halo_t ghost cells (n_ghost_cells, n_cells_with_ghosts = n_cells + n_ghost_cells), optional extended neighbourhood cell_cells_idx/lst, vtx_interfaces and vtx_range_set for shared vertices. OpenFOAM: processorN decomposition with processor patches (from memory, unverified). Exodus: Nemesis extension (NEMESIS_FILE_VERSION 2.6 in exodusII.h). VTKHDF: partitioned datasets in a single .vtkhdf file (high-level doc only; dataset layout unverified). meshio: serial only.
database_like_aspects: Face-based meshes are already relational: owner/neighbour is an adjacency (face->cell) table, CSR face->vertex is a join table, and cells are a derived view (OpenFOAM). CGNS Elements_t sections with ElementRange are tables with ranges and optional ParentElements as foreign keys. meshio's cell_data/point_data are columns attached to entity tables, and cell_sets/cell_data_to_sets show sets and integer attributes are interchangeable (a tag column is a set partition). This supports a columnar, entity-table IR (Arrow/HDF5-like) with derived indexes.
ecosystem: OpenFOAM, Code_Saturne, Fluent and STAR-CCM+ for CFD polyhedra; CGNS read by many CFD tools and by VTK/ParaView (polyhedral reader MR in VTK); Exodus (SEACAS 9.06) with MOOSE/libMesh, Cubit and ParaView; OpenMC via MOAB or libMesh with linear tets/hexes; meshio for Python conversion between dozens of formats and a 67-cell-type dictionary; VTK/VTKHDF for visualization.
geometry_association: Not found in the surveyed polyhedral formats' core mesh data: OpenFOAM, Code_Saturne arrays and meshio have no link to B-rep entities beyond names/tags (meshio CellBlock.tags, gmsh_periodic). CGNS has separate geometry reference nodes (GeometryReference_t, from memory, unverified). Exodus relies on block/set ids that Cubit maps from geometry. So geometry association is a genuine differentiator for our IR.
spec_quality: CGNS: formal, versioned SIDS spec with change proposals (CPEX); best-documented polyhedral format. OpenFOAM: de facto format documented in the user guide with explicit validity rules. Code_Saturne: doxygen API docs, not a file spec. Exodus: API header versioned (9.06), but polyhedral semantics weakly documented. Fluent: public doc exists but polyhedral details unclear. meshio: no spec, behavior defined by code. VTKHDF: versioned (2.8).

corrections.claim: An older CPEX 0041 v0.16 draft used inline per-face node counts instead of offsets (sources disagree; the current form is offsets).
corrections.correction: Direction is reversed. Inline per-face counts in ElementConnectivity were the official CGNS 3.x layout; CPEX 0041 (ONERA, 2017) is what INTRODUCED ElementStartOffset. It shipped in 3.4.0 (breaking forward compatibility inside major version 3), was reverted in 3.4.1, and re-released as 4.0.0. Consequence: two incompatible NGON_n/NFACE_n encodings exist in the wild; an exporter must pick a target CGNS version and a reader must handle both (VTK/ParaView do).
corrections.source: https://cgns.org/cgns-archives/CGNS_docs_current/sids/changes.html and https://cgns.org/cgns-archives/download.html (fetched via search snippets); SIDS gridflow page (fetched): 'ElementStartOffset is required only for MIXED, NGON_n and NFACE_n', length ElementSize+1.

corrections.claim: Of the interchange formats, only CGNS (NGON_n/NFACE_n) is a formal, versioned, standard way to carry polyhedra losslessly.
corrections.correction: VTKHDF (spec version 2.8) carries polyhedra since VTK 9.6 via FaceOffsets/FaceConnectivity (faces as a separate 2D cell array) + PolyhedronToFaces/PolyhedronOffsets, with a single oriented face shareable by several polyhedra, plus per-partition/per-step counts (NumberOfFaces, NumberOfPolyhedronToFaceIds, NumberOfFaceConnectivityIds). Exodus has an official 'Polyhedral Element Storage' page: element block type 'nfaced', face block type 'nsided', ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra, since Exodus v4.93. MED (Salome, HDF5, versioned) also has polyhedron connectivity routines (MEDmeshPolyhedronWr/Rd with face-index + node-index arrays) per the med-4.2.0 API listing (not fetched directly).

corrections.claim: Exodus has face blocks/NFACED but is poorly specified for it and rarely supported by readers; NFACED spec text not verified.
corrections.correction: Official doc exists (polyhedra.html: nfaced/nsided, counts via ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra, example with 3 polyhedra sharing faces 4 and 8). libMesh's ExodusII_IO reads AND writes NFACED <-> C0POLYHEDRON (exodusII_io_helper.C: conversion_map C0POLYHEDRON->"NFACED", C0POLYGON->"NSIDED"; read_face_blocks() requires NSIDED face blocks and uses ex_get_entity_count_per_polyhedra; mixed subdomains are split into one block per element type). ParaView reader bug fixed in 2016. Residual weakness stands: the official page's example has one face block and does not state the cross-face-block numbering rule; Sjaardema's mailing-list reply (file-implicit order) is the only source.

corrections.claim: libMesh/MOOSE has only a recent, limited Polyhedron class (no refinement, no flip, convexity assumed).
corrections.correction: Sharpen: cell_polyhedron.h is authored 2025 (Stogner), lives in master and v1.9.0-rc1/rc2, and is ABSENT from every released libMesh (v1.7.x, v1.8.0-v1.8.4; latest stable v1.8.4, 2025-10-06). runtime_topology()=true; num_children=0 ('Refinement not yet supported'); flip() is libmesh_not_implemented(); convex() helper; internal tetrahedralization (_triangulation) for mapping/quadrature; concrete class C0Polyhedron with first-order C0Polygon sides. mooseframework.inl.gov hosts doxygen for cell_c0polyhedron, so MOOSE builds see it, but FE-family support and any transport-code (Griffin) use on polyhedra are unverified.
corrections.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/include/geom/cell_polyhedron.h (fetched; the report's include/mesh/ path 404s); GitHub tags/releases API (fetched); mooseframework.inl.gov doxygen cell__c0polyhedron_8h (search snippet).

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM non-conformal interfaces are handled by separate coupled patch types (AMI/cyclicAMI, mapped); weights computed at runtime from geometry (from memory).
corrections.correction: True for AMI, but OpenFOAM.org v10 (July 2022) added Non-Conformal Coupling (NCC): createNonConformalCouples creates nonConformalCyclic patches that start with zero faces; at run time the solver 'creates new faces at the intersections of overlapping faces on the coupled patches' which become real FV faces on both sides (conservative, handles partial overlap; periodic repeats via transformed couples). OpenFOAM 11 release notes: 'Non-conformal coupling (NCC) replaces arbitrary mesh interface (AMI)'; ACMI and Repeat AMI removed. So there are two live approaches: interpolation weights (AMI) vs runtime imprinting into real faces (NCC). On-disk form is unchanged (two patches + couple declaration), so the report's storage takeaway survives. openfoam.com (ESI) line not checked.

corrections.claim: Fluent: reportedly cell type 7 = polyhedral (inferred from OpenFOAM's fluentFvMesh writer, unverified in ANSYS docs) and for polyhedral grids the cell list is not used - faces carry the topology.
corrections.correction: Now verified from Fluent documentation (6.x mirror): Cells section (12) element-type codes 0 mixed, 1 triangular, 2 tetrahedral, 3 quadrilateral, 4 hexahedral, 5 pyramid, 6 wedge, 7 polyhedral (NN nodes/NF faces vary). Faces section (13) face types 0 mixed, 2 linear, 3 triangular, 4 quadrilateral, 5 polygonal; record 'x n0..nf c0 c1' for mixed zones; boundary face has c0 or c1 = 0; right-hand rule: thumb points toward c1. The 'cell list not used' phrasing is misleading: the cells section exists for ALL types (zone ranges + type code; a body only for mixed zones) and never carries node connectivity for any type - Fluent is face-based throughout, like OpenFOAM. The ANSYS 2025R2 URL listed in the report was not fetched.

corrections.claim: meshio polyhedron support is a stub: ragged Python lists, no real semantics - effectively a pass-through stub.
corrections.correction: meshio's VTU reader/writer do implement polyhedra: _polyhedron_cells_from_data parses faces/faceoffsets into cell types 'polyhedronN' whose data is a per-cell list of face node arrays, and the writer rebuilds faces/faceoffsets (vtu/_vtu.py). No other meshio writer supports polyhedra. Also note project dormancy: last release v5.3.5 (2024-01-31), last push 2024-07-23, repo not archived. The 67 named cell types claim is verified.

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM polyMesh (verified, v9 guide): owner/neighbour ordering constraints - internal faces first, upper-triangular ordering, patches as contiguous face ranges.
corrections.correction: As attributed. Neither the v9 nor the v12 'Mesh description' guide page mentions upper-triangular order or internal-faces-first (they do define startFace/nFaces, owner/neighbour, normal toward higher cell label, closure rules). The constraint is enforced in code: primitiveMesh::checkUpperTriangular reports ' ***Faces not in upper triangular order.' and returns true (error) when own >= nei or faces are out of order within a cell's neighbour list. Substance of the weakness stands; cite the code, not the guide.

corrections.claim: CGNS element lists include second-order types (HEXA_27 etc. from memory, unverified).
corrections.correction: CGNS ElementType_t goes well beyond second order: cgnslib.h enumerates cubic (BAR_4, TRI_10, QUAD_16, TETRA_20, PYRA_30, PENTA_40, HEXA_64) and quartic (TETRA_35, PYRA_55, HEXA_125, enum value 56) Lagrange and serendipity variants. Caveat: the 'CGNS_docs_current' archive SIDS page the report cites is dated 2016 and stops at HEXA_64; it is not the current spec.

missing_important: Serpent 2 (Monte Carlo) reads OpenFOAM-format polyMesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour) for unstructured-mesh geometry and multiphysics interfaces; accepts tetrahedral, hexahedral AND polyhedral meshes, converting all cells to tetrahedra after reading. This directly weakens 'polyhedra reach few transport codes' and makes an OpenFOAM polyMesh exporter a transport deliverable, not just a round-trip test. (serpent.vtt.fi/docs/user_guide/polymesh.html and the Serpent wiki 'Unstructured mesh based input' - direct fetches returned 403; from search snippets. Web-search quota was exhausted before a second pass.)

MCNP6 unstructured mesh: Abaqus .inp (ASCII, MCNP6.0+), MCNPUM (6.2-6.3, deprecated), HDF5 input (6.3+); element types are first- and second-order tetrahedra/pentahedra/hexahedra only (4/10, 6/15, 8/20 nodes). No polyhedra. (LANL reports LA-UR-21-26436, LA-UR-22-30643, LA-UR-25-26170; search snippets.)

OpenMC libMesh backend details (mesh.cpp, fetched): fatal_error unless the mesh is a libMesh::ReplicatedMesh; LibMesh::sample_element assumes 4 vertices (tet barycentric sampling), so mesh-based source sampling is tet-only even for hex meshes; statepoint 'connectivity' is fixed shape (n_elements, 8); libMesh support added in 0.12.2 (confirmed in the API doc). Formats: moab .h5m/.vtk, libmesh .exo.

CGNS non-conformal data model (SIDS cnct page, fetched): GridConnectivityType_t = {Overset, Abutting, Abutting1to1}; GridConnectivity1to1_t is structured-only; mismatched Abutting interfaces carry CellListDonor and optionally InterpolantsDonor, but 'InterpolantsDonor is currently only defined for structured grids and certain basic unstructured grid element types' - CGNS cannot carry interpolation weights for polyhedral interfaces. Supports the report's 'store pair labels + transform only' lesson.

CGNS partition/geometry layer (SIDS misc page, fetched; archive page dated 2016): Family_t lives under CGNSBase_t, nests (child Family_t), and is attached to Zone_t (volume) or BC_t (BCType=FamilySpecified). GeometryReference_t exists only inside Family_t, is surface-only ('for zone properties ... GeometryReference_t is not used'), GeometryFormat enum is {NASA-IGES, SDRC, Unigraphics, ProEngineer, ICEM-CFD, UserDefined} (no STEP), and GeometryEntity is a name string. So the closest existing CAD link is name-based and dated - confirms geometry association as a differentiator.

VTKHDF's polyhedron layout (faces as a shared, separately indexed 2D cell array referenced by polyhedra via offsets; HDF5 partitions per MPI rank; time steps appended with offsets in a Steps group) is structurally the closest existing format to the report's proposed face-based CSR IR core. The report ranked VTKHDF as viz-only and left its polyhedron support unverified. (vtkhdf_specifications.html, fetched.)

VTK XML (.vtu) polyhedron layout verified: types=42; 'faces' per cell = [nFaces, (nPts, ids...)...]; 'faceoffsets' = end index of each cell's entries. VTK 9.4 changed the in-memory storage to shared face arrays (polyhedron_face_connectivity/offsets + polyhedron_face_location_* per PyVista docs), so readers/writers must handle both the stream form and the 9.4+ API. (VTK XML file-format page and PyVista docs; search snippets.)

Code_Saturne joining confirmed as a preprocessing step (cs_preprocess --join): vertex-fusion tolerance = fraction 0.1 of shortest connected edge, coplanarity cosine 0.8, --semi-conf fast mode when faces already share vertices; joinings run before periodicity in cs_user_mesh order. Confirms the report's 'from memory' claim. (manpages.org/cs_preprocess and code-saturne.org forum; search snippets.)

STAR-CCM+ interchange is the .ccm format via the proprietary libccmio (users must contact CD-adapco/Siemens); OpenFOAM.com ships ccmToFoam which requires libccmio and reads sub-domains/baffles. Not a free lossless polyhedral exchange path. (api.openfoam.com ccmToFoam_8C, openfoamwiki Ccm26ToFoam; search snippets.)

Exodus header confirms report's numbers exactly: EXODUS_VERSION "9.06", EXODUS_RELEASE_DATE "August 25, 2025", NEMESIS_FILE_VERSION 2.6, ex_put/get_entity_count_per_polyhedra present (exodusII.h fetched). No correction needed.

topic: Non-conformal interfaces in FE/multiphysics codes (MOOSE/libMesh mortar, MFEM/deal.II hanging-node AMR, Nitsche/cut-cell)
summary: There are two unrelated meanings of "non-conformal", and codes treat them with completely different machinery. (A) Hanging-node / AMR non-conformity: the mesh is one connected topology with a refinement hierarchy. Coarse-fine faces are identified from parent/child info (MFEM NCMesh master/slave lists, deal.II 1-irregular face subdivision, libMesh parent/children + neighbor-is-ancestor). Continuity is restored algebraically (constraint matrix P, deal.II AffineConstraints) and no geometric search is needed. (B) Genuinely non-matching interfaces (separately meshed parts, sliding or contact, tied surfaces): the mesh file carries no special "non-conformal" marker in MOOSE/libMesh/Exodus. It just has coincident or near-coincident, un-merged surfaces. The user designates them as sidesets (Exodus: element id + local side number) and, in MOOSE, as lower-dimensional blocks. At run time the code builds the projection with a geometric search plus clipping (MOOSE AutomaticMortarGeneration: k-d tree screening, projection onto a linearized secondary face, polygon clipping, triangulation into a mortar segment mesh). Nitsche/cut-cell methods (deal.II NonMatching, Massing/Larson/Logg) instead compute mesh intersections to integrate on cut cells. Maturity: all of these are production-grade. None of them stores the interface pairing as first-class mesh data in the file. It is re-derived each run, and the "which surface pairs with which" intent lives in the input deck. This is the gap our IR can fill. Caveat: mooseframework.inl.gov docs pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so MOOSE claims come from the raw GitHub source, search-result excerpts of the docs, and the libMesh headers. Items from memory are marked unverified.
data_model:
MOOSE/libMesh (type B, mortar). The mesh is a libMesh Mesh (Elem/Node objects, usually read from Exodus). Each Elem stores neighbor(side), parent, children, interior_parent (lower-d element -> higher-d element for which it is a face), subdomain id. Boundary info is (elem, side, boundary_id) triples. Only face neighbors are stored; a null neighbor means the side is on a domain boundary. To do mortar, MOOSE needs lower-dimensional elements on both interface sides. These are created in the mesh pipeline by LowerDBlockFromSidesetGenerator (MooseMeshUtils::createSubdomainFromSidesets, optional new_block_id/new_block_name) or already exist in the Cubit/Gmsh file. The user then names primary_boundary/primary_subdomain and secondary_boundary/secondary_subdomain in the Mortar constraint (primary/secondary naming per the docs excerpt; I could not open the page). At run time AutomaticMortarGeneration (framework/include/constraints/AutomaticMortarGeneration.h) holds: _nodes_to_secondary_elem_map and _nodes_to_primary_elem_map; _secondary_node_and_elem_to_xi2_primary_elem and _primary_node_and_elem_to_xi1_secondary_elem (projection parameters, ordered for cross-rank consistency); _msm_elem_to_info (MortarSegmentInfo); _secondary_elems_to_mortar_segments; _secondary_node_to_nodal_normal and Householder tangents; _mortar_interface_coupling; and _lower_elem_to_side_id. The output is a separate "mortar segment mesh" (MSM): 1D elements in 2D (buildMortarSegmentMesh), triangles in 3D (buildMortarSegmentMesh3d). Algorithm in 3D from the source comments: linearize secondary faces (Tri3/Quad4 around the center; Tri6/Quad9/Tri7 subdivided into first-order sub-elements, each linearized), coarse screening with a k-d tree against the secondary face center, then breadth-first neighbor search over primary candidates, then project the primary sub-element onto the linearized secondary sub-element, clip (MortarSegmentHelper), and triangulate. Tolerances: an area tolerance rejects slivers, and a sine-of-angle test uses the cross product normalized by tangent lengths so it does not depend on length scale. Node and element IDs for MSM entities are allocated by an exclusive prefix scan over ranks, with 9 as the maximum nodes per secondary/primary sub-element pair.

MFEM (type A). NCMesh (mesh/ncmesh.hpp) stores a refinement forest. Elements hold geom, ref_type (X/Y/Z split bitmask), parent, and a union of node[8] (leaf) or child[10] (refined). Nodes are hashed by their two parent node ids (Hashed2) and can be a vertex, an edge, or both. Faces are hashed by 4 vertex node ids and hold elem[2]. NCList holds conforming, masters and slaves arrays. A Master is "Nonconforming edge/face that has more than one neighbor"; a Slave is a "Nonconforming edge/face within a bigger edge/face" and stores master (mesh index), matrix (index into point_matrices) and edge_flags (orientation). A PointMatrix maps the slave's vertices into the master's reference coordinates, and the interpolation Q_k per slave is built from it. Entities are classified as CONFORMING, MASTER, SLAVE or UNRECOGNIZED. Paper (Cerveny, Dobrev, Kolev, arXiv:1905.04033): about 290 bytes/element for a uniform hex mesh. Entity identity is by vertex-index tuples in hash tables, explicitly not the Sieve representation. The constraint P splits into identity rows, direct slave rows and indirect slave rows, resolved in n sweeps for n-irregular meshes (typically at most 3-irregular).

deal.II (type A). Triangulation is a cell hierarchy. Meshes are 1-irregular by default: adjacent cells differ by at most one level, enforced through the MeshSmoothing flags. Hanging-node constraints x_i = sum a_ij x_j + b_i live in AffineConstraints, built by DoFTools::make_hanging_node_constraints. The mesh stores no extra pairing: coarse-fine faces are found from child links.
polyhedra: Not first-class in any of these. libMesh has Tet/Hex/Prism/Pyramid, and Polygon support was added in recent versions (unverified, not checked here). deal.II is cell-type fixed (quad/hex/simplex/wedge/pyramid, no general polyhedra). MFEM NCMesh supports quad/hex, tri/tet, prism and pyramid, with anisotropic refinement and arbitrary irregularity, but no general polyhedra. For mortar in MOOSE, interface faces must be Tri3/Tri6/Tri7/Quad4/Quad9. The docs excerpt recommends QUAD secondary faces in 3D because TRI secondaries can be poorly conditioned. Face linearization via the center point and sub-patch subdivision means an arbitrary polygon face would need a new linearization rule. For our IR, polyhedral cells with arbitrary n-gon faces mean any projection layer must be defined on polygon faces. The clipping step (convex polygon clipping, then triangulation) already generalizes to polygons naturally. Only the linearization step is element-type specific.
nonconformal:
File level. MOOSE/libMesh: there is no explicit non-conformal marker in the format. The non-conformity is just un-merged surfaces. Two meshes are read or combined, and the stitching generators (StitchedMeshGenerator, StitchBoundaryMeshGenerator, libMesh stitch_meshes / stitch_surfaces) merge coincident nodes only if you ask. Stitching uses a relative tolerance against the smallest edge length of the surfaces. It uses sort-then-binary-search node matching by default, with an O(N^2) fallback for slightly misaligned meshes. It can optionally leave coincident nodes unmerged (merge_boundary_nodes_all_or_nothing), and clear_stitched_boundary_ids defaults to true. So detection of "these two faces should be glued" is not in the file. It is the user's choice of stitch call, or of mortar/contact constraint on a named sideset pair. Cubit/Exodus: the Cubit docs describe sidesets as an (element number, local side number) pair, and the Cubit help text suggests the usual flow is Imprint All then Merge All, with merging limitable to subsets of the model. A non-conformal interface is therefore a case where merge was skipped for that surface pair, and the two sidesets are exported (details of Cubit's "no merge" mechanics were not verified). Cubit also ships a Matching Tetrahedral Meshes tool that imports two Exodus/Genesis files and locally modifies the tets to make the interface conforming (tets and free mesh only; one target sideset enclosing the source sidesets).

Run-time detection and projection. MOOSE: k-d tree on primary-node/center positions, BFS over candidate primary faces, projection along the secondary-face normal onto a local linearization, polygon clipping, tolerance filters. Segment integration follows Puso (2004, CMAME 193:601-629). Per a secondary description, 3D integration cells are built by triangulating the clipped segment (the sources I found describe Puso-Laursen's cells as triangles formed by connecting the centroid to the corners, with 7-point quadrature; not primary-verified). In 2D, nodal-normal projection at the nodes, plus splitting of secondary elements at projected primary nodes. Nitsche/cut-cell (Massing, Larson & Logg, arXiv:1210.7076): the key difficulty is the automatic detection of mesh intersections and integration over cut cells and subsimplices. deal.II NonMatching offers create_coupling_mass_matrix and sparsity patterns, MeshClassifier with LocationToLevelSet {inside, outside, intersected, unassigned}, and QuadratureGenerator/FaceQuadratureGenerator for cut-cell quadrature. Hanging-node AMR (type A): no geometric search at all. Parent/child links give master/slave directly, with PointMatrix giving the slave's position in the master reference frame. MFEM's NCMesh also needs consistency rules (anisotropic refinement can create inconsistent masters/slaves, and further refinement is added to restore valid relations; Fig 5.3 of the paper).
sets_and_partitions: MOOSE/libMesh: subdomain (block) id + name per element (the partition-layer analogue); boundary ids (sidesets as elem,side pairs; nodesets as nodes) with names; mortar adds lower-dimensional subdomains whose elements carry interior_parent links. The "geometry / partition / mesh" separation is not modeled: names live in the file and everything else is in the input deck. MFEM: per-element and per-boundary-element integer attribute in the element lines (<owner rank> <attribute> <geom> <refinement type> ...), with the boundary section identical to the conforming format. deal.II: material_id on cells, boundary_id on lower-dimensional objects (interior faces default to the internal_face_boundary_id), and manifold_id (geometry association). Refinement children inherit the parent's material_id. This is the cleanest built-in "geometry link" among these codes. Because material_id and boundary_id are separate from manifold_id, deal.II has the three-way split (partition tag, boundary tag, geometry tag) as plain integers.
strengths: Two clean regimes: topological non-conformity (hanging nodes, solved algebraically with master/slave + point matrices, no search) vs geometric non-conformity (mortar/Nitsche, solved with search + clipping + a derived segment mesh).
MOOSE keeps the interface pairing explicit at the input level (primary/secondary boundary + subdomain), so detection is never ambiguous and the file stays a plain mesh.

The mortar segment mesh is a derived, cacheable, separately-stored mesh with its own ids and per-segment info (MortarSegmentInfo). It is rebuilt on mesh change (meshChanged()/clear()) and is parallel-aware (prefix-scan ids, ordered maps for cross-rank consistency).

MFEM NCMesh: very compact (about 290 B/element), hanging vertices need no stored coordinates (derived from two parents), arbitrary irregularity, anisotropic refinement, and a documented text format (MFEM NC mesh v1.0) with vertex_parents.
deal.II keeps the geometry link (manifold_id) separate from the partition tag (material_id) and the boundary tag (boundary_id), which maps well onto the user's 3-layer model.
Constraint algebra is generic: x_i = sum a_ij x_j + b_i (AffineConstraints) works for hanging nodes, periodicity, and mortar-like ties alike.
weaknesses: The file/mesh does not record the interface relation. 'These two sidesets are a tied or non-matching pair' is only in the solver input, so it is lost on export and must be re-specified for every code.
The geometric search is redone every run and uses ad-hoc tolerances (area, sine-of-angle, 100*TOLERANCE scaling). The tolerances are not part of the mesh data.
MOOSE mortar needs lower-d blocks to exist beforehand (LowerDBlockFromSidesetGenerator or Cubit), a workaround for the lack of first-class face entities in libMesh (Elem stores only face neighbors).

In 3D, mortar quality depends on the secondary face type (QUAD preferred, TRI can be ill-conditioned) and depends on linearizing faces, which is not valid for curved/high-order interfaces without sub-division; polyhedral faces are unsupported.

Stitching is tolerance-based, and 'merge or not' is a mutable action on the mesh, not a persistent property (clear_stitched_boundary_ids by default wipes the labels). Docs for merge_boundaries_with_same_name defaults were inconsistent between pages in the search results.

Hanging-node codes only handle refinement-derived non-conformity (1-irregular by default in deal.II; MFEM allows more but must repair inconsistent anisotropic cases); an arbitrary imported non-matching interface cannot be expressed in the NCMesh forest.
No spec for any of this beyond source/headers: MFEM NC format is documented but tied to the forest; Exodus has no concept of an interface pair.
lessons_for_us: ADOPT: make the interface relation a first-class, persisted entity, not a solver-input convention. Define an Interface table with (side_A face set, side_B face set, kind in {conformal-merged, tied, sliding, hanging/AMR-derived}, tolerance, geometric gap/offset). It is then exportable to Exodus sidesets + MOOSE input or to Nitsche/mortar as needed, as 'imprinted vs not imprinted' becomes data. The user's 'imprinting' concept maps to: information-level imprint = Interface record linking face sets; physical imprint = actually merging/splitting faces to make conformal.

ADOPT: keep the two regimes distinct in the IR. (1) Hierarchical/hanging: parent/child + point-matrix (slave-in-master reference coords) as in MFEM NCList, which makes the constraint algebra derivable without search. (2) Geometric non-matching: pair of face sets plus an optional cached 'overlap/segment' layer.

ADOPT: store the derived overlap (mortar segment) mesh as an optional cache layer attached to an Interface: segments with (primary face, secondary face, polygon in both reference frames). This is exactly MOOSE's _msm_elem_to_info/_secondary_elems_to_mortar_segments. Version it with a hash of the two face sets plus tolerances, so consumers (DG transport upwinding across non-matching faces, Monte Carlo ray crossing) can reuse it instead of re-running search + clip.

ADOPT: make faces first-class entities with ids and (cell, local side) incidences, not only cell-to-cell neighbors. libMesh's lack of this forces the lower-d-block workaround. With first-class faces, an interface is simply a set of face ids on each side and 'sideset' is a view.
ADOPT: derive hanging vertices from parents, don't store coordinates (MFEM) and keep IDs stable; store hierarchy as an optional tree layer.

ADOPT: separate integer tags per layer like deal.II: material/partition id (partition layer), boundary id (on faces), and geometry id (B-rep entity: manifold_id analogue) so the three layers coexist and link by id.

ADOPT: tolerances are data. Record the merge/projection tolerance (relative to local edge length, as libMesh's stitching does) and a scale-free angle test in the interface record, so detection is reproducible across codes.

DIFFER: polygon-native clipping. MOOSE linearizes Tri/Quad faces and clips convex polygons then triangulates; our IR should define overlap on arbitrary planar polygon faces (and later curved high-order faces via sub-division) so polyhedra work without a face-type-specific path.

DIFFER: record detection provenance (explicit user pair vs automatic detection of coincident-but-unmerged faces). Automatic detection should be a mesher/validation tool producing candidate Interface records that a human or script confirms. Do not rely on 'two coincident un-merged faces' as the only encoding, because then a solver cannot tell an intentional gap/contact from an error.
DIFFER: parallel. Make Interface records partition-aware (per-rank owned faces + ghost info), since MOOSE needed ordered maps and prefix-scan id allocation to stay consistent across ranks.

Open question for the neutron-transport consumer: for DG-SN, upwind flux across a non-matching face needs the overlap polygons with their cosines and areas, so the cached overlap layer is directly useful; for Monte Carlo, a conformal or tied interface only needs adjacency (face-to-face crossing), so an 'adjacency-through-interface' view should be derivable from the same record.

UNVERIFIED: Abaqus/LS-DYNA/Sierra tied-contact and surface-based tie handling, libMesh polygon support, and Exodus II spec array names (elem_ss/side_ss) were not checked against primary sources
spec_quality: Mixed. MFEM publishes a versioned text format ("MFEM NC mesh v1.0", with legacy v1.1), with named sections (elements, boundary, vertex_parents, root_state, coordinates, mfem_mesh_end), but it describes a refinement forest and not arbitrary non-matching interfaces. Exodus II is a stable, de facto format for sidesets as (element, local side) pairs, but it has no concept of an interface pair, and the Exodus spec itself was not re-checked here. libMesh, deal.II and MOOSE have class documentation and papers but no formal data-model spec for interfaces. The mortar data model is only observable in the source, headers, and docs of AutomaticMortarGeneration. I could not open the MOOSE docs pages directly (HTTP 403).
storage: Meshes are normally Exodus II (NetCDF/HDF5 container) read via libMesh for MOOSE. MFEM has a human-readable text format (NC v1.0). deal.II is mostly in-memory plus its own serialization (and external readers). The mortar segment mesh is in-memory only (not persisted; rebuilt on mesh change). Performance-relevant: MFEM hashes entity identities by vertex tuples (about 290 B/element), MOOSE uses a k-d tree for coarse screening and ordered maps for cross-rank consistency. There is no persisted interface cache in any of these codes.
parallel: MOOSE: AutomaticMortarGeneration allocates node/element ids for the MSM with an exclusive prefix scan (bound reserved per rank, 9 nodes max per sub-element pair), and keeps _primary_node_and_elem_to_xi1_secondary_elem as an ordered map "for consistency across processes". libMesh uses remote_elem as a placeholder for elements living on other processors. MFEM: element lines carry an owner rank, partitioning is element-based by splitting a Hilbert space-filling curve over the refinement trees (Hilbert gives better connectivity than Z-curve), and it builds the parallel conforming P. deal.II NonMatching: parallel support is limited (immersed triangulation must be shared-type; the kernel version needs at least one shared triangulation).
high_order: MOOSE mortar handles second-order faces (Tri6/Quad9) and third-order (Tri7) by sub-dividing into four first-order elements and linearizing each, so segments are not exact for curved interfaces. MFEM NCMesh supports high-order with the conforming interpolation computed element-locally (slave DOFs as combinations of master DOFs via shape functions evaluated at the slave positions; same order p on both sides, so no p-nonconformity), including H1 and Nedelec. deal.II hanging-node constraints cover hp-mode with differing h and p (Q1/Q2 example in docs). Curved geometry is attached via manifold_id objects, not the mesh itself.
geometry_association: deal.II: manifold_id on cells/faces maps to Manifold objects and can be set on the boundary (set_all_manifold_ids_on_boundary); children inherit boundary and manifold ids as the mesh refines. MOOSE/libMesh: no B-rep link; the geometry association is purely through Exodus block/sideset names and ids carried from Cubit. MFEM: curvature carried by a nodes grid function (curvilinear meshes use a nodes section), and the refinement tree keeps root-element attributes only.
database_like_aspects: The mortar machinery is already implicitly relational: _nodes_to_secondary_elem_map, _secondary_elems_to_mortar_segments, _msm_elem_to_info, _lower_elem_to_side_id and interior_parent are join tables built on demand from the mesh plus a spatial index (k-d tree). MFEM's NCMesh looks like a small database too: entities keyed by vertex-tuple hashes, with an inverse index (inv_index) mapping Mesh ids to classification {CONFORMING, MASTER, SLAVE}. The natural database view is: Faces(id, cell_L, cell_R, geometry_id), Interfaces(id, face_set_A, face_set_B, kind, tol), Overlaps(interface_id, faceA, faceB, polygon) as a materialized view, with spatial indexes as an implementation detail. This is an opinion derived from the sources above, not something any of these codes provides as a queryable store.
ecosystem: Exodus II (via Cubit/Gmsh) is the interchange into MOOSE/libMesh and many Sandia codes. MFEM and deal.II mostly generate their own meshes or read common formats. Python-level tooling for MOOSE mesh generators (Stitch*, LowerDBlockFromSidesetGenerator) is configured through input files. Interface/contact definitions are code-specific (MOOSE input blocks), which is why they do not interoperate. (Interop of Abaqus/LS-DYNA tie constraints: unverified.)

corrections.claim: Polyhedra: "Not first-class in any of these. libMesh has Tet/Hex/Prism/Pyramid, and Polygon support was added in recent versions (unverified)"
corrections.correction: libMesh now has element types C0POLYGON (=39, arbitrary N-gon) and C0POLYHEDRON (=40, arbitrary polyhedron with C0POLYGON faces) in include/enums/enum_elem_type.h, classes include/geom/face_c0polygon.h (first commit 2025-03-04) and include/geom/cell_c0polyhedron.h (first commit 2025-05-06), and ExodusII_IO reads/writes them as Exodus NSIDED/NFACED blocks (src/mesh/exodusII_io_helper.C lines 463-467, 588-589, 1294-1333). Present at tag v1.9.0-rc2, absent at v1.8.4 and v1.7.9; no v1.9.0 final release is listed on GitHub, so this is master/1.9.0-RC only. Not checked: shape-function/quadrature completeness on polyhedra, and whether MOOSE's pinned libMesh includes it. The MOOSE 3D mortar face-type switch is unchanged, so polyhedral interface faces remain unsupported for mortar regardless.
corrections.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/include/enums/enum_elem_type.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/master/src/mesh/exodusII_io_helper.C ; GitHub commits API for include/geom/cell_c0polyhedron.h and face_c0polygon.h ; raw.githubusercontent.com/libMesh/libmesh/{v1.8.4,v1.9.0-rc2}/include/geom/cell_c0polyhedron.h (404 vs 200)

corrections.claim: "None of them stores the interface pairing as first-class mesh data in the file ... This is the gap our IR can fill."
corrections.correction: True for the four FE frameworks surveyed (MOOSE/libMesh, MFEM, deal.II, Exodus), false as a statement about the mesh-format landscape. CGNS SIDS GridConnectivity_t is a persisted interface record: ZoneDonorName (required), PointRange/PointList of receiver points with GridLocation Vertex or FaceCenter (on unstructured zones faces are indexed by their Elements_t numbering), GridConnectivityType_t in {Overset, Abutting, Abutting1to1}, and its stated purpose is to "describe mismatched-abutting and overset interfaces"; it can also carry cached projection data (CellListDonor for any type, optional InterpolantsDonor interpolation factors, PointListDonor for Abutting1to1 only). OpenFOAM-dev polyMesh also persists coupled non-conformal patch pairs (nonConformalCyclicPolyPatch with origPatchName and a cyclicTransform at patch level; header comment: most non-conformal interfaces are sliding). The 'conceptually similar to X' baseline for the proposed Interface table is CGNS GridConnectivity_t, not 'nothing'.

corrections.claim: "Segment integration follows Puso (2004, CMAME 193:601-629)"
corrections.correction: Wrong paper. MOOSE's AutomaticMortarGeneration.md cites puso20043d = M. A. Puso, 'A 3D mortar method for solid mechanics', Int. J. Numer. Meth. Engng 59(3):315-336 (2004) for the 3D linearization approach, and puso2008segment = Puso, Laursen, Solberg, 'A segment-to-segment mortar contact method for quadratic elements and large deformations', CMAME 197(6-8):555-566 (2008) for second-order faces. CMAME 193:601-629 is Puso & Laursen's 2D segment-to-segment paper, which MOOSE does not cite here.

corrections.claim: "For mortar in MOOSE, interface faces must be Tri3/Tri6/Tri7/Quad4/Quad9"
corrections.correction: QUAD8 is also handled in 3D (switch cases TRI3, QUAD4, TRI6, TRI7, QUAD8, QUAD9; default branch mooseError 'Face element type ... not supported for 3D mortar'). Also, the MOOSE Constraints docs describe the TRI problem as 'locking' producing singular systems needing stabilization, and recommend QUAD secondary faces (HEX volumes or carefully oriented PRISM/PYRAMID) in 3D.

corrections.claim: "the stitching generators (StitchedMeshGenerator, StitchBoundaryMeshGenerator ...)" and "clear_stitched_boundary_ids defaults to true"
corrections.correction: In MOOSE next, StitchedMeshGenerator was renamed StitchMeshGenerator (registerMooseObjectRenamed with deprecation stamp '06/30/2026', already past); files are StitchMeshGenerator.C, StitchMeshGeneratorBase.C, StitchBoundaryMeshGenerator.C. Defaults: MOOSE StitchMeshGeneratorBase sets clear_stitched_boundary_ids=true and algorithm=BINARY (alt. EXHAUSTIVE); StitchMeshGenerator adds prevent_boundary_ids_overlap and merge_boundaries_with_same_name. The libMesh API default is the opposite: UnstructuredMesh::stitch_meshes/stitch_surfaces have clear_stitched_boundary_ids=false, use_binary_search=true, tol=TOLERANCE relative to smallest edge length on the surfaces. The report cited the libMesh header while reporting the MOOSE default.

corrections.claim: deal.II: "Meshes are 1-irregular by default: adjacent cells differ by at most one level, enforced through the MeshSmoothing flags"
corrections.correction: One-irregularity across faces is an unconditional Triangulation invariant, not a flag: 'the levels of two adjacent cells may differ by one at most', and MeshSmoothing::none is documented as 'No mesh smoothing at all, except that meshes have to remain one-irregular'. MeshSmoothing flags add further constraints (e.g. limit_level_difference_at_vertices, since level jumps of two or more can otherwise occur at vertices where more than four cells meet).

corrections.claim: MFEM NCMesh: "same order p on both sides, so no p-nonconformity"
corrections.correction: That is the 2019 paper's assumption ('all elements have the same order p'). MFEM 4.3 (July 29, 2021) added variable-order spaces via FiniteElementSpace::SetElementOrder, with the conforming interpolation matrix automatically constraining p- and hp-interfaces 'on uniform or mixed NC meshes' (serial); MFEM 4.8 (Apr 9, 2025) added parallel p- and hp-refinement on quad/hex meshes.

corrections.claim: "MFEM NCMesh supports quad/hex, tri/tet, prism and pyramid, with anisotropic refinement and arbitrary irregularity"
corrections.correction: Supported geometries per NCMesh::CheckSupportedGeom: SEGMENT, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, CUBE, PRISM, PYRAMID, TETRAHEDRON. Anisotropic refinement applies to quads/hexes; prisms: 'Anisotropic prism refinement is only available in the serial version' (4.1, Mar 2020); pyramids in NC meshes since 4.5.2 (Mar 2023) with 'only isotropic refinement'; tets isotropic. Arbitrary irregularity is correct (LimitNCLevel optional); the paper notes 'in practice ... at most 3-irregular' and that one example enforced 1-irregularity for stability.

corrections.claim: "MFEM publishes a versioned text format ('MFEM NC mesh v1.0', with legacy v1.1)" and MFEM sets are "per-element and per-boundary-element integer attribute" only
corrections.correction: mfem.org documents 'MFEM mesh v1.0', 'MFEM NC mesh v1.0', 'MFEM mesh v1.3' (adds named attribute_sets and bdr_attribute_sets) and 'MFEM NURBS mesh v1.0'; 'MFEM mesh v1.1' is only referenced in the CHANGELOG as the legacy NC format replaced in 4.3. The v1.3 named sets mean MFEM's set model is not integer-attribute-only. NC format sections (dimension, rank, elements, boundary, vertex_parents, root_state, coordinates/nodes, mfem_mesh_end) and element lines '<owner rank> <attribute> <geometry type> <refinement type> <vertex or child indices>' are confirmed.

corrections.claim: "UNVERIFIED: ... Exodus II spec array names (elem_ss/side_ss)"
corrections.correction: Now verified: exodusII_int.h defines VAR_ELEM_SS(num) -> 'elem_ss<num>' and VAR_SIDE_SS(num) -> 'side_ss<num>' (DIM_NUM_SIDE_SS -> 'num_side_ss<num>'). Current Exodus API version string is 9.06.

missing_important: CGNS SIDS GridConnectivity_t is the existing standard for persisted interface pairing, including non-conformal ones: GridConnectivityType_t {Overset (zones overlap; default), Abutting (touch without overlap), Abutting1to1 (grid lines continue, vertices shared)}; stores ZoneDonorName, receiver PointList/PointRange with GridLocation Vertex|FaceCenter (unstructured faces indexed by Elements_t numbering), and optional cached projection (CellListDonor for any type; InterpolantsDonor factors, defined for structured grids and basic linear unstructured element types; PointListDonor only for Abutting1to1). GridConnectivity1to1_t is structured-only (PointRange, PointRangeDonor, Transform). This is the baseline the proposed Interface+Overlap tables should be compared against. (https://cgns.org/standard/SIDS/multizone.html)

Exodus (API 9.06) does support arbitrary polyhedra: 'nfaced' element blocks whose connectivity references faces in EX_FACE_BLOCK 'nsided' face blocks, with ex_put_entity_count_per_polyhedra (seacas test testwt-nfaced.c). libMesh reads/writes C0POLYHEDRON<->NFACED and expects NSIDED face blocks. Caveat (secondary source, 2016 Kitware/ParaView mailing-list excerpt, Sandia Exodus maintainer): faces are referenced by file-implicit ids, duplicate coincident faces on block interfaces are not recognized as the same face, and the polyhedral capability is thinly documented.

Exodus also has hierarchical 'assemblies' (EX_ASSEMBLY; ex_assembly members are EX_ELEM_BLOCK or EX_ASSEMBLY, i.e. nestable groupings) and 'blobs' (EX_BLOB) in exodusII.h — a native partition-layer grouping mechanism the report's 'Exodus is sidesets + blocks only' framing omits, relevant because Exodus is the interchange into MOOSE/Cubit.

PETSc DMPlex is the closest existing 'mesh as a graph/database' baseline: every entity (cell, face, edge, vertex) is a 'point' in a DAG/Hasse diagram related by cone/support (covering relation), with depth/height strata, transitive closure, join/meet queries; the manual states closure-based traversal 'will work for polyhedral cells, hybrid meshes, and meshes of any dimension, without change'; parallel HDF5 storage version 3.0.0 since PETSc 3.19 with save/load on different process counts. (https://petsc.org/release/manual/dmplex/) The report lists no such baseline.

OpenFOAM-dev persists non-conformal coupled patch pairs in the polyMesh boundary file: nonConformalCyclicPolyPatch (derived from cyclic/nonConformalCoupledPolyPatch) carries origPatchName and a cyclicTransform, with a moveUpdate policy {always, detect, never}; the header notes most non-conformal interfaces are sliding interfaces. (Only the Foundation header was verified; the ESI cyclicAMI header fetch returned a GitLab login page.)

MOOSE BreakMeshByBlockGenerator is the operation that creates an un-merged interface from a conformal mesh: shared nodes are duplicated N-1 times, a new interface sideset is added (linked to the lower block id), optionally split per adjacent block pair (split_interface=true), restricted by surrounding_blocks or block_pairs. This is the inverse of imprinting/merging and is how MOOSE users typically produce the 'coincident but un-merged' surfaces the report describes, so the information-level 'Interface' record proposal should account for it. (framework/doc/content/source/meshgenerators/BreakMeshByBlockGenerator.md)

libMesh timeline detail: polygon/polyhedron support postdates 1.8.x; GitHub releases list v1.8.3 (2025-09-17), v1.8.4 and v1.9.0-rc2 (2025-10-06), v1.7.9 (2026-02-06) and no v1.9.0 final, so any design relying on libMesh polyhedra via MOOSE should check the libMesh submodule pin.

deal.II manifold_id inheritance (report claim) is confirmed by the manifold module docs: 'Mesh refinement will then inherit these indicators to child cells, faces, and edges'; default is numbers::flat_manifold_id; set_all_manifold_ids / set_all_manifold_ids_on_boundary(b_id, number) exist. Interior-face disambiguation defaults to flat_manifold_id when parents disagree.

Verified as stated (no correction): Cerveny et al. 'about 290 bytes per element' for uniform hex; n sweeps for n-irregular with 'typically at most 3-irregular' in practice; Hilbert vs Z-curve partitioning; explicit contrast with the Sieve representation; NCList::MeshIdType {CONFORMING, MASTER, SLAVE, UNRECOGNIZED}; deal.II NonMatching::LocationToLevelSet {inside, outside, intersected, unassigned} and shared-triangulation requirements; MOOSE Constraints parameters primary_boundary/secondary_boundary/primary_subdomain/secondary_subdomain with LowerDBlockFromSidesetGenerator.

topic: Non-conformal interfaces in FV/CFD codes (OpenFOAM AMI/ACMI, Fluent/STAR-CCM+, Code_Saturne joining, CGNS abutting, supermesh/MEDCoupling)
summary: There are two opposite philosophies for non-conformal interfaces. (A) Keep the two sides separate and carry a runtime "interface" object holding donor/receiver addressing plus weights. OpenFOAM AMI/ACMI/cyclicAMI, Fluent mesh interfaces (zones typed "interface", then intersected to make new wall/interior zones), STAR-CCM+ mapped-contact and (imprinted) contact interfaces, and CGNS GridConnectivity_t (Abutting) all do this in different forms. (B) Physically/topologically merge ("join") in preprocessing so the result is a conforming, usually polyhedral, mesh. Code_Saturne does this (cs_preprocess --join), and STAR-CCM+ "imprinted" interfaces create new faces/vertices. The interface weights are generally conservative area-overlap (supermesh / local Galerkin projection, Farrell and Maddison 2011), which is the same math as MEDCoupling's P0P0 intersection-volume matrix. In every system, "which faces are non-conformal" is NOT detected automatically from mesh topology: it is declared by the user (patch/zone pairing, GridConnectivity record) and then geometry is checked or intersected at runtime/preprocessing. Evidence is from primary docs where fetched, and mirrors or search summaries are marked unverified. I could not fetch the OpenFOAM user-guide pages (404) or the Fluent current manual.
data_model: OpenFOAM (AMIInterpolation, api.openfoam.com/2506): per-pair object over two primitive patches with opposite normals; per-source-face ragged arrays srcAddress_ (list of target face ids per source face) and srcWeights_ (matching weights), same in reverse for tgt (tgtAddress_, tgtWeights_); srcWeightsSum_/tgtWeightsSum_ store the sum of weights BEFORE normalisation (a coverage measure); srcMagSf_/tgtMagSf_ face areas, centroids; singlePatchProc_ (rank holding both sides or -1 if distributed); srcMapPtr_/tgtMapPtr_ distribution maps. Weights are normalised overlap-area fractions. Algorithms are plug-in classes: faceAreaWeightAMI (advancing front, derives advancingFrontAMI, ctor args requireMatch, reverseTarget, lowWeightCorrection default -1, triangulation mode, restartUncoveredSourceFace=true; methods calcInterArea, overlaps, setNextFaces), partialFaceAreaWeightAMI (reported deprecated in a dev commit - unverified), plus others (mapNearest etc. - unverified in this session). ACMI (cyclicACMIPolyPatch): computes AMI with partial face-area weighting; weight sums are fractions of local area (sum=1 = fully covered); a src/tgt mask field is derived from weight sums, clamped to [tol, 1-tol]; non-overlap part of the face is a separate "non-overlap" patch. CGNS SIDS (cgns.org/standard/SIDS/multizone.html): GridConnectivity_t with GridConnectivityType in {Overset (default), Abutting, Abutting1to1}; PointRange XOR PointList on the receiver side; PointListDonor only for Abutting1to1; CellListDonor usable for any type; InterpolantsDonor only for structured and linear elements (BAR_2, TRI_3, QUAD_4, HEXA_8); GridLocation Vertex or FaceCenter for Abutting; one interface needs TWO GridConnectivity_t records (one per side); donor info has three levels: full (ZoneDonorName+CellListDonor+InterpolantsDonor), partial (ZoneDonorName+CellListDonor), minimal (ZoneDonorName only). Code_Saturne: no interface object; joining changes the mesh, joined faces become ordinary interior faces. MEDCoupling remapper: sparse matrix W (rows=target cells T_i, columns=source cells S_j, nonzero iff intersect), phi_t = W phi_s, from remap.prepare(src,trg,"P0P0"), getCrudeMatrix(). Supermesh (Farrell 2009 thesis): common refinement built locally from element-element intersections after an element association search.
polyhedra: Joining in Code_Saturne most often yields polyhedral cells (developer Yvan Fournier on the forum; ParaView display artefacts noted). Code_Saturne is natively polyhedral (face-based), so a joined mesh needs no special cell type. OpenFOAM AMI works on arbitrary polygonal faces (primitive patches; face intersection by triangulation mode option). MEDCoupling Geometric2D handles any 2D cell incl. non-convex polygons; Triangulation and Convex are faster options. CGNS interpolants are only defined for linear standard element types, so polyhedral/arbitrary faces are poorly served by InterpolantsDonor (need CellListDonor/own weights). Takeaway: polygon-face intersection (clipping) must be first-class.
nonconformal: Detection/declaration: never inferred from topology automatically. OpenFOAM: user names two patches as cyclicAMI/nonConformalCyclic/ACMI types; AMI computed at run start/each mesh motion; requireMatch flag decides whether a full overlap is required (error otherwise); uncovered fraction shows in weight sums (<1) and is handled by lowWeightCorrection (threshold below which interpolation is deactivated, falling back to a default/zero-gradient style value; exact semantics unverified) or by ACMI masks (blend between coupled and a non-overlap boundary condition). Fluent: user sets two zones to type "interface", creates a Mesh Interface (tip: pick smaller zone as Interface Zone 1 for accuracy); Fluent intersects them and creates new wall zones for the non-overlapping regions (may be empty when one zone is contained in the other); periodic variant with translational/rotational option; TUI /mesh/non-conformals/ (old 12-era docs via mirrors). STAR-CCM+ (third-party mirror topcfd.cn of Siemens docs, unverified as official): Interface types Contact with Imprinted or Conformal connectivity; imprinted creates new faces connecting touching cells (adding vertices) via geometry-based (default; single tolerance as fraction of min edge length around vertex) or topology-based intersector; Metrics-Based option stores new faces as area and centroid vectors only with no new vertices; Conformal only keeps conformal faces and discards the rest as remainder faces; Mapped Contact does no intersection, uses proximity mapping tolerant of gaps/overlaps (for cases where >98% face match is not achievable). Code_Saturne: cs_preprocess -j/--join with face-selection sub-options; --fraction (default 0.1: fraction of smallest edge under which vertices may fuse), --plane (default 0.8: minimal cosine of normals of two coplanar faces), --semi-conf (fast, only if faces already share vertices); env CS_PREPROCESS_JOIN_MAX_SUB_FACES (default 100) caps new faces per initial face; `code_saturne check_mesh -j` to test; GUI Calculation environment / Meshes selection / Face joining. CGNS: Abutting GridConnectivity_t with receiver PointList and CellListDonor(+Interpolants); a quirk is that Abutting1to1 with unstructured PointList/PointListDonor is legal but confusing (Pointwise README). Codes that handle non-conformal natively: OpenFOAM, Fluent, STAR-CCM+, CFX (GGI, unverified), Code_Saturne (via joining), MOOSE/libMesh-style mortar for FEM (not researched here).
sets_and_partitions: OpenFOAM: interface = a boundary patch pair (patch groups; neighbourPatch keyword); ACMI adds a third non-overlap patch. Fluent: face zones typed interface, interface object named, pair of zones. CGNS: Zone-level ZoneGridConnectivity_t lists, interface relation stored per side by name/ZoneDonorName, i.e. relation expressed as named references between sets. Code_Saturne: face groups/colors used as selection criteria for joining (--color to restrict). Common pattern: interfaces are set-pairs plus a link, not entity relations; the intersection result (weights) is derived data that is cached and recomputed on motion.
strengths: Interface-object approach (OpenFOAM/CGNS) keeps both meshes untouched and original, enabling sliding/rotating meshes by recomputing weights only.
Ragged addressing+weights arrays (srcAddress/srcWeights, tgtAddress/tgtWeights) are simple, parallelisable, and symmetric (both directions stored).
Storing the unnormalised weight sum gives a built-in coverage measure that drives ACMI masks and partial-overlap handling.

Supermesh/local Galerkin projection (Farrell-Maddison 2011) gives provably conservative transfer and is the basis of OpenFOAM AMI; MEDCoupling gives the same conservative P0P0 matrix with documented intensive/extensive and conservation vs maximum-principle policies.
Joining (Code_Saturne, STAR imprinted) yields a fully conforming polyhedral mesh so every downstream solver, partitioner and post-processor works unchanged.
CGNS has three explicit donor-information levels (minimal/partial/full), a good model for 'declared vs derived' data.
weaknesses: Interfaces are user-declared pairings; no tool detects non-conformality from topology or flags accidental near-conformal gaps.

Joining is destructive and tolerance-driven (fusion fraction, coplanarity cosine, cap on sub-faces); can produce sliver faces and polyhedral artefacts, and loses the original face identity unless provenance is stored.

CGNS non-conformal support is weak for unstructured/polyhedral: InterpolantsDonor only for linear standard elements, PointListDonor only for Abutting1to1, two records per interface, and the standard text itself is awkward (noted in an averaging-interface proposal).
Gaps/overlaps (geometry mismatch) are handled ad hoc: lowWeightCorrection, requireMatch, mapped contact tolerance; behaviour differs between codes and is poorly specified.
OpenFOAM AMI class family is in flux across forks/versions (e.g. partialFaceAreaWeightAMI deprecation, lowWeightCorrection transform bug #2226 for cyclicPeriodicAMI).
lessons_for_us: Represent a non-conformal interface as a first-class DERIVED relation entity: (side A face set, side B face set, transform, tolerance, algorithm id) plus a cached sparse overlap matrix W (CSR: row=face A, col=face B, value=intersection area, optional centroid/normal) stored both ways like OpenFOAM src/tgt; keep unnormalised area sums so coverage (ACMI mask) is derivable, never stored as truth.

Make 'imprint' (user's term: information-level merge) a lazy view: an imprinted/supermesh layer holding sub-faces with provenance (parentA, parentB, area, centroid, normal) that can be either exported as a conforming polyhedral mesh (Code_Saturne/STAR-imprinted style) or kept as weights only (OpenFOAM/Fluent style, and STAR 'metrics-based' with area+centroid vector but no new vertices). Same IR, two exports.

Deliberately differ from CGNS: relation stored once with symmetric donor/receiver roles and with explicit 'declared vs derived' levels (minimal/partial/full), supports polygons/polyhedra and high-order, and does not tie weights to element type.

Detect non-conformality as a mesh-check query rather than user guess: face-pair candidates from coplanarity (cosine threshold like --plane 0.8), distance within tolerance fraction of min edge (like --fraction 0.1), plus boundary faces left unmatched; report coverage fraction per interface and fail or warn per a requireMatch policy.

Expose conservation policy explicitly (MEDCoupling table): intensive vs extensive, conservative vs maximum-principle, and note they cannot both hold when coverage < 1; for neutron transport, flux/current conservation across interface needs the area-overlap matrix with exact reciprocity (W_AB area == W_BA area), which AMI's two-way storage supports.

Specify the geometric tolerance and intersection algorithm (advancing front over face adjacency, seeded; triangulation of polygons; robust predicates) as pluggable nodes in the DAG: 'interface-detect', 'face-intersect', 'weights', 'imprint-export'. Provide provenance maps so that CAD/partition layers (material, surface id) survive the imprint.

Store transforms for periodic/rotating pairs as part of the interface (Fluent translational/rotational periodic, OpenFOAM cyclicAMI), including the known pitfall that values like lowWeightCorrection must be transformed with the local side (issue #2226): keep tolerance values frame-independent.

For parallel: follow OpenFOAM singlePatchProc/distribution maps idea, i.e. interface weights computed on gathered or map-distributed geometry; keep partition-local CSR plus a distribution map, but this is unverified from source in this session.
spec_quality: CGNS has a formal, versioned SIDS spec, but its non-conformal/unstructured interface part is weak and awkward (see weaknesses). OpenFOAM has no spec: behaviour is defined by source and varies between ESI and Foundation forks. Fluent/STAR-CCM+ are proprietary documentation only. MEDCoupling documents the math well but not the matrix storage format or tolerances. Code_Saturne documents joining via man page/user guide with parameters.
storage: OpenFOAM AMI weights are in memory (recomputed at runtime, not a mesh file artefact); CGNS stores connectivity records in HDF5/ADF; Code_Saturne writes the joined mesh to its own preprocessed .csm file (unverified). MEDCoupling matrix is a sparse structure returned by getCrudeMatrix() (layout unspecified in the docs fetched).
parallel: OpenFOAM AMI carries singlePatchProc_ (-1 if distributed) and srcMapPtr_/tgtMapPtr_ distribution maps with comm_/geomComm_ communicators, so weights are computed after redistributing remote geometry; details of ghosting not verified. Code_Saturne joining is done in parallel in the preprocessor stage (unverified). Not researched for Fluent/STAR.
geometry_association: None of these tie interfaces to CAD B-rep; interfaces are mesh-boundary face groups (patches/zones/colors). For our IR this is an opportunity: an interface could reference the B-rep face pair (or an imprint of B-rep faces) so the non-conformal relation is generated from geometry rather than guessed from mesh.
high_order: Not documented in the sources checked. CGNS InterpolantsDonor is limited to linear elements. Farrell-Maddison Galerkin projection supports arbitrary-order fields on the supermesh (from the abstract, general formulation), but curved-face intersection is not covered. Mark as largely unverified.
ecosystem: OpenFOAM (ESI and Foundation), Ansys Fluent (TUI /mesh/non-conformals, journal files), Siemens STAR-CCM+, Code_Saturne (cs_preprocess, also couples via MEDCoupling intersector cs_medcoupling_intersector), SALOME/MEDCoupling, CGNS (many solvers and tools such as Pointwise), Firedrake/Fluidity-lineage supermesh code (libsupermesh, unverified).

corrections.claim: Code_Saturne joins non-conformal faces in preprocessing via `cs_preprocess -j/--join` with `--fraction` (default 0.1), `--plane` (default 0.8 = minimal cosine of normals), `--semi-conf`, env var CS_PREPROCESS_JOIN_MAX_SUB_FACES (default 100), and `code_saturne check_mesh -j`.
corrections.correction: All of this is from an obsolete preprocessor-era man page. Current code_saturne (user guide 9.2) states joining and periodicity are done by the SOLVER (kernel), the Preprocessor only imports meshes and checks element orientation; the current preprocessor option list has no --join. Current API: `cs_join_add(sel_criteria, fraction, plane, verbosity, visualization)` with `fraction` default 0.1 (0 < r < 0.49, multiplies the shortest incident edge length) and `plane` in DEGREES, default 25° (max angle between normals for coplanarity), plus `cs_join_set_advanced_param(join_num, mtf=1 default, pmf, tcm=1 default, icm=1 default, max_break, max_sub_faces, tml, tmb, tmr, tmr_distrib)`. `--semi-conf` and the env var have no documented modern equivalent (max_sub_faces replaces the env var). `check_mesh -j` only appears in old forum posts; unverified for current versions.

corrections.claim: Code_Saturne writes the joined mesh to its own preprocessed .csm file (unverified).
corrections.correction: Now verified but with corrected roles: the Preprocessor writes `mesh_input.csm` (un-joined import); the Solver, when preprocessing stages (joining, periodicity, smoothing) effectively modify the mesh, writes `mesh_output.csm`, usable directly as input for a later run. The `.csm` extension was introduced in release 6.1.0 (NEWS.md); older `mesh_input`/`mesh_output` names without extension remain accepted. Since 6.3.0 .csm is treated like an external format (read without the Preprocessor).

corrections.claim: Supermesh/local Galerkin projection (Farrell-Maddison 2011) gives provably conservative transfer and is the basis of OpenFOAM AMI.
corrections.correction: AMIInterpolation.H does cite Farrell & Maddison 2011 (CMAME 200:89-100) as the algorithm basis, but AMI is an interpolation (weighted sum) and the OpenFOAM Foundation itself states AMI fluxes 'are not guaranteed to be conservative' (≈0.1% channel conservation error that never returns to zero; spurious ~40 kPa pressure rise in a closed mixer), and that ACMI is 'completely unreliable unless the coupled patches are entirely flat' because its weights do not sum to unity on curved patches. The conservative property belongs to the full Galerkin projection, not to AMI's one-sided weight application.

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM: user names two patches as cyclicAMI/nonConformalCyclic/ACMI types; AMI class family is in flux across forks.
corrections.correction: The two forks have diverged into different architectures and should not be lumped together. ESI (openfoam.com, v2506) still ships cyclicAMI, cyclicACMI (cyclicACMIPolyPatch with nonOverlapPatch, srcMask/tgtMask, reportCoverage) and AMI methods faceAreaWeightAMI, faceAreaWeightAMI2D (AABB-tree, added June 2021), nearestFaceAMI; partialFaceAreaWeightAMI was deprecated in commit ba4d38da (June 2021) and is absent from the v2506 API. The Foundation (openfoam.org) introduced Non-Conformal Coupling (NCC) in dev on 18 May 2022, removed ACMI and Repeat AMI then, kept AMI only through v10 (July 2022); v11 release notes say 'NCC replaces AMI', and cyclicAMIPolyPatch no longer exists in the v12 API (404). With NCC the user does NOT set patch types manually: `createNonConformalCouples` creates zero-face `nonConformalCyclic` patches (plus nonConformalError, and since v12 nonConformalMappedWall for multi-region and nonConformalProcessorCyclic for decomposition).

corrections.claim: There are two opposite philosophies: (A) separate sides + runtime interface object with weights, (B) merge/join in preprocessing into a conforming polyhedral mesh.
corrections.correction: There is a third, established philosophy that is exactly the user's 'imprint at the information level': runtime topological stitching without touching the stored mesh. OpenFOAM Foundation NCC: the polyMesh is unchanged (nonConformalPolyPatch 'is a placeholder and must have no faces'); the fvMeshStitcher adds real intersection faces to the finite-volume mesh only, assigns their Sf/Cf from the patchToPatches::intersection, keeps `polyFacesBf` (map from each fv face to its parent poly face), supports connect/disconnect/reconnect, 'conform/unconform' operations with mesh-flux correction, and 'stabilisation geometry' (small values, no cutting) when cutting cannot run. Result: 'the mesh is closed, area vectors sum to zero for each cell', conservation follows from standard FV. STAR-CCM+ 'Metrics-Based' intersection (new faces as metrics, no new vertices) is the same idea. The report's lesson #2 ('imprint as lazy view, same IR two exports') therefore has an existing baseline to cite.

corrections.claim: In every system 'which faces are non-conformal' is NOT detected automatically; no tool detects non-conformality / pairs interfaces automatically.
corrections.correction: Overstated. Fluent's current solver API has `auto_create` ('Automatically pair and create mesh interfaces for some or all interface zones'), `one_to_one_pairing` (default one-to-one creation method), `create_manually` (pair even if not overlapping), and `delete_interfaces_with_small_overlap`. STAR-CCM+ also auto-creates interfaces from part contacts (not fetched; unverified). What is true: no FV code infers non-conformality from mesh topology alone; pairing is geometric proximity between user-typed interface zones. Lesson #4 is a smaller differentiator than claimed.

corrections.claim: CGNS InterpolantsDonor only for structured and linear elements (BAR_2, TRI_3, QUAD_4, HEXA_8).
corrections.correction: SIDS lists InterpolantsDonor as defined for structured grids and the unstructured linear types BAR_2, TRI_3, QUAD_4, TETRA_4, PYRA_5, PENTA_6 and HEXA_8 (the report omitted the three 3D simplex/prism types). The rest of the CGNS GridConnectivity_t summary (Overset default, PointRange XOR PointList, PointListDonor only Abutting1to1, CellListDonor any type, GridLocation Vertex/FaceCenter for Abutting vs Vertex/CellCenter for Overset, two records per Abutting interface, full/partial/minimal donor levels) is verified.

corrections.claim: srcWeightsSum_/tgtWeightsSum_ store the sum of weights BEFORE normalisation; lesson: 'keep unnormalised area sums'.
corrections.correction: In ESI v2506 `AMIInterpolation::normaliseWeights`, `wghtSum[facei] = sum(w)/patchAreas[facei]`, i.e. the stored sum is the COVERAGE FRACTION (overlap area / face area), not a raw area sum. Weights themselves are divided by face area when `conformal=false`, or by their own sum (so they sum to 1) when `conformal=true`; `agglomerate` always uses conformal=true for the source side. Faces with no overlap get wghtSum=0.

corrections.claim: lowWeightCorrection: threshold below which interpolation is deactivated, falling back to a default/zero-gradient style value; exact semantics unverified.
corrections.correction: Now verified: in `weightedSum`, if `lowWeightCorrection > 0` and `weightsSum[facei] < lowWeightCorrection` then `result[facei] = defaultValues[facei]` (caller-supplied per-face defaults, not zero-gradient); FatalError if `defaultValues.size()` differs from the target (interpolateToTarget) or source (interpolateToSource) patch size. Dictionary default is -1 (disabled); only written when > 0. Mark as verified.

corrections.claim: partialFaceAreaWeightAMI (reported deprecated in a dev commit - unverified), plus others (mapNearest etc. - unverified).
corrections.correction: Verified: deprecated in ESI commit ba4d38da 'ENH: AMI improvements' (June 2021, 'primarily used by ACMI; functionality now offered by the AMI variants'), still present in the v2012 API tree, absent from v2506 (class page 404). v2506 AMI methods are advancingFrontAMI (base) -> faceAreaWeightAMI, faceAreaWeightAMI2D; and nearestFaceAMI. 'mapNearest' was not found in v2506; drop it. faceAreaWeightAMI ctor defaults confirmed: requireMatch, reverseTarget=false, lowWeightCorrection=-1, triMode=tmMesh (other value tmFan), restartUncoveredSourceFace=true.

corrections.claim: STAR-CCM+ Mapped Contact does no intersection, uses proximity mapping tolerant of gaps/overlaps (for cases where >98% face match is not achievable); imprinted uses a single tolerance as a fraction of min edge length around a vertex.
corrections.correction: The cited mirror page (Simcenter STAR-CCM+ 2406) contains no '98%' statement and no tolerance definition. It describes Mapped Contact as an indirect interface using a proximity algorithm (Mapped Interface Tolerance: Minimum Proximity relative to cell size, Minimum Angle between normals), splitting faces into associated/disassociated sets, with two stencils: Compact (nearest-neighbour + area-ratio weights) and Imprint ('better connectivity' but 'can fail in the case of poor quality meshes'), and a diagnostic field 'Mapped Facet Area Match' (≈1.0 = good). So Mapped Contact can also imprint. Verified on the other page: Conformal (discards non-conformal faces as remainder faces, no new vertices), Imprinted (geometry- or topology-based direct intersector, adds vertices), Metrics-Based (no new vertices, better performance for sliding motion).
