corrections.claim: Joining in Code_Saturne most often yields polyhedral cells (developer Yvan Fournier on the forum, viewtopic.php?p=3913; ParaView display artefacts noted).
corrections.correction: The cited thread returns 404. Code_Saturne being natively face-based (so joined faces simply become interior faces and no special cell type is needed) is confirmed by other forum posts, and the GUI path 'Calculation Environment / Meshes selection / Face joining' is confirmed, but the specific 'most often polyhedral' quote and ParaView artefact attribution could not be verified.

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM issue #2226 at develop.openfoam.com (lowWeightCorrection transform bug for cyclicPeriodicAMI).
corrections.correction: Content confirmed (cyclicPeriodicAMI transforms lowWeightCorrection values with the neighbour transform instead of the local one; reproduces with differing face counts and lowWeightCorrection=1; dev version Sept 2021), but the tracker moved: develop.openfoam.com now shows only a sign-in page; the live issue is https://gitlab.com/openfoam/core/openfoam/-/issues/2226. Status/fix version not stated on the page.

corrections.claim: Fluent TUI /mesh/non-conformals/ (old 12-era docs via mirrors).
corrections.correction: `/mesh/non-conformals/` is the Fluent MESHING-mode TUI (pyfluent meshing docs). In SOLVER mode, interfaces live under `/define/mesh-interfaces/` (settings object `mesh_interfaces` with `mapped_interface_options`, `non_conformal_interface_numerics`, `lean_memory_mode`, `auto_options`, `turbo_interface`). The Fluent 12.0 (2009) user guide is the source for 'fluxes computed on faces produced by intersecting the two zones', the interior + wall zones creation and the 'smaller zone as Interface Zone 1' tip; those are confirmed but 17 years old.

corrections.claim: High-order: Farrell-Maddison supports arbitrary-order fields but curved-face intersection is not covered; largely unverified.
corrections.correction: MEDCoupling's Geometric2D intersector explicitly handles 'any 2D cell: linear, quadratic, convex and non-convex polygons', i.e. curved (quadratic-edge) 2D cells are supported for conservative P0P0 intersection (slower than Triangulation/Convex). So curved-edge supermeshing exists in 2D in a production library; curved-face 3D surface intersection remains uncovered (MEDCoupling 3D-surface supports only tri/quad meshes).

corrections.claim: OpenFOAM AMI parallel: singlePatchProc_ (-1 if distributed), srcMapPtr_/tgtMapPtr_ with comm_/geomComm_; details unverified.
corrections.correction: Member list and comments confirmed from v2506 API: singlePatchProc_ 'Index of processor that holds all of both sides. -1 for distributed cases'; comm_ 'Communicator to use for parallel operations'; geomComm_ 'Communicator for geometry calculations, -1 on processors without faces'; srcMapPtr_/tgtMapPtr_ 'parallel running only'; also srcCentroids_/tgtCentroids_, srcPatchPts_/tgtPatchPts_ (manipulated/projected points), upToDate_. Mark as verified. Note this is AMI (ESI) only; Foundation NCC handles parallel via nonConformalProcessorCyclic patches created by decomposePar (v12) and works with load-balancing redistribution and adaptive refinement.

missing_important: OpenFOAM Foundation NCC (v10+) is the closest existing analogue of the proposed 'imprint as a lazy information-layer view': stored polyMesh untouched + runtime-cut FV faces with provenance (polyFacesBf: fv face -> parent poly face), Sf/Cf from intersection, nonConformalError patch for uncovered parts, checkMesh -allGeometry writes NCC coverage (v11), 'stitched' output to avoid visualisation discontinuities (v11), and reuse of the same patchToPatches::intersection engine for the stitchMesh utility (v12). The design doc should name it as the baseline to differ from.

CGNS already has native polyhedra: NGON_n (all faces) + NFACE_n (cells as face lists) + ElementStartOffset (offset array, replaced the older per-element count-prefix layout; introduced via CPEX 0041, CGNS 4.x) + optional ParentElements (face -> two cells) / ParentElementsPosition. The report's claim that CGNS 'poorly serves polyhedral' is true only for interface interpolants; the cell representation itself is a face-based database very close to the user's model, and current SIDS text is stated consistent with CGNS 4.2.

MEDCoupling intersector limits relevant to 'polygon-face intersection must be first-class': 3D SURFACE intersection (the case for non-planar interface patches) supports only mixed triangle/quadrangle meshes (projection on a median plane, MedianPlane=0.5, Precision 1e-12 scaled, MaxDistance3DSurfIntersect=-1 disables), i.e. arbitrary polygonal faces are NOT supported there; 3D VOLUME Triangulation (Grandy 1999) handles arbitrary non-convex polyhedra with hex SplittingPolicy (PLANAR_FACE_5 default, PLANAR_FACE_6, GENERAL_24, GENERAL_48). 2D Convex intersector is limited to tri/quad meshes.

MEDCoupling field-nature semantics are a good spec to copy: IntensiveMaximum (integral conserved, cell sum not), ExtensiveConservation (cell sum conserved, integral not); transferField without a nature raises an exception; getCrudeMatrix returns per-target-cell {sourceCellId: intersection area} rows (row sums should be 1 for full coverage).

Fluent 12 geometric constraints for non-conformal interfaces: gap between the two interface zones must not exceed the adjacent cell size, no cell may be fully enclosed between two interfaces, each cell zone needs a distinct face zone on the interface, periodic rotational angle must divide 360, and 'periodic repeats' requires one pair of conformal periodic zones per interface zone (3D: at most one). Fluent also has 'Mapped' interfaces (mapped_interface_options: tolerance, frequency, under-relaxation) as its gap-tolerant alternative, mirroring STAR Mapped Contact.

ACMI mask tolerance in Foundation v8 is a hard-coded static `tolerance_ = 1e-10` (not user-configurable); the non-overlap patch face areas are scaled by (1 - mask) so uncovered area is preserved on the non-overlap patch. ESI v2506 cyclicACMIPolyPatch retains this design (scalePatchFaceAreas 'to maintain physical area', reportCoverage uncovered/blended/covered counts) with default AMI method faceAreaWeightAMI.

libsupermesh is real and maintained: github.com/firedrakeproject/libsupermesh, v2025.3.0 (tag), LGPL-2.0-or-later, CMake + MPI + gfortran, depends on libspatialindex; also on PyPI. Farrell thesis confirmed: 'Galerkin projection of discrete fields via supermesh construction', Imperial College, 2009 (awarded Jan 2010).

CGNS Pointwise README confirms the unstructured-interface gap: GridConnectivity1to1_t only allows PointRange/PointRangeDonor (structured), so unstructured 1-to-1 interfaces must use GridConnectivity_t with GridConnectivityType=Abutting1to1 and PointList/PointListDonor; interior interface Elements_t need ParentElements filled from both sides; hybrid structured/unstructured interfaces lack a standard way to express the cell face (proposed user-defined PointListPosition/PointRangeDonor).

Code_Saturne joining diagnostics worth copying: `visualization>=1` in cs_join_add writes a JOINING.case post-processing output of the joined faces; advanced params expose the tolerance computation mode (tcm=2 scales by sin of edge angles), pre-merge factor, intersection algorithm choice (icm 1/2), and an octree search (tml/tmb/tmr) - a concrete pluggable-node decomposition matching the report's DAG proposal.

topic: Non-conforming meshes in neutron transport codes (DFEM-SN and Monte Carlo)
summary: Verified from primary sources: (1) The transport codes I could check treat mesh connectivity as a face-adjacency graph that is built assuming conformity, and handle non-conformity by making the mesh conform at the data level rather than by integrating mortars. PDT "stitches" hanging nodes at subset boundaries into degenerate polygons, which its PWLD basis tolerates (Ghaddar and Ragusa, M&C 2017). Serpent reads OpenFOAM polyMesh (points, faces, owner, neighbour), which is conformal by construction, and internally converts everything to tetrahedra (Serpent user guide, via search summary). (2) Monte Carlo codes keep geometry and mesh separate: DAGMC requires a watertight, imprinted-and-merged triangle surface mesh in .h5m. OpenMC unstructured tally meshes (MOAB .h5/.vtk, libMesh .exo) are overlays on that geometry, so no conformity is required between the two, and volumes are recovered by ray-tracing (OpenMC docs). (3) DG SN with true hanging nodes exists mostly in academic work (Owens thesis 2017, 2D isogeometric, with conservative upwinding across hanging nodes and cycle-breaking; Ragusa and Wang two-mesh AMR; Haut et al. 2019 on cycle-breaking for curved high-order meshes). Production-code detail for Griffin/Rattlesnake, Denovo, Thor and Lupine was NOT obtainable: several primary sites returned 403/429, so those claims are marked unverified. Net: the neutron-transport ecosystem has no common mesh IR. Each code accepts a different format (Exodus, OpenFOAM polyMesh, .h5m, STL, Abaqus), and non-conformal support is rare and ad hoc.
data_model:
Verified data layouts:
- OpenFOAM polyMesh (read by Serpent): `points` (list of vectors); `faces` (each face is a list of point indices, so arbitrary polygons); `owner` (cell label per face); `neighbour` (cell label for internal faces); `boundary` (patches, each with type, nFaces, startFace). Internal faces come first, then boundary faces grouped by patch. An internal face's normal points from the lower-labelled cell to the higher-labelled one, and a boundary face has no neighbour. Serpent's variant uses zero-based indexing and requires the face normal to point outward from the owner cell (doc.cfd.direct mesh-description; Serpent polymesh guide, via search summary). Cells must be closed geometrically and topologically. Face-based storage means polyhedral cells fall out for free, but the cell-to-face list has to be derived.
- OpenMC UnstructuredMesh Python object: `vertices`, `connectivity` of shape (n_elements, 8) (added in 0.13.1), `element_types`, `volumes`, `centroids`, `bounding_box`, `length_multiplier`. The docs do not say how tets are stored in an 8-column array; I would guess padded, but that is unverified.
- DAGMC: a triangle surface mesh per CAD surface in MOAB .h5m, with parent-child links from surfaces to volumes. Materials come from CAD-side tags (UWUW libraries). Volumes are never meshed.
- PDT: 2D PSLG meshed per orthogonal "subset" with the Triangle mesh generator, then extruded in z. Subsets are aggregated into "cellsets". The result is a conformal mesh with degenerate polygons at subset borders.
- Haut et al. 2019: a directed weighted graph with elements as vertices and upwind face dependencies as edges. Cycles are broken by removing a minimum-weight edge set, and the broken edges are lagged in the sweep.
- Cycle-free Voronoi sweeping (arXiv 2412.01660): the dual graph of any Voronoi tessellation can be topologically sorted for any direction.
Unverified: Griffin/Rattlesnake/MOOSE internal layout (libMesh elements, Exodus input), and the exact element-face storage in Denovo, Thor and Lupine.
polyhedra:
Verified:
- OpenFOAM polyMesh and Serpent: arbitrary polyhedra are read natively, but Serpent converts all unstructured meshes to tetrahedra internally after reading (Serpent user guide, via search summary).
- PDT/Hackemack: PWLD DFEM on arbitrary polygons and polyhedra, plus a quadratic serendipity extension (TAMU Multiphysics group page; Hackemack J. Comput. Phys. 2018 as cited in the MDPI paper). The 3D high-order basis in the MDPI Bernstein-Bezier paper is limited to extruded polygonal prisms.
- Cycle-free Voronoi sweep paper: targets polytopal (Voronoi) cells.
- A search summary says Griffin/Rattlesnake DFEM-SN works on arbitrary polygonal/polyhedral meshes; I did not confirm this from a primary source (unverified).
- OpenMC/MOAB/libMesh: the docs describe tet/hex-style elements (connectivity shape n x 8). No polyhedra support was found.
- DAGMC: triangles only, since it is a surface representation.
- Implication: polyhedra are first-class only in face-based formats (OpenFOAM) and in the research DFEM codes. Element-based formats (Exodus, MOAB) do not carry them in the common path.
nonconformal:
Findings by mechanism:
1. Avoid it. PDT stitches hanging nodes into degenerate polygons so the mesh is topologically conformal (Ghaddar and Ragusa, M&C 2017). Serpent, via OpenFOAM polyMesh, assumes strictly conformal owner/neighbour faces. DAGMC requires imprint and merge, and the docs state that unmerged surfaces and overlaps are not yet supported. OpenMC states that unmerged surfaces and small overlaps may be supported in future.
2. Overlay (geometry-independent mesh). OpenMC unstructured tally meshes need not conform to the CSG or DAGMC geometry. Per-element material volumes are estimated by ray-casting along x, y and z (`material_volumes()`), so a mesh element straddling two materials gets a fractional volume per material. This is detection-free: the mesh and the geometry are simply two independent layers.
3. Hanging nodes in DG SN. Owens (Imperial EngD thesis 2017, 2D isogeometric) introduces hanging nodes and addresses conservative upwinding across curved boundaries containing them, plus cycle-breaking for a unique sweep order. Ragusa and Wang (J. Comput. Appl. Math. 2010) give a two-mesh AMR technique for DGFEM SN, and Wang and Ragusa (Nucl. Sci. Eng. 2010) give DSA on locally refined unstructured meshes. A Chinese-journal paper reports tree-based hex grids with hanging nodes and a modified sweep order (authors unverified). In DG, upwinding is a face integral. At a hanging face the coarse face is split into sub-faces matching the fine neighbours, and the upwind flux is integrated per sub-face. The mortar and hanging-node literature (MFEM non-conforming refinement, arXiv 1905.04033) supports this.
4. Mortar. MOOSE has segment-based mortar constraints, extended to 3D in 2021 (MOOSE newsletter Oct 2021 and Constraints docs). It is used for contact/gap-type problems, not for SN transport that I could verify.
Detection: none of the sources describe an explicit "imprint status" or conformity flag. Conformity is implicit (a face has exactly one neighbour). OpenFOAM's AMI/nonConformalCyclic exists, but I could not verify details because the page I fetched did not cover them. Unverified: how Griffin's sweeper handles hanging nodes. I could not read the Griffin docs or the Prince et al. 2024 paper (403/429).
sets_and_partitions:
Verified:
- OpenFOAM polyMesh: boundary patches (type, nFaces, startFace) are contiguous ranges of boundary faces. Cell zones are not covered by the pages I read (unverified).
- Serpent: the file set (points, faces, owner, neighbour, plus a materials file) separates mesh from material assignment, but I could not read the Serpent wiki, so the details are unverified. Interface types 7/8/9 (OpenFOAM-based, many-material, and mesh plus geometry creation) come from search snippets. A search summary says STL geometry carries no material information.
- DAGMC: materials via CAD-side tags and UWUW libraries, with `replace_material_assignment()` and `add_material_override()` in OpenMC. Cell and surface IDs come from the CAD engine and can clash with CSG IDs (`auto_ids`). `sync_dagmc_universes()` makes per-cell materials for depletion.
- OpenMC unstructured meshes are tally containers. Materials come from the geometry layer, never the mesh, which is a clean separation of the geometry, material and mesh layers.
- PDT: "subsets" and "cellsets" are partition constructs for parallelism, distinct from materials.
Takeaway for the three-layer model: DAGMC plus OpenMC already realise "geometry layer (B-rep or facets) / material partition (tags) / mesh layer (tally overlay)" as three loosely coupled things, with association by ray tracing rather than stored links.
strengths: OpenFOAM polyMesh (Serpent): a face-based owner/neighbour layout is minimal and handles arbitrary polyhedra natively; internal and boundary faces are cheap to iterate.
OpenMC: mesh and geometry are decoupled by ray-traced volume apportionment, which makes non-conformal overlays trivial and robust.
DAGMC: watertight facet geometry plus tag-based materials gives a simple CAD-to-MC path and a shared standard.
PDT: degenerate-polygon stitching reuses a conformal data structure with no extra face logic, because PWLD tolerates degenerate polygons.

Haut et al. and the Voronoi sweep paper show that sweep scheduling reduces to a directed graph over faces, with cycle-breaking by weighted edge removal, so the face-adjacency graph is the key object for deterministic transport.
weaknesses: Fragmented ecosystem: Exodus (libMesh/MOOSE/OpenMC), .h5m (DAGMC), OpenFOAM polyMesh (Serpent), STL (Serpent, no materials), Abaqus (MCNP) and PSLG (PDT) all coexist, with no common mesh IR.
Serpent flattens polyhedra to tets, and OpenMC's connectivity is (n, 8), so polyhedra and high-order cells are not preserved end-to-end.
True non-conformal DG SN is mostly academic (2D, isogeometric, AMR). I found no production code with documented, general 3D polyhedral hanging-face upwinding (Griffin unverified).

Conformity is implicit in all of these formats, with no explicit record of imprinted versus non-imprinted shared geometry. DAGMC imprint/merge failures cause lost particles (OpenMC discourse threads on overlaps and force-merging).
OpenMC unstructured tallies are costly: the tutorial says the particle rate drops dramatically in active cycles. PUMI-Tally (arXiv 2504.19048, a 2025 GPU tally library) targets this.
Mortar methods in MOOSE are fragile on triangular interface faces (MOOSE Constraints docs).
lessons_for_us: Make the face-adjacency graph a first-class stored relation, in the OpenFOAM owner/neighbour style: each face lists 1 or 2 cells. Add an explicit 'interface' entity for non-conformal pairs. This is the single object that sweeps, upwinding, DG fluxes and partitioning all consume.

Represent a non-conformal interface as a first-class record: {face-set A, face-set B, kind: conformal | hanging | mortar-overlap | sliding, optional precomputed intersection polygons (sub-face segments with parent-face ids and areas)}. Hanging nodes become a degenerate case of the same record. This is what OpenFOAM, Serpent, PDT, DAGMC and OpenMC all lack.

Deliberately differ from PDT and Serpent: do not require conformity or degenerate-polygon stitching, and do not flatten polyhedra to tets on read. Keep cells as polyhedra with a derived tet decomposition cache for consumers that need it.

Adopt OpenMC's decoupling of mesh and geometry. Store explicit mesh-to-geometry association (cell-to-volume id, face-to-surface id) so that a ray-traced overlay is not required. Keep the overlay path as one more mechanism by which the mesh layer can relate to the geometry layer.
Adopt DAGMC's tag-based material model for the partition layer, but make it a typed set (name, kind) so materials, boundary sets and colours are all queryable sets over the same entity ids.

Detection of non-conformity: store an 'imprint status' on every shared geometry face (imprinted/merged vs coincident-but-unmerged vs overlapping). Run a validator at mesh-write time, and verify watertightness and conformity as DAGMC's tools do, instead of discovering overlaps at tracking time.

Provide a sweep-oriented derived view: directed upwind graph per angle with cycle detection and weighted edge removal (Haut et al.), cached lazily. This gives deterministic-transport consumers the main thing they need.

Export strategy: IR to Exodus (libMesh/OpenMC), to .h5m (DAGMC, triangles only), to OpenFOAM polyMesh (Serpent, conformal polyhedra only), and to an own columnar format for the neutron-transport code. Each exporter should declare which IR features it loses, for example polyhedra, high-order cells or non-conformal interfaces.

Verify before relying on it: how Griffin, Denovo, Thor and Lupine actually treat non-conformal faces. I could not read their docs (403/429), so ask for or fetch the source before fixing the first consumer's format.

corrections.claim: Polyhedra are first-class only in face-based formats (OpenFOAM) and research DFEM codes; element-based formats (Exodus, MOAB) do not carry them in the common path.
corrections.correction: The formats do carry arbitrary polyhedra. Exodus II: element blocks of type "nfaced" whose elements are lists of faces from "nsided" face blocks (seacas test: ex_put_block(EX_FACE_BLOCK, "nsided") + ex_put_block(EX_ELEM_BLOCK, "nfaced")). MOAB: MBPOLYGON and MBPOLYHEDRON entity types (polyhedron connectivity = its faces). libMesh: C0POLYGON/C0POLYHEDRON (enum 40, "arbitrary polyhedron whose faces are C0POLYGON sides"); MOOSE Aug-2026 newsletter lists parallel comm, ExodusII and CheckpointIO support and quality metrics for them, plus a polyhedronElemSplitter to TET4. CGNS: NGON_n (faces) + NFACE_n (polyhedra as face lists) with ParentElements giving the two adjacent cells per face (0 at boundary), i.e. owner/neighbour on polyhedral zones. What is uneven is consumer/tooling support (ParaView Exodus polyhedra reader bug 2016; OpenMC exports only tet4/hex8; Griffin unknown). For an IR-with-exporters design, the distinction 'format carries it vs consumer reads it' is the point.

corrections.claim: None of the sources describe an explicit conformity flag; a first-class non-conformal interface record is what OpenFOAM, Serpent, PDT, DAGMC and OpenMC all lack.
corrections.correction: True of the five neutronics consumers surveyed, false for the format landscape. CGNS SIDS has first-class GridConnectivityType_t = {Abutting1to1, Abutting (non-1to1 = 'patched or mismatched'), Overset}; mismatched interfaces use receiver PointList (Vertex or FaceCenter) + CellListDonor, optionally InterpolantsDonor; GridConnectivity_t 'may be used for any mix of structured and unstructured zones'. Exploitable gap: InterpolantsDonor is defined only for structured grids and BAR_2/TRI_3/QUAD_4/TETRA_4/PYRA_5/PENTA_6/HEXA_8, so mismatched-abutting on polyhedral NGON/NFACE zones is CellListDonor-only (no stored intersection polygons/weights). OpenFOAM (openfoam.org) v10 added Non-Conformal Coupling that 'connects regions of a domain with independent meshes', 'replacing the unreliable, inaccurate AMI and ACMI'; AMI to be removed after v10 (openfoam.com/ESI line still documents cyclicAMI). The baseline 'conceptually similar to X' should be CGNS GridConnectivity, not 'nobody has it'.

corrections.claim: Production-code detail for Thor (listed among Griffin/Denovo/Lupine as DFEM-SN codes to verify for non-conformal face handling).
corrections.correction: THOR (NCSU, MIT license, github.com/NCSU-NCSG/THOR) is an AHOT-C (arbitrarily high-order transport, characteristic) code on unstructured tetrahedral grids; meshes come from Gmsh via OpenMeshConverter into THOR's own format. Not DFEM, tets only, no polyhedra, so it is not a polyhedral/non-conformal target.
corrections.source: https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/items/28046e6e-80be-470e-97af-4f1dca3cc03d ; https://git.tdem.in/NCSU-NCSG/THOR (search summaries; repo README not fetched)

corrections.claim: Unverified: the exact element-face storage in Denovo.
corrections.correction: Moot: Denovo is a 3-D SN code on XYZ orthogonal (Cartesian) meshes with KBA sweeps; Exnihilo ray-traces arbitrary CAD/CSG geometry onto that grid with volume-mixed materials per cell (SCALE DEVC samples volume fractions per voxel). It is another 'overlay' mechanism like OpenMC, not an unstructured consumer.

corrections.claim: Lupine is a neutron transport code whose non-conformal handling should be verified.
corrections.correction: A targeted search found no deterministic or Monte Carlo transport code named Lupine. Ask the user which code is meant before treating it as a consumer; do not assert nonexistence.
corrections.source: WebSearch '"Lupine" neutron transport code discrete ordinates' returned no match

corrections.claim: OpenMC/MOAB/libMesh: docs describe tet/hex-style elements (connectivity n x 8); no polyhedra support; tets probably padded but unverified.
corrections.correction: Padding confirmed in src/mesh.cpp: 4-node element -> LINEAR_TET, 4 node ids + four -1; 8-node -> LINEAR_HEX; anything else -> UNSUPPORTED, row all -1, skipped with warning 'not of type linear tet/hex'. That is an export (HDF5/connectivity) limit, not a tally limit. MOAB path is effectively tets (warning 'Non-tetrahedral elements found', kd-tree over MBTET). libMesh path has no element-type gate; a maintainer forum post shows hex+prism tallies working, though sample_element fills a 4-position array. Also: 'LibMesh tallies require a replicated mesh'; 'Unstructured mesh surface tallies are not implemented'; an AdaptiveLibMesh class handles non-contiguous element ids from refinement (Exodus output disabled for adaptive meshes).

corrections.claim: OpenMC unstructured tally mesh volumes are recovered by ray-tracing.
corrections.correction: Element volumes come from the mesh library (libMesh elem.volume() x length_multiplier^3; MOAB tet volumes). Only per-element material apportionment is ray-traced: material_volumes() ('Added in version 0.15.1'), three ray sets parallel to x, y, z, n_samples default 10000 split by bounding-box aspect ratio, max_materials default 4.

corrections.claim: DAGMC docs state that unmerged surfaces and overlaps are not yet supported.
corrections.correction: Misattributed. That is OpenMC's geometry guide: 'DAGMC geometries used in OpenMC are currently required to be clean' (all surfaces imprinted and merged, watertight) and 'Future implementations of DAGMC geometry will support small volume overlaps and un-merged surfaces.' DAGMC's own page only says 'all of the surfaces must be imprinted and merged' for optimal results and recommends the make_watertight tool.

corrections.claim: PDT 'avoids' non-conformity by stitching hanging nodes into degenerate polygons (framed as a PDT-specific workaround, mechanism 1).
corrections.correction: Verbatim confirmed: 'Discontinuities along the boundary are fixed by "stitching" hanging nodes, creating degenerate polygons along subset boundaries. Because PDT's spatial discretization employs Piece-Wise Linear Discontinuous (PWLD) finite element basis functions, there is no problem solving on degenerate polygons' (Ghaddar & Ragusa, M&C 2017, 'An Approach for Load Balancing Massively Parallel Transport Sweeps on Unstructured Grids'). But this is the canonical PWL design intent, not a PDT quirk: Bailey/Adams 2003 present PWL as 'promising for transport on spatial grids that have local refinement'; 2004: PWL diffusion 'on arbitrary polygonal (2D) or polyhedral (3D) grids'; OpenSn's PWLD page states the same. A hanging node is just one more polygon vertex, so a polyhedral-first IR represents hanging-node refinement with no special interface record. The paper also concedes the extruded-2D mesh 'is not as good as general an unstructured grid as a tetrahedral grid'.

corrections.claim: Haut et al. 2019: cycles are broken by removing a minimum-weight edge set.
corrections.correction: arXiv 1810.11080 (Haut, Maginot, Tomov, Southworth, Brunner, Bailey; v1 Oct 2018, rev. Jan 2019): edges are removed 'in a way that approximately minimizes the sum of removed edge weights'; lagging of removed dependencies confirmed.

corrections.claim: Owens thesis 2017 includes cycle-breaking for a unique sweep order.
corrections.correction: Abstract confirms 2D discontinuous isogeometric discrete-ordinates with hanging nodes and heuristic adaptive refinement (EngD, Imperial, 2017) and mentions sweep ordering, but not cycle breaking. Needs the thesis body to support.

corrections.claim: Serpent polyMesh uses zero-based indexing and requires outward owner-face normals; polyhedral cells fall out for free.
corrections.correction: Indexing/normal claims could not be checked (Serpent pages 403). What search summaries of Serpent's docs do state: tetrahedral, hexahedral and polyhedral inputs accepted but 'internally all unstructured meshes are handled as tetrahedral meshes'; cells must be closed and convex; each face must have exactly one owner and zero or one neighbour. So Serpent's polyhedra are convex-only and conformity is an explicit input rule, not merely assumed.

corrections.claim: Source 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.01591' (listed without description).
corrections.correction: It is Kim, Im, Lee, Jung (submitted 2 Jul 2026), 'Verification and Performance Assessment of NuDEAL, a GPU-Accelerated Deterministic Transport Framework on Unstructured Meshes': planar MOC + hybrid FEM, DG characteristics, and a DFEM-SN solver on unstructured meshes (C5G7, ABTR, Empire, MSRE). A relevant unstructured DFEM-SN consumer the report body never discusses.

corrections.claim: Griffin paper at osti.gov purl 2345902 not readable; Griffin details unverified.
corrections.correction: The OSTI record is Prince, Hanophy, Labouré, Wang, Harbour, Choi, 'Neutron transport methods for multiphysics heterogeneous reactor core simulation in Griffin', Annals of Nuclear Energy 200 (2024): DFEM-SN with a 'fully asynchronous parallel sweeper' and 'unstructured coarse-mesh finite difference acceleration'; INL VTB inputs use scheme=DFEM-SN, family=MONOMIAL, order=FIRST, meshes via MOOSE FileMeshGenerator/Exodus. Polyhedra and hanging-node handling remain unverified; libMesh having C0Polyhedron does not imply Griffin's sweeper supports it.

corrections.claim: MDPI J. Nucl. Eng. 2(3):22 limits the 3D high-order basis to extruded polygonal prisms and cites Hackemack JCP 2018.
corrections.correction: Could not be fetched (403 / expired certificate on www2.mdpi.com). Treat as unverified pending a readable copy.

missing_important: OpenSn (TAMU, open-source successor of Chi-Tech) is omitted and is the strongest candidate first consumer / direct comparison: PWLD DGFEM on 'arbitrary polyhedra in 3D and arbitrary polygons in 2D' with planar faces; each polyhedron is split internally into tets (vertex, vertex, face centroid, cell centroid) but DOF count = number of vertices; sweep cycles broken by lagging the faces with smallest |Omega.n|; FromFileMeshGenerator auto-detects .obj, .msh (Gmsh), .e (ExodusII), .vtu/.pvtu, .case (EnSight Gold) and OpenFOAM constant/polyMesh directories; partitioners ParMETIS/PTSCOTCH via PETSc, KBA, linear. Landing page claims compatibility with 'adaptively refined grids'; user guide is marked Draft. Lineage: Vermaak, Ragusa, Morel 2020 (arXiv 2004.01824) sweeps with cyclic dependencies at >100k processes. (open-sn.github.io/opensn/userguide/geometry_mesh.html, /theory/discretization.html)

MCNP6 unstructured mesh (Abaqus .inp or mcnpum) is a production MC code with defined tolerance semantics for non-conformal part interfaces, a fifth mechanism the report missed: 'all gaps in the unstructured mesh are treated as voids'; 'source particles may not be started in mesh gaps'; 'overlapping parts must not be severe; any single element may not be wholly contained within another element'; 'there is no correction while tracking through overlapping elements'; 'CSG surfaces must not clip or intersect the unstructured mesh'; 'surface tallies are not permitted'. Elements: 1st/2nd-order tetrahedra, pentahedra, hexahedra only ('Unstructured polyhedrons with 4-, 5-, and 6-sides'); 'only pentahedra and hexahedra may appear together in a part'. Materials via pseudo-cells mapped on the EMBED card; a background cell fills gaps. Source is a 2012 LANL course deck (LA-UR-12-00795), so check against the MCNP 6.3 manual.

CGNS is the best existing baseline IR for the 'similar to X, differing in Y' framing: HDF5-backed, well-specified SIDS, polyhedra (NGON_n/NFACE_n + ParentElements = owner/neighbour), first-class interface types (Abutting1to1 / mismatched Abutting / Overset), zones as partitions, boundary conditions, families. Its gaps are the differentiation slots: no stored intersection polygons or weights for mismatched polyhedral interfaces (InterpolantsDonor only for structured grids and basic linear elements), no imprint/merge status, no explicit mesh-to-B-rep association, high-order limited to fixed Lagrange element types.

OpenMC's libMesh path already tolerates adaptively refined (hanging-node) tally meshes via AdaptiveLibMesh, so the overlay mechanism needs no conformity at all; constraints that matter for the stated requirements: libMesh tallies require a ReplicatedMesh (no distributed mesh), unstructured surface tallies are not implemented (no face currents on UM), and connectivity export covers only linear tet/hex.

MOOSE mortar claims are verified, not just plausible: Oct-2021 newsletter 'MOOSE now supports mortar constraints on 3D geometries' (previously 2D only); Constraints docs: segment-based mortar integrals; verified on 3D hexahedral meshes; 'Triangular elements on the mortar interface typically exhibit the infamous ... locking phenomenon', tets need stabilization (delta=0.1), uniform tet refinement showed Lagrange-multiplier divergence; adaptive refinement with mortar 'should be approached with caution'. (raw.githubusercontent.com/idaholab/moose/master/framework/doc/content/syntax/Constraints/index.md; modules/doc/content/newsletter/2021/2021_10.md)

OpenFOAM's two lines diverge on non-conformal interfaces: openfoam.org v10+ uses Non-Conformal Coupling (nonConformalCyclic patch pairs) and is removing AMI; openfoam.com (ESI) still documents cyclicAMI. Either way the interface is encoded as a pair of boundary patches in the 'boundary' file with weights computed at run time, i.e. the data model stores the pairing, not the intersection. cellZones/faceZones/pointZones (the natural 'partition layer' over the same face-based mesh) remain unverified: neither mesh-description page fetched mentions them.

Exodus polyhedra caveats worth recording for an exporter: faces are referenced by file-implicit ids depending on face-block order; a file may hold several face blocks (quad faces in one, 5-gons in another) and element blocks may reference any of them; ParaView's reader got this wrong until 2016 and Sandia's Exodus lead acknowledged scarce documentation. libMesh C0Polyhedron ExodusII I/O only arrived in 2026, so downstream MOOSE apps may lag.

Serpent's convexity requirement means an exporter to Serpent must convex-decompose or tet-decompose non-convex polyhedra, and its 'exactly one owner, zero or one neighbour per face' rule is an explicit conformity validator you can mirror.

topic: Geometry-partition-mesh layer models in meshing tools (Cubit, Gmsh, Salome SMESH, ANSYS Meshing/Fluent, Simmetrix, Pointwise, PUMI/SCOREC classification)
summary: Every mature tool keeps the three layers coherent by one mechanism: each mesh entity carries a single back-pointer, its "classification" or "owner", to the lowest-dimensional model (B-rep) entity that contains it. The conceptual partition layer (materials, blocks, physical groups, named selections, sidesets) is then defined on model entities and, in most tools, evaluated into mesh entities on demand. Cubit, Gmsh, Salome, Simmetrix and PUMI all do this (checked against primary docs or source). Where the model is non-manifold, Cubit uses imprint then merge, Gmsh uses BooleanFragments/Coherence, and ANSYS uses shared topology, so that neighbouring volumes share the same interface face entities. The layers are linked by identity (dim,tag), not by geometric search. Shephard's formalism (PUMI) states this as M^d_i -> G^q_j with d<=q (seen in the FEP19 slides via search snippet only; I could not open the slides or the TOMS paper). The partition layer is the weakest-specified part in all of them. Cubit allows a volume in only one block, Gmsh physical groups are bare integer tags with names stored separately, and ANSYS Named Selections are fragile under shared-topology operations. Non-conformal interfaces (Fluent) are a runtime concept: two un-imprinted face zones are paired and intersected at solve time, with no persistent geometry link between them.
data_model:
CUBIT (owner geometry, blocks, merge). Hierarchy: Body, Volume, Surface, Curve, Vertex, with mesh entities "owned" by a geometry entity. Cubit's docs say "Any mesh entity owned by the geometric entity in a nodeset or sideset is automatically assigned to the same nodeset or sideset" and "if a surface belongs to a specific sideset, remeshing the surface will automatically delete any old faces from the sideset and add the faces of the new mesh". Blocks: "If a block is defined at a geometric entity, each of the elements owned by the geometry are automatically assigned to the block." Constraints from the 15.8 docs: a volume, surface or curve can be in only ONE block; each block has a single element type; ids are arbitrary integers; a block holds entities of one dimensionality only. Block membership may also be set per mesh entity (e.g. "Block 1 remove hex 1"), and then it is not tied to geometry. Nodesets and sidesets are many-to-many (a node or side may be in several sets). Sideset direction (Forward/Reverse/Both, "wrt Volume") uses the surface's forward and reverse volumes, so the non-manifold surface keeps two-sided volume adjacency. MERGE: the algorithm is "check lower-order geometry, merge if possible; check topology; check geometry; if both entities are meshed, check topology of meshes". Merge needs matching geometry and topology, and if both sides are meshed, topologically identical meshes; nodes of the lowest-ID entity win. Merged entities form a non-manifold model. Imprint (regular, tolerant, mesh-based) exists to make surfaces have like topology so that they can merge. Per-entity "Merge On/Off" flags exist. Internally Cubit/CGM uses RefEntity over TopologyBridge objects; one cgma-dev thread says a merged RefEntity can hold several TopologyBridges (partially verified from list posts only). 

GMSH. Elementary entities are Points/Curves/Surfaces/Volumes identified by (dim, tag>0), with tags unique per dimension. Mesh nodes and elements are "stored (classified) in the model entity they discretize": a curve holds its line elements plus interior nodes, boundary nodes sit in the bounding points, a surface holds its elements plus all nodes not classified on its boundary or embedded entities, and so on (gmsh.texi, "Gmsh application programming interface"). Physical groups are "simply stored as integer tags in the entities" (GEntity.h), with the names in $PhysicalNames. Default output keeps only elements in at least one physical group unless Mesh.SaveAll. MSH 4.2 (current revision per the manual's master source) layout: $MeshFormat; $PhysicalNames (dim, tag, "name" up to 127 chars); $Entities (points: tag X Y Z numPhysicalTags tags; curves/surfaces/volumes: tag, bbox min/max, numPhysicalTags + tags, numBounding* + signed tags where the sign encodes orientation, numEmbedded + (dim,tag) pairs); $PartitionedEntities (parentDim/parentTag, partition list); $Nodes in blocks (numEntityBlocks, numNodes, minTag, maxTag; per block entityDim, entityTag, parametric flag, numNodesInBlock, tags array, then xyz array, plus optional u,v,w); $Elements in blocks (entityDim, entityTag, elementType, count, then (elementTag, nodeTags...)); $Polytopes (types 34 polygon / 35 polyhedron: elementOffset array of n+1 values, per-face node lists, optional sub-triangulation or sub-tetrahedralization); $Edges / $Faces (global mesh edges and faces with tags); $Periodic (entity master/slave plus affine transform and corresponding node pairs); $GhostElements; $Parametrizations. Block layout allows single-fread bulk reads. Tags may be sparse but sparse tags force map instead of vector storage. Fragments/Coherence: BooleanFragments "making all interfaces conformal; lower-dimensional entities automatically embedded"; with OpenCASCADE, Coherence is BooleanFragments on all entities.

SALOME SMESH. A mesh is built on a main shape (GEOM). "Every mesh entity can be associated with the sub-shape it was generated on, if any", and nodes on edges and faces store parametric coordinates. Sub-meshes attach local algorithms/hypotheses to a sub-shape; the hypothesis search order is edge, groups, wires, faces, shells, solids, main shape (more local wins; the lower sub-shape ID breaks ties). Three group kinds: standalone (explicit list, goes empty if its entities are recomputed away), group on geometry (bound to a sub-shape or sub-shape group at creation, link not changeable, contents "always updated automatically"), and group on filter (a predicate). One group holds one element type (node, edge, face, volume, 0D, ball). Groups are exported to MED/UNV/CGNS; sub-meshes are not. Several meshes in a study do not form one super-mesh and are exported individually.

ANSYS. Meshing: Parts are made of bodies. A multibody part with "Shared Topology" merges common faces, "the shared faces belong to both of the neighboring bodies", giving a conformal interface; without it the duplicate faces are meshed separately and are non-conformal. Imprint mode only imprints. Named Selections are sets of geometric entities, and the same entity in two Named Selections raises an error (forum report, not official doc). A forum report says Named Selections can vanish after SpaceClaim share-topology (anecdotal). Fluent mesh: cell zones (volumes), face zones (boundary or interface), and the doc requires "each cell zone has a distinct face zone on the non-conformal boundary" (same position/shape, one per cell zone). Zone type is a mutable label (wall, interior, interface, ...). 

SIMMETRIX. MeshSim models are non-manifold; classification is a first-class API. PUMI's apfSIM.cc implements toModel(e) as EN_whatIn(entity) and the GeomSim adapter uses GEN_type/GEN_tag/GM_entityByTag (dimension-unique tag lookup). Analysis/meshing attributes attach to model entities and groups, organised into "cases" (SimModeler marketing text; API-level details of Simmetrix not verified, since its docs are behind login). 

POINTWISE (Glyph). A hierarchy: database entities (CAD) -> connectors (1D grid) -> domains (2D) -> blocks (3D). A block is "bounded by one or more pw::Faces". A "register" ties a domain into a block with an orientation (Same/Opposite). Grid entities project onto database entities; a Glyph action returns the database entities a grid entity uses. Key-value attributes attach to entities (Glyph docs; pages 403 when fetched, so results are search-snippet level). 

PUMI/SCOREC (Shephard). Mesh = topological hierarchy of vertex/edge/face/region with one-level or full adjacency. MDS stores types: vertex, edge, triangle, quad, wedge, pyramid, tet, hex (8 types; no polyhedron), in per-type arrays with down[4][types] and up[4][types] adjacency arrays. Classification is a per-entity pointer array: struct mds_apf { ... struct gmi_ent** model[MDS_TYPES]; double (*point)[3]; double (*param)[2]; void** parts[MDS_TYPES]; struct mds_net remotes, ghosts, matches; }. The API is toModel(MeshEntity*), getModelType (dimension), getModelTag (unique within dimension), and findModelEntity(type,tag). GMI is a small C interface to any B-rep: gmi_dim, gmi_tag, gmi_find, gmi_adjacent (usually one level), gmi_eval, gmi_closest_point. Backends: analytic, Parasolid/ACIS via Simmetrix GeomSim, .smd, Capstone, Gmsh-derived models, and a pure-topology discrete model (.dmg) that drops geometry but keeps classification. mktopomodel/deriveMdsModel can create such a model from a bare mesh by classifying interior entities on a model region and boundary entities on a boundary model entity from upward adjacencies. The rule d<=q (mesh entity of dimension d classified on model entity of dimension q) is from the FEP19 slides (search snippet).
polyhedra: Mixed. Gmsh MSH 4.2 has first-class polyhedra in $Polytopes, as polygon/polyhedron types 34/35 with a face-node list and optional sub-tetrahedralization (hanging/interior nodes). Polytopes share the element tag space and are classified on entities like any element, so the format already supports them at the file level. Whether Gmsh's mesher generates them is unverified. PUMI MDS supports only vertex, edge, triangle, quad, wedge, pyramid, tet and hex, so no polyhedra in the mesh database itself. Cubit blocks are Exodus element types (HEX8/20, TETRA4/10, PYRAMID5, WEDGE6, ...), so no polyhedra in the Cubit block model (Exodus has NFACED/NSIDED, but I did not verify that Cubit emits them). Salome volumes include polyhedra in MED, but I did not verify this in this pass. Fluent is natively polyhedral at solve time, but I did not read the zone-type docs on that.
nonconformal: Three different strategies appear. (1) Avoid by making the geometry conformal (Cubit imprint+merge; Gmsh BooleanFragments/Coherence; ANSYS shared topology). This is physical conformality, i.e. identical model face entities on both sides. The user's term "imprinting" is the topological step that enables this. (2) Keep both sides as separate face entities and pair them later. Fluent requires one distinct face zone per cell zone on the non-conformal boundary and sets zone type "interface". The user defines a Mesh Interface pairing zones (one-to-one or many-to-many), and Fluent "computes the intersection of the two interface zones" at setup/runtime; fluxes use the faces produced by the intersection. Overlap yields interior zone or coupled wall, and non-overlapping portions become new boundary zones; options: periodic, periodic repeats, matching, mapped, static, coupled wall. Detection is therefore not automatic: the user declares the pairing (auto-pairing is available by name/proximity). The pair is not persisted as geometric adjacency in the mesh. (3) Periodic/matched entities. Gmsh $Periodic (entity slave/master + affine transform + node correspondences) and PUMI getMatches (periodic copies) store explicit point-to-point correspondences. ANSYS also has a "Match Mesh Where Possible" patch-independent option (being deprecated). Cubit also has tolerant imprint and mesh-based imprint (uses coincident mesh entities with virtual geometry). Not covered: dedicated DG/hanging-node representation. PUMI declares getDgCopies, but the MDS implementation asserts "not implemented yet", so I found no worked non-conformal DG representation there.
sets_and_partitions: Conceptual partitions are named or numbered sets over geometry entities, and mesh membership is derived through classification. Cubit: blocks (element sets, 1 element type, a geometry entity belongs to at most one block), nodesets, sidesets (many-to-many; face/side sets oriented against forward/reverse volume); sets can be geometry-bound (auto-updating on remesh) or mesh-bound (lost on remesh); a "material" is just a block attribute. Gmsh: physical groups = (dim, tag, optional name), an element only gets exported if it has a physical group, and an entity may belong to several groups (list of physicalTags in $Entities). Salome: standalone / on-geometry / on-filter groups; one element type per group. ANSYS: Named Selections (entity sets), Parts/bodies, zones in Fluent (cell zone = volume partition, face zone = boundary, with a mutable type). Simmetrix: attributes and cases keyed by (model-entity dim, tag), groupable. Pointwise: BC and volume condition names on domains/blocks. PUMI itself does not define materials; they are model-entity attributes or mesh tags (createIntTag/createDoubleTag by name with array size and type INT/DOUBLE/LONG). Observation relevant to the user's 3-layer model: only classification is a true cross-layer link; partitions are sets over layer-1 entities. Multi-membership and typed-set semantics differ in every tool, which is why exporters are lossy.
strengths: Classification (one dim/tag back-pointer per mesh entity) is simple, cheap, and makes remeshing, adaptation, BC assignment and geometry snapping automatic (Cubit and Salome docs: membership 'updates automatically' on remesh; PUMI uses it for snapping/adaptation).
Defining partitions on geometry (Cubit blocks/sidesets, Gmsh physical groups, Salome group-on-geometry) keeps the partition valid across remeshes without touching the mesh.

Gmsh MSH 4.2 shows a concrete, versioned, block-structured format that stores B-rep topology (signed bounding entities, embedded entities), per-entity mesh blocks, physical groups, periodicity, partitions, ghost data, and polytopes in one file, with bulk-readable arrays.
PUMI's gmi interface proves the model layer can be abstracted: a tiny interface (dim, tag, find, adjacent, eval, closest point) plus a topology-only model (.dmg) works without any CAD kernel.

Imprint then merge (Cubit) / Fragments (Gmsh) / shared topology (ANSYS) all converge on the same idea: make interfaces a single shared model face with two adjacent volumes, which then yields conformal meshes automatically.
Fluent's zone/interface design shows non-conformal coupling can be declared at setup time without geometric modification.
weaknesses: The partition layer is an afterthought in several tools: Cubit's one-block-per-volume rule; Gmsh physical groups are integer tags with names stored separately and ungrouped elements are silently dropped unless SaveAll; ANSYS Named Selections can break under shared-topology operations (anecdotal) and one entity in two selections errors; Salome sub-meshes are not exported.
Mesh-bound sets (Cubit, Salome standalone groups) are lost or emptied on remesh, so two kinds of set coexist with different lifetimes.

Classification alone has no notion of the interface between two parts of the partition (e.g. material A|B face) unless the model has it; in Fluent the interface is an unlinked pair of face zones with no persistent adjacency, and it is rebuilt by intersection at setup.

Merge in Cubit is restrictive: meshes on both sides must be topologically identical (nodes of the lower ID win), and imprint and merge are separate steps that can create sliver entities (sliver cleanup tolerance).

Format exchange loses information: Exodus only carries blocks, node/side sets; Gmsh drops elements outside physical groups; Salome sub-meshes and hypotheses are not exported; none of these export 'why' (the geometry association) except Gmsh .msh.
PUMI MDS is limited to 8 element types, with no polyhedra and an unimplemented DG-copies path.
Specifications are mixed: Gmsh is a real versioned spec, but Cubit/Exodus semantics live in manuals and Simmetrix/Pointwise API docs are gated or return 403.
lessons_for_us: ADOPT classification as the core cross-layer key: every mesh entity (node, edge, face, cell) stores (dim, tag) of its lowest-dimensional containing model entity, with the rule model_dim >= mesh_dim. Store it as a struct-of-arrays column (u32 per entity), exactly like PUMI's model[type] arrays and Gmsh's per-entity blocks.

ADOPT the 'imprint = information-level merge' reading the user described: in our IR a conformal interface should be one shared B-rep face with two adjacent volumes (Cubit/Gmsh/ANSYS do this), and imprinting is the operation that creates it. Keep it purely topological/informational as a first step; do not require the mesh to be conformal.

DIFFER from Cubit: allow a model entity to belong to multiple partitions of different kinds, and make the partition layer a first-class typed entity (Material, Region, BoundarySet, BlockForOutput), not an integer id plus a few commands. Cubit's one-block-per-volume and Gmsh's untyped integers are the pain points to beat.

DIFFER from Gmsh: separate the layers explicitly. Layer 1 = B-rep (vertices, edges, faces, volumes with signed bounding lists like $Entities). Layer 2 = partitions as named sets over layer-1 entities (a DAG or tree is allowed). Layer 3 = mesh with classification column. Do not silently drop unclassified elements.

ADOPT PUMI's gmi idea: define the geometry layer by a narrow trait (dim, tag, find, adjacent, optional eval/closest_point) so that our own B-rep kernel, imported STEP/OCC, or a topology-only model (like .dmg) are interchangeable, and a bare mesh can derive a topology-only model (deriveMdsModel).

ADOPT geometry-bound set semantics and make them the default: set membership is computed from classification on demand (Cubit/Salome behaviour), mesh-bound sets are an explicit second kind, and the IR records which is which so remeshing can preserve intent.

Make non-conformal interfaces first-class in the IR: a Pairing object (faceset A, faceset B, tolerance, transform for periodic, kind: conformal | nonconformal | periodic | mapped) that references layer-1 faces or layer-3 face sets, rather than relying on the solver's setup stage like Fluent. This is a real differentiator; I found no tool that persists it as geometry-linked data (Gmsh $Periodic is the closest).

Detection of non-conformality should be derivable: two layer-1 faces that are geometrically coincident but not shared (not imprinted) are the candidates; a verification pass reports them, rather than the user hand-declaring zone types as in Fluent.
ADOPT block-oriented, offset-array storage (Gmsh $Nodes/$Elements blocks per entity, $Polytopes elementOffset array of n+1 values) for I/O and for polyhedra; this is directly mmap/Arrow-friendly.
ADOPT explicit ids (dim,tag) that are stable and dimension-unique across all three layers, so graph/DAG nodes can refer to them without pointers.

Treat exporters (Exodus, MED, CGNS, MSH, Fluent .msh, a solver input format) as lossy projections of the IR and record, per exporter, which layers/features are dropped; the table above is a starting inventory of what each target can carry (e.g. Exodus: blocks and sets only).
sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/live-clones/gmsh/master/doc/texinfo/gmsh.texi (MSH file format section, 'Gmsh application programming interface' data model, BooleanFragments, Coherence)

https://scorec.rpi.edu/~shephard/FEP19/notes-2019/Parallel%20Mesh%20Infrastructure/PUMI.pdf and https://scorec.rpi.edu/~shephard/FEP19/papers/TOMS-PUMI.pdf (found by search; could not be opened, d<=q rule is search-snippet only)
https://lagrit.lanl.gov/mstkla/GeomEntity.html (MSTK classification rules, search snippet only; fetch failed)

https://www.cadence.com/doc/glyph2/files/Glyph/cxx/GlyphGridEntity-cxx.html and https://pointwise.com/doc/user-manual/getting-started/data-hierarchy.html (Pointwise; fetch returned 403, claims are from search snippets only)

corrections.claim: Cubit: 'a volume, surface or curve can be in only ONE block' and 'Cubit allows a volume in only one block' (pain point to beat); Cubit/Gmsh both drop or lose unblocked mesh.
corrections.correction: The geometry-level rule stands as documented in both 15.8 and current Coreform docs ('A volume, surface, or curve can only be in one element block'). But there is a documented per-element escape hatch: 'Set Duplicate Block Elements {on|OFF}' lets a mesh element belong to several blocks (Exodus export assigns an extra GID per additional block; Cubit tracks only the first). Separately, Cubit does NOT drop unblocked mesh: 'Set Default Block ON' (the default) exports automatic blocks keyed by owning geometry (block ID = geometry ID); only 'Set Default Block OFF' drops unblocked mesh. Gmsh is the only tool in the report that silently drops.

corrections.claim: MSH 4.2 is the current revision of the Gmsh format, with $Polytopes (types 34/35), $Edges and $Faces sections.
corrections.correction: MSH 4.2 and the $Polytopes/$Edges/$Faces sections exist only in Gmsh master, i.e. 5.0.0 'Work-in-progress'. The latest release, 4.15.2 (24 Mar 2026), writes MSH 4.1, which has no $Polytopes (dev builds wrote a differently shaped $Faces into 4.1 files). The 5.0 polytope implementation 'replaces the old polygon/polyhedron elements, levelset commands and Plugin(CutMesh)'; polyhedra come in through the API (mesh/addPolyhedra, setPolytopeSimplices) or cut-mesh. No polyhedral generation algorithm appears in the 5.0 changelog (Algorithm3D=11 is the parallel Delaunay). Treat 4.2 as an unreleased spec that may still change.

corrections.claim: Exodus only carries blocks, node/side sets ('Exodus: blocks and sets only').
corrections.correction: Current Exodus (SEACAS exodusII.h) also has edge blocks, face blocks, edge/face/element sets, ASSEMBLIES (ex_assembly whose members are of type EX_ELEM_BLOCK or EX_ASSEMBLY, i.e. a hierarchy/DAG of blocks), blobs, and named attributes on entities. Assemblies are a partition-layer construct that already exists in the main target format. Polyhedra: element type 'nfaced' whose connectivity lists faces defined in one or more face blocks ('nsided' or regular); requires ex_put_init_ext; face IDs are file-implicit by block order.

corrections.claim: Cubit blocks are Exodus element types, so no polyhedra in the Cubit block model; 'I did not verify that Cubit emits them'.
corrections.correction: Confirmed; drop the hedge. Cubit's supported volume element types (15.8 and current Coreform docs) are only HEX8/9/20/27, TETRA4/8/10/14/15, PYRAMID5/13/18, WEDGE6/12/15/16/20/21. No NFACED/NSIDED: Cubit neither generates nor exports polyhedral cells.

corrections.claim: Salome volumes include polyhedra in MED, but I did not verify this in this pass.
corrections.correction: Confirmed; drop the hedge. SMESH volume types are tetrahedron, hexahedron, pentahedron, pyramid, hexagonal prism or polyhedron, and polyhedra are generated by released algorithms: 'Polyhedron per Solid' (one polyhedron per geometric solid), 'Body Fitting' (polyhedra where Cartesian cells cut the boundary) and 'Create Dual Mesh' (polyhedral dual of a tet mesh via MEDCoupling computeDualMesh). Salome, not Gmsh, is the open tool with released first-class polyhedral generation plus geometry classification.

corrections.claim: A Pairing object for non-conformal interfaces 'is a real differentiator; I found no tool that persists it as geometry-linked data (Gmsh $Periodic is the closest)'.
corrections.correction: Mesh-level persistence of non-conformal pairings is standard: CGNS SIDS stores multizone interface connectivity in-file with GridConnectivityType_t = Overset | Abutting (mismatched) | Abutting1to1 in GridConnectivity_t / GridConnectivity1to1_t, including donor-cell data for unstructured mismatched abutting interfaces; MFEM's 'NC mesh v1.0' format persists non-conforming (hanging-node) meshes. CAD linkage in CGNS is only Family_t -> GeometryReference_t (GeometryFormat, GeometryFile), not attached to the interface itself. So the narrow 'geometry-linked' statement survives, but the 'real differentiator' is only the B-rep-face-level link, not persistence of the pairing per se; the lesson should be rewritten against CGNS Abutting as the baseline.

corrections.claim: Salome hypothesis search order is edge, groups, wires, faces, shells, solids, main shape.
corrections.correction: Documented order: the edge itself, groups of edges, wires, faces, groups of faces, shells, solids, groups of solids, main shape. Multi-dimensional algorithms beat uni-dimensional ones at equal priority; ties go to the lower sub-shape ID and the user can reorder concurrent sub-meshes.

corrections.claim: Gmsh default output keeps only elements in at least one physical group unless Mesh.SaveAll; 'Gmsh drops elements outside physical groups'.
corrections.correction: Only 'if physical groups are defined'; with no physical groups all elements are saved. Also, in some legacy formats (e.g. MSH2) Mesh.SaveAll discards the physical group definitions.

corrections.claim: Shephard classification rule d<=q seen only in a search snippet; TOMS/FEP19 PDFs could not be opened.
corrections.correction: The rule is correct; the citable primary source is M.W. Beall & M.S. Shephard, 'A general topology-based mesh data structure', IJNME 40(9):1573-1596 (1997), which defines classification of M^d_i on G^q_j with d<=q (reviewer knowledge; the scorec.rpi.edu PDFs also returned HTML here). Supporting primary text: apfMesh.h documents toModel() as 'get geometric classification', and the SCOREC wiki states deriveMdsModel 'will classify all interior entities onto a model region and all boundary entities onto a boundary model entity, as defined by mesh upward adjacencies'.

corrections.claim: Fluent is natively polyhedral at solve time but I did not read the zone-type docs on that.
corrections.correction: Fluent non-conformal interfaces do work with polyhedral meshes; the documented exceptions are that the one-to-one interface creation method (for splitting large boundary zones) 'is not available for polyhedral meshes', and S2S face-to-face view factors are incompatible with mapped interfaces on polyhedral meshes. The doc also confirms 'each cell zone has a distinct face zone on the non-conformal boundary' and that fluxes use faces from the computed intersection.

missing_important: MOAB (Mesh-Oriented datABase, ANL SIGMA) is the existing 'mesh as a database' design and is absent from the report. Entities (finite-element zoo plus polygons and polyhedra) are addressed by EntityHandle; entity sets carry parent/child relations and arbitrary tags; B-rep topology is stored as sets tagged GEOM_DIMENSION ('entities owned by a given topological entity in a geometric model') / GLOBAL_ID / CATEGORY with parent-child links volume->surface->curve->vertex, and surface sense wrt forward/reverse volumes (GeomTopoTool::set_surface_senses, sense2 tag); MATERIAL_SET / DIRICHLET_SET / NEUMANN_SET tags map to Exodus blocks / nodesets / sidesets; file format is HDF5 .h5m. It is the geometry+mesh database behind DAGMC (CAD-based Monte Carlo transport; documented workflow = Cubit imprint + merge + groups -> .h5m) and one of OpenMC's two unstructured-mesh backends (class MOABMesh; the other is libMesh). For a neutron-transport-first IR this is the primary baseline to position against. Sources: https://bitbucket.org/fathomteam/moab (repo description; src/MBTagConventions.hpp; src/moab/GeomTopoTool.hpp) ; https://svalinn.github.io/DAGMC/usersguide/cubit_basics.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmc-dev/openmc/develop/include/openmc/mesh.h

CGNS SIDS is the 'modern, well-specified' candidate the report skips: polyhedra via NGON_n (all faces) + NFACE_n (cells as lists of those faces, 'each face must be shared by another polyhedral element except boundary faces') with a mandatory ElementStartOffset offset array (same offset idea as Gmsh $Polytopes), MIXED sections, high-order element types, Family_t with FamilyBC and CAD GeometryReference_t, ZoneGridConnectivity with Overset / Abutting / Abutting1to1, HDF5 backing. Gmsh and Salome both export CGNS. Sources: https://cgns.github.io/standard/SIDS/grid.html (7.4.2 NGON_n/NFACE_n) ; .../multizone.html ; .../misc.html

Exodus assemblies (hierarchical groupings of element blocks or other assemblies), edge/face/element sets and entity attributes exist today, so the 'partition layer as a DAG of named sets' lesson already has a target in Exodus; the lossy-exporter inventory should be updated. Source: exodusII.h (EX_ASSEMBLY, ex_put_assemblies).

Codes that solve on non-conformal meshes (the user asked): Fluent (interface zones + runtime intersection; verified), any CGNS-consuming solver via Abutting connectivity (spec verified), MFEM (NC mesh v1.0 hanging nodes; verified), OpenFOAM (face-based polyhedral polyMesh with owner/neighbour verified; cyclicAMI 'Arbitrary Mesh Interface' coupled patches from reviewer knowledge, fetch blocked), deal.II / libMesh / MOOSE (hanging-node constraints and mortar; reviewer knowledge), code_saturne ('joining' of non-conforming meshes into a conforming polyhedral mesh; reviewer knowledge). In every case the two sides are separate face sets/patches plus a declared pairing; detection is pairing + geometric intersection, not B-rep identity.

Cubit's default-block behaviour is the opposite of Gmsh's: unblocked mesh is exported in automatic blocks keyed by owning geometry ID unless 'Set Default Block OFF'. This changes the 'do not silently drop unclassified elements' lesson: Gmsh is the only tool that drops, and only when physical groups exist.

Gmsh 5.0 (unreleased) adds MSH 4.2, API-level polytopes (addPolyhedra / getPolyhedra / setPolytopeSimplices), Mesh.CreateEdges / CreateFaces, partition overlaps and 'save only the local partitioned Brep'. Since smart-mesh will target Gmsh as an exporter, the 4.1 (released) vs 4.2 (dev) split must be tracked; do not design against 4.2 as if stable.

Verified-as-stated (no correction needed): Cubit merge requires topologically identical meshes and uses node positions of the lowest-ID entity; Cubit sideset Forward/Reverse/Both wrt volume; Salome's three group kinds and 'association cannot be changed / always updated automatically'; PUMI MDS has exactly 8 types (mds.h) and getDgCopies asserts 'not implemented yet' (apfMDS.cc); Simmetrix classification via EN_whatIn (apfSIM.cc); Gmsh physicals are std::vector<int> in GEntity.h; $Entities bounding tags 'sign encodes orientation'.

Web search budget was exhausted mid-task; all checks came from direct fetches of primary sources (manuals, headers, specs). Not re-verified here: Pointwise/Glyph and Simmetrix API claims (gated), the ANSYS Meshing shared-topology page, the cgma-dev TopologyBridge thread, and the ANSYS forum anecdotes.

topic: SCOREC PUMI / Simmetrix: mesh-model classification, MDS topology database, attribute systems, classification-preserving adaptation
summary: PUMI (Parallel Unstructured Mesh Infrastructure, SCOREC/RPI; Ibanez, Seol, Smith, Shephard, ACM TOMS 42(3), Art. 17, 2016, doi 10.1145/2814935) is a C/C++ library suite (APF, MDS, GMI, PCU, PARMA, MA, CRV, ...) whose core idea is a mesh as a topological hierarchy (vertex/edge/face/region) where every mesh entity is CLASSIFIED against an entity of a geometric model (CAD or discrete). The mesh database (MDS) is an array-based, type-indexed, adjacency-storing structure. Boundary conditions, materials and sizing are attached as attributes to model entities (in Simmetrix's SimModSuite/SimModeler, held in the .smd model file with meshing/analysis "cases"), never to the mesh, so they survive remeshing; PUMI itself deliberately keeps the attribute system outside GMI and uses integer tags/fields on the mesh. Adaptation (MA) is local cavity modification (split/collapse/swap/snap/shape-fix) that maintains classification by construction. It is the closest published baseline for our "geometry layer + mesh layer linked by classification" idea, but it is conforming-only, element set is fixed to 8 types (no polyhedra), and the partition/material layer is not first-class. Maturity: active, BSD-licensed, used in production (e.g. PHASTA, M3D-C1, Albany, PUMIPic/Tally for Monte Carlo transport). Note: I could not fetch the TOMS/FMDB PDFs (SCOREC hosts returned 404 for them), so paper-level claims are marked unverified; struct/API claims come from source code on GitHub.
data_model: VERIFIED from source (github.com/SCOREC/core, mds/mds.c, mds.h, mds_apf.h, mds_net.h): Entity types enum MDS_VERTEX, EDGE, TRIANGLE, QUADRILATERAL, WEDGE, PYRAMID, TETRAHEDRON, HEXAHEDRON (MDS_TYPES=8). Static tables mds_dim, mds_degree[type][4] (e.g. tet {4,6,4,1}, hex {8,12,6,1}) and mds_types[type][dim] give template topology (e.g. T01 edge->vertex pairs, T12 face->edge). An entity id is a single integer mds_id (MDS_ID_TYPE, int by default, recompile with -DMDS_ID_TYPE=long for >2^31) encoding type and index by interleaving: ID(t,i)=i*MDS_TYPES+t, TYPE=id%MDS_TYPES, INDEX=id/MDS_TYPES. struct mds holds per-type counters n[], cap[], end[], and adjacency arrays down[4][MDS_TYPES], up[4][MDS_TYPES], first_up[4][MDS_TYPES] (dimension x type), free-list free[]/first_free[] for entity deletion/hole reuse. Adjacency is a 'one-level' style: downward adjacencies stored as flat id arrays per type (fixed degree from mds_degree), upward stored as lists, other adjacencies derived on demand (mds_get_adjacent fills struct mds_set {n; e[MDS_SET_MAX]}); apf::Mesh has createAdjacency/hasAdjacency(from_dim,to_dim) to opt in to storing extra adjacencies. The wrapper struct mds_apf adds: tags (struct mds_tags), double (*point)[3] coordinates (per vertex), double (*param)[2] parametric coords on the model entity, struct gmi_ent** model[MDS_TYPES] = the CLASSIFICATION (one model-entity pointer per mesh entity, per type array), void** parts[MDS_TYPES], and three struct mds_net (remotes, ghosts, matches) each = per-type arrays of struct mds_copies {n; {mds_id e; int p;} c[]}. Geometric model side (gmi/gmi.h): struct gmi_model {ops*; int n[4]} with a C vtable gmi_model_ops (begin/next/end, dim, tag, find, adjacent, is_discrete_ent, eval, reparam, periodic, range, closest_point, normal, first_derivative, is_point_in_region, bbox, is_in_closure_of, destroy); gmi_ent opaque; entities identified by (dim, tag). Backends: gmi_mesh (.dmg files via gmi_write_dmg), gmi_analytic, gmi_sim (wraps Simmetrix: GM_vertexIter/GM_edgeIter/GM_faceIter/GM_regionIter, GEN_type, GEN_tag, GM_entityByTag, GV_/GE_/GF_/GR_ topology queries, GF_closestPoint, GR_containsPoint, GR_inClosure; Parasolid/ACIS/Discrete kernels), gmi_cap. API surface (apf/apfMesh.h): toModel(e), getModel(), setModel(), getModelType/Tag, getType, getDimension, getAdjacent/getDownward/getUp/countUpward, getResidence/getRemotes/getGhosts/isShared/isOwned/getOwner/isGhost, hasMatching/getMatches, getDgCopies, tags createInt/Double/LongTag + get/set/has/removeTag, Numbering/GlobalNumbering, Fields (nodal, element, integration-point). Native file: SMB (SMB_VERSION=6), per-part binary files; mds_smb.c writes classification as pairs (model id, model dim) per entity (class[2*j]=id, class[2*j+1]=dim), plus header magic/version, coordinates, tags, remote links. mds_derive_model() shows the minimum classification semantics: classify everything to interior (dim d, id 0); a facet with <2 adjacent regions and no remote copy puts its closure on boundary (dim d-1, id 0).
polyhedra: Not supported by MDS: the type enum is fixed at 8 (vertex, edge, tri, quad, wedge, pyramid, tet, hex) with compile-time template adjacency tables (verified in mds.c). Fixed per-type degree arrays make general polygons/polyhedra impossible without a new type mechanism. Higher-order geometry is handled by CRV (Bezier-curved meshes) rather than by arbitrary cells. Lesson: template-table elements give very compact, fast adjacency but are the opposite of what we need (polyhedral first-class).
nonconformal: MDS is fundamentally conforming: adjacency is by shared sub-entity (a face is shared by exactly two regions; mds_derive_model treats a face with fewer than 2 regions and no remote copy as boundary), so there is no representation of hanging nodes or mismatched interface faces and no 'imprint' relation. Related but different features, verified in apfMesh.h: (a) 'matching' (hasMatching/getMatches/Matches) for periodic boundaries, i.e. entities linked as copies of each other across model boundaries, stored in mds_apf.matches; (b) getDgCopies(e, dgCopies, ModelEntity*) for discontinuous-Galerkin style duplicated entities on a model entity; (c) part-boundary 'remotes'. MA has adaptMatching() for matched meshes. No mortar/projection support for non-conformal meshes. Non-conformal detection is therefore outside the model: because classification is to a CAD model, two bodies touching would have distinct (or shared, if the CAD was imprinted) model faces; PUMI assumes the geometry was already made conformal. (Unverified: Simmetrix MeshSim may offer non-matching-interface features in commercial modules; not checked.)
sets_and_partitions: Classification IS the grouping mechanism: a mesh entity belongs to the set of entities classified on a model entity (e.g. all tets classified on model region 3, all faces on model face 7), so material/BC sets are derived by querying classification, not stored as sets on the mesh. Layers (as the user describes them): geometry = gmi_model (B-rep, topology + evaluation); mesh = mds_apf; link = the model[] classification array with parametric coords for boundary entities. Partition/'material' layer: not a separate layer in PUMI; materials/BCs are attributes on model entities. In Simmetrix SimModeler, model entities can be 'grouped' so an attribute applies to all group members (verified from vendor material), and attributes are organised into named cases ('Mesh case 1' for meshing attributes, analysis/solver cases for BCs/materials, e.g. Abaqus/ANSYS CFX/FUN3D attribute definitions); the .smd file holds model plus applied attributes (verified from SimModeler 6.0 tutorial at m3dc1.pppl.gov/Weekly/SimModeler.pdf). Attribute application inheritance (an attribute on a face applying to its bounding edges/vertices, mesh entities inherit from classified model entity) is the standard SCOREC/Trellis design (unverified here: the attributes.pdf/Trellis page returned 404). PUMI itself deliberately does not carry an attribute system in GMI (gmi_ent is opaque, no attribute API); users attach data via mesh tags and fields keyed on the classification (getModelType/getModelTag). Mesh tags are named typed per-entity arrays (int/long/double). Parallel: each part holds a mesh; residence set (set of parts an entity lives on), remote copies (mds_copy {e,p}), owner part, optional ghost copies; parts partitioned by Zoltan/PARMA (hypergraph-based PUMI-Balance).
strengths: Classification as a first-class, mandatory link: every mesh entity points to a (dim,tag) model entity, plus parametric coords; this decouples BC/material/size attributes from any particular mesh and survives remeshing/adaptation (verified in mds_apf.h, mds_smb.c).

Clean abstraction boundary: GMI is a small C vtable for geometry (eval, closest_point, normal, reparam, periodic, bbox, is_in_closure_of) with swappable kernels (Parasolid, ACIS, discrete, analytic, Cap); mesh code never touches CAD directly.
Compact array-based storage with O(1) adjacency and entity deletion/free-list reuse, designed for evolving meshes (adaptation), not just static I/O.
Single-integer ids encoding type+index; per-type arrays give cache-friendly iteration.
Parallel model is part of the data structure (residence/owner/remotes/ghosts), with mds_verify and mds_verify_residence invariants checking consistency.

Adaptation preserves classification by construction (local modifications on cavities; new entities created via mds_apf_create_entity(type, model, from) which requires the model entity); MA offers shouldSnap, shouldTransferParametric, shouldTransferToClosestPoint, shouldFixShape, solution transfer (maInput.h).
Proven at scale (billions of elements per the PUMI literature; unverified exact figures) and BSD licensed with a rich ecosystem (PHASTA, M3D-C1, PUMIPic, PUMI-Tally for MC neutral transport).
weaknesses: Fixed 8 element types with hard-coded template tables: no polyhedra/polygons, no arbitrary mixed cells.
Conforming-only topology; no first-class non-conformal interface, mortar, or imprint concept (matching = periodic copies only).

Classification is a single pointer per entity: no multi-layer model (geometry vs partition/material vs mesh) and no explicit many-to-one 'material' layer; no way to express an entity lying on two coexisting layered models.

Attributes are not part of the open GMI/PUMI interface; the rich attribute system (cases, groups, solver attribute definitions) lives in proprietary Simmetrix tooling (SimModSuite), so the open stack lacks it.

C/C++ with raw pointers and abort-on-error (gmi_fail), MPI-centric; no versioned, language-neutral on-disk spec: SMB is a per-part binary format versioned (6) but defined by the code, and .dmg is a simple text model.
Geometry kernel high-quality only with commercial Simmetrix/Parasolid; open backends are limited (discrete, analytic, mesh-model).
lessons_for_us: ADOPT classification as the backbone linking layers: every mesh entity carries a (model_dim, model_id) reference to a model entity, plus parametric coords for boundary entities; store as parallel columns (struct-of-arrays) in the mesh tables. BCs/materials/sizing attach to model entities, never to mesh entities; mesh sets are derived views via classification.

DIFFER: make classification multi-layer. Keep geometry (B-rep), partition (material/region grouping = a separate abstract layer with its own entity set: 'partition region' that groups volumes and 'interface' entities between them), and mesh layer; classification links mesh -> partition entity -> geometry entity, so the partition layer is explicit rather than pushed into attributes on geometry.

ADOPT a small vtable-style geometry interface (GMI-like: eval, closest_point, normal, reparam, periodic, is_in_closure_of, bbox) so the mesher/adapter depends on a trait, not on our kernel, enabling STEP/other-kernel import or discrete geometry; in Rust this is a trait with capability queries (gmi_can_eval etc.).

DIFFER on element model: replace fixed type tables with a general cell-face-edge-vertex incidence (polyhedral first-class, like OpenFOAM/CGNS NGON/NFACE) and treat tet/hex/etc. as 'shape tags' with optional fast paths, instead of compile-time templates.

ADOPT array-based, type/dim-indexed storage with a free list and O(1) downward adjacency; compute upward/derived adjacency on demand but let consumers opt in to stored adjacencies (createAdjacency(from,to)). This fits the 'mesh as geometric database' view: tables + indexes materialised on demand.

ADOPT the invariants-checker idea: a mds_verify-like validator (classification closure rule: a mesh entity's model entity must be in the closure of its coboundary's classification; faces with <2 cells must be on model boundary; residence consistency) shipped as part of the IR spec and run on import/export.

DIFFER on non-conformity: model interfaces as explicit first-class 'interface' relations (face-to-face imprint relation with a pair of classified model faces and a mapping/projection record), rather than hoping geometry was already imprinted; conformal case is the special case with identity mapping. PUMI's 'matches' and 'dgCopies' suggest storing copies as (entity,part) pairs; generalise to (entity, entity, transform/map).
ADOPT explicit remote/owner/residence in the parallel representation (mds_copy {e,p}); store per-type CSR-style arrays on disk for fast I/O instead of a per-part opaque binary.

ADOPT the save-with-classification file idea (SMB stores (id,dim) pair per entity; versioned header/magic): our IR file should be a versioned, language-neutral, chunked columnar container (e.g. Arrow/HDF5/Zarr-like) holding geometry ref + partition table + mesh tables + classification column, with a published schema, unlike PUMI's code-defined SMB.

ADOPT adaptation that takes classification as input to every local operator (create_entity requires a model entity), so remeshing/refinement never loses the geometry/material link; expose snap-to-model with parametric transfer as a first-class step.

DIFFER on attributes: build an open, versioned attribute system with named cases (meshing, solver/physics), groups of model entities, and inheritance down the model hierarchy (face -> edges -> vertices), i.e. what Simmetrix keeps proprietary; this becomes the natural export hook for transport-code inputs (materials, boundary conditions, sources).
spec_quality: No formal versioned specification for the in-memory/database model. The authoritative definition is the C/C++ source plus the TOMS paper (not retrievable here; contents unverified). SMB has an embedded version number (SMB_VERSION=6, read_header asserts version <= 6) and a magic word, but is defined only by reader/writer code; the .dmg model text format is simple and documented in code. GMI is a documented C header with explicit 'implementations may omit pointers' semantics. Simmetrix SimModSuite/.smd formats are proprietary with vendor API docs behind a licence.
