Overall: good code-level API, weak external spec.
storage: In memory: flat malloc'd arrays per entity type and dimension (realloc growth with cap/end/n counters, free list for holes). On disk: SMB, one binary file per part (header magic, version, dimension, number of peers; then per-type entity counts, vertex coordinates and parametric coords, downward adjacency, classification as (id,dim) pairs, tags, remote links) written via PCU file I/O; also VTK output for visualization and conversion tools (e.g. Exodus/STK, PHASTA formats, Simmetrix .sms meshes). Performance: scalable parallel reads/writes in the paper (specific numbers unverified).
geometry_association: Core feature: classification. Each mesh entity has a model[] pointer to a gmi_ent (identified by (dim, tag)); boundary-classified vertices/edges/faces optionally keep parametric coordinates in param[]. gmi_model interface supports evaluation (eval, reparam between adjacent entities, closest_point, normal, first_derivative, periodic, range, is_in_closure_of, is_point_in_region). Supports CAD through Simmetrix (Parasolid, ACIS via gmi_sim; Discrete model for mesh-only geometry), Cap, analytic and mesh-derived models. Model topology is a B-rep hierarchy vertex/edge/face/region with use/orientation in the Simmetrix backend (GF_use for face uses). The mesh can be read against a model by id lookup (mds_find_model(dim,id)), so the geometry file and mesh are separate and joined on (dim,id).
high_order: Handled outside MDS: CRV module provides Bezier-curved meshes with control points stored as fields (apf::Field with shape functions) on edges/faces/regions; MDS topology stays low-order and vertex coordinates are per-vertex double[3]. Fields (nodal, element, integration-point, Lagrange/Bezier shapes) live in APF as per-entity data; geometry snapping onto the model uses closest_point. Details of CRV (orders, validity checking) unverified from primary source in this session.
parallel: Distributed mesh with explicit part model. Each MPI rank holds one or more parts; entities on part boundaries carry remote copies (mds_net.remotes: per-type arrays of {mds_id e, int p} lists), a residence set (set of parts) and an owner part (getResidence/getRemotes/getOwner/isShared/isOwned). Ghosting via mds_net.ghosts and getGhosts/isGhost; migration of entities between parts preserves adjacencies and classification; load balancing via Zoltan interface and PARMA (PUMI-Balance hypergraph balancer). Link tables (struct mds_links with per-peer arrays) are used for serialisation of remotes in SMB. Verification: mds_verify_residence, mds_align_remotes/ghosts/matches. Scalability claims (hundreds of thousands to over a million cores, billions of elements) are from the PUMI literature and unverified here.
ecosystem: C/C++ with Python wrappers (PYCORE), build via CMake; BSD licence. Users: PHASTA (CFD), M3D-C1 (fusion MHD, via SimModeler/Simmetrix), Albany/Trilinos (STK conversion), MFEM/others via converters, PUMIPic (particle-in-cell) and PUMI-Tally (Monte Carlo neutral particle transport) built on top, PUMI-Fields/MeshFields (performance-portable on GPUs via Kokkos). Simmetrix SimModSuite/SimModeler (commercial) provides CAD import, meshing, attribute GUI and the .smd/.sms formats; PUMI accesses it via gmi_sim/apf_sim. No Rust bindings known (unverified); C ABI is plain, so FFI is feasible. ParaView reads VTK output (pumi write via apf::writeVtkFiles)."

corrections.claim: Ecosystem/maturity: PUMIPic and PUMI-Tally (Monte Carlo neutral transport) are built on top of PUMI, listed as PUMI/MDS production users
corrections.correction: PUMI-Tally (arXiv 2504.19048, 2025; repo SCOREC/pumi-tally, pushed 2026-10-23) is built on PUMIPic, which 'makes use of the Omega_h mesh data structure' (CSR arrays, Kokkos, CUDA), not PUMI/MDS. Its constructor 'loads a Omega_h mesh'; it targets simplex meshes; it plugs into OpenMC through a PIMPL interface (OpenMC's own unstructured backend in the paper is MOAB). SCOREC's GPU-era transport stack therefore sits on Omega_h, and SCOREC's apf page now labels core as 'PUMI-General-Adapt' (CPU) and Omega_h as 'PUMI-Portable-Adapt'.

corrections.claim: getDgCopies(e, dgCopies, ModelEntity*) for discontinuous-Galerkin style duplicated entities on a model entity (presented as a verified PUMI/MDS feature)
corrections.correction: Only an abstract apf::Mesh virtual. MDS's implementation asserts 'getDgCopies for MDS is not implemented yet!' (mds/apfMDS.cc:743); apf_cap also fails. Only the Simmetrix wrapper implements it (apf_sim/apfSIM.cc:972) via the commercial M_splitMatch(part, ent, modelFace) from SimMeshTools.h; PHASTA uses it for a 'DG interface' BC attribute on interior model faces (phasta/phOutput.cc:255). Duplicated-entity interior interfaces exist only with the Simmetrix mesh, not in the open MDS.

corrections.claim: parts partitioned by Zoltan/PARMA (hypergraph-based PUMI-Balance)
corrections.correction: Two different things conflated. Inside SCOREC/core, MDS meshes are balanced by ParMA ('Partitioning using Mesh Adjacencies': diffusive, multi-criteria, priority list region/face/edge/vertex, adjacency-based, not hypergraph) and by the separate Zoltan interface library (graph/hypergraph/RCB/RIB). 'PUMI-Balance' is SCOREC's name for EnGPar, a separate repo ('A hyper-graph based parallel unstructured mesh dynamic load balancing component'), used mainly with PUMIPic/Omega_h.
corrections.source: https://scorec.rpi.edu/apf/ ; https://scorec.rpi.edu/parma ; PUMI User Guide v3.0.2 §2.3 (parma = 'adjacency-based mesh partitioning', zoltan = 'graph partitioning S/W')

corrections.claim: Invariants checker: mds_verify / mds_verify_residence (classification closure rule; faces with <2 cells must be on model boundary; residence consistency)
corrections.correction: Both are declared in mds_apf.h (lines 72-73) but have no definition anywhere in the repo (dead declarations). The actual checker is apf::verify (apf/apfVerify.cc): verifyDown asserts each downward entity's model dimension <= the entity's model dimension and residence is a subset of candidate parts; verifyUp derives the expected upward count from classification, treating a model face adjacent to >1 model regions (non-manifold interior interface) as needing 2 regions, and part-boundary sharing or periodic matches as 'exposed'; plus cross-part checks of remotes, ghosts, matches, coordinates, tags, fields.
corrections.source: github.com/SCOREC/core apf/apfVerify.cc lines 49-183; grep of mds/*.c

corrections.claim: mds_derive_model: a facet with <2 adjacent regions and no remote copy puts its closure on boundary (dim d-1, id 0)
corrections.correction: Code is `if (c || s.n == 2) continue;` — a facet is left interior only if it has a remote copy or exactly 2 adjacent regions; facets with 1 OR >=3 regions get their closure classified to the boundary. It also builds only a 2-entity model (interior (d,0), boundary (d-1,0)).

corrections.claim: Classification is a single pointer per entity: no multi-layer model (geometry vs partition/material vs mesh)
corrections.correction: SCOREC's formal design is already a 3-layer classification hierarchy: models V in {G geometric, P partition, M mesh}, classification U ⊏ V 'where U is lower than V in a hierarchy of domain decomposition' (Guide §1.3; Fig.17 geometry model -> partition model -> distributed mesh). Partition-model entities P_i^d group mesh entities with the same residence part set and store dim, id, residence set and owner; 'partition classification' M ⊏ P and reverse classification are defined (Defs 2.8-2.10, consistent with ITAPS iMeshP). Caveat for the design: SCOREC's 'partition model' means parallel part decomposition (FMDB lineage), not material grouping, and in MDS code P is implicit (residence/remotes/owner) while only G is an explicit pointer. The user's 'partition layer' term collides with this.

corrections.claim: Material/BC sets are derived by querying classification, not stored as sets on the mesh; no set concept
corrections.correction: Entity sets ARE in PUMI's specification (Guide §2.2.5: list-type L-SET, set-type S-SET, part-level P-SET, add/remove, filtered iteration, boolean ops, subset and parent/child relations, usable as migration units; tag type PUMI_SET) but the guide states 'entity set is not supported in the current PUMI release' and PUMI_SET/PUMI_STR tags are 'NOT SUPPORTED'. Unimplemented design, not absent concept. Omega_h does implement named groups over classification: `ClassSets = std::map<std::string, std::vector<ClassPair{dim,id}>>` (physical-group style).
corrections.source: PUMI User Guide v3.0.2 pp.16-17, 30, 32; sandialabs/omega_h src/Omega_h_mesh.hpp

corrections.claim: PUMI deliberately does not carry an attribute system in GMI (gmi_ent is opaque, no attribute API); users attach data via mesh tags and fields keyed on classification
corrections.correction: True for gmi.h, but the open pumi.h layer provides geometric-model tags: pumi_geom_createTag/findTag/deleteTag and pumi_gent_set/get{Int,Long,Dbl,Ent,Ptr}Tag plus array variants (pumi.h lines 166-199); Guide §6.4 lists model tag types DBL/INT/LONG/ENT/PTR/BYTE, while mesh tags are limited to DBL/INT/LONG. It also provides reverse classification pumi_gent_getRevClas(model entity -> mesh entities). What is missing is the attribute 'case'/information-node system (Beall 1999; Simmetrix), not per-model-entity data.
corrections.source: github.com/SCOREC/core pumi/pumi.h; PUMI User Guide v3.0.2 §6.4, §9.4-9.5

corrections.claim: Fixed per-type degree arrays make general polygons/polyhedra impossible without a new type mechanism
corrections.correction: Correct for shipped code (MDS_TYPES=8; apf::Mesh::TYPES=8; PUMI_EntTopology 8 values), but the MDS design doc (mds/mds.tex, Ibanez, 'Efficient Storage of Adaptive Topological Meshes', 2014) addresses it explicitly: 'General polyhedral meshes are the main exception... it should be possible for the MDS structure to accept new topological types at runtime, though its performance will degrade as the number of types grows large. Good performance can be found using about ten types or less, but when more than a hundred types are involved this may no longer be the optimal structure.' The template design is a stated trade-off, not an oversight.

corrections.claim: Unverified: Simmetrix MeshSim may offer non-matching-interface features in commercial modules
corrections.correction: Vendor pages list: tri/quad/mixed surface meshes, tetrahedral and 'hexahedral-core' volume meshes, boundary layers/extruded/thin-section (MeshSim Advanced), curved quadratic elements, assembly/non-manifold models, and 'face matching for periodic and contact boundary conditions' (MeshSim Core). Neither polyhedral elements nor non-conforming/non-matching interfaces are mentioned. The only interface-duplication mechanism observed is M_splitMatch (split-match copies on an interior model face).

corrections.claim: Proven at scale (billions of elements per the PUMI literature; unverified exact figures); scalability claims unverified
corrections.correction: PHASTA strong-scaling on a 92-billion-element PUMI mesh with 3,145,728 MPI processes on 786,432 Mira cores (Rasquin et al., Computing in Science & Engineering 2014); that mesh was generated with 256K ranks x 8 threads (SciDAC poster); ParMA partition improvement reported on up to 92B elements on ~3/4 million cores.

corrections.claim: No formal specification; TOMS/FMDB PDFs not retrievable so paper-level claims unverified; no version stated
corrections.correction: The PUMI User's Guide v3.0.2 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16412599, PUMI.pdf, 24 July 2025) is openly available and defines the data model, nomenclature, partition model and API. Repo tags: v3.0.1, v3.0.2, v4.1.0, v4.2.1 (CITATION.cff still says 2.2.6/2021 — stale); last push 2026-10-16; license 3-clause BSD. FMDB citation: Seol & Shephard, 'Efficient distributed mesh data structure for parallel automated adaptive analysis', Engineering with Computers 22(3):197-213, 2006 (not IJNME). TOMS citation 42(3):17:1-17:28, 2016, doi 10.1145/2814935 confirmed.

corrections.claim: SMB layout: header, per-type counts, coordinates and parametric coords, downward adjacency, classification, tags, remote links
corrections.correction: Actual write_smb order: header (magic, version=6, dim, npeers) -> per-type counts -> connectivity -> coords (+2D parametric coords, present since v2) -> remotes -> classification (id,dim pairs) -> tags (int/double only) -> matches (v>=3; new layout v>=4) -> 'meta' (fields/numberings, v>=5). Reader asserts version <= 6. Uses a separate SMB type ordering with smb2mds/mds2smb conversion.

missing_important: Omega_h (sandialabs/omega_h, FreeBSD license; upstream last pushed 2024-06, tags to v10.1.0; SCOREC fork active, pushed 2026-10-21) is the SCOREC-lineage GPU data model actually used by PUMIPic/PUMI-Tally and is the closest existing 'mesh as array database' baseline: pure struct-of-arrays/CSR (Adj a2ab/ab2b; ask_down/ask_up/ask_dual/ask_star derived and cached per (from,to) pair; per-dimension tags, owners, Dist), families OMEGA_H_SIMPLEX or OMEGA_H_HYPERCUBE (tri/tet or quad/hex, not mixed), classification as class_dim/class_id arrays plus named class_sets, and an AMR module doing non-conforming hanging-node hypercube refinement with parent/child relations, leaf flags and enforce_2to1_refine (amr_test2.cpp builds quad/hex boxes and refines/derefines). It is the only SCOREC code with a first-class non-conforming representation.

MDS defaults to the full ONE-LEVEL representation in both directions: mds_create sets mrm[i][j]=1 for |i-j|==1 (region<->face, face<->edge, edge<->vertex); other pairs are derived on demand or stored via mds_add_adjacency (apf createAdjacency). The User Guide's taxonomy (full vs reduced x complete vs incomplete; 12 possible adjacencies; one-level = representation (b); 'complete minimum sufficient representation' (e) storing only equal-order-classified faces/edges) is a ready vocabulary for specifying which adjacency tables an IR materialises.

Measured storage costs (mds.tex, serial all-tet mesh of 93,710 elements, full one-level + coords + classification + matches): object-based PUMI 897 B/tet, Simmetrix 589 B/tet, MDS 241 B/tet; MDS topology only 133 B/elem; reduced MDS ~79 B/elem; MOAB AHF 80 B/elem, standalone AHF ~39 B/elem. By design MDS never shrinks memory on deletion (free-list reuse only).

PUMI's explicit mesh-topology restrictions (Guide §2.2.1): regions/faces have no interior holes; an entity uses a given lower-order entity at most once (so orientation is defined from boundary entities without 'use' entities); an interior entity is uniquely specified by its bounding entities (relaxable only under equal-order classification). These are exactly the rules a polyhedral/non-conformal IR relaxes, so they are the precise baseline to diff against.

Non-manifold geometric models (Radial-Edge lineage, Weiler 1988) are first-class in PUMI: an interior model face bounding two model regions is the normal multi-material conformal ('imprinted') interface, and apf::verify expects such mesh faces to have 2 adjacent regions. Mesh-level tags are restricted to int/long/double; entity-handle, pointer and byte tags exist only on the geometric model.

SCOREC's four-component 'geometry-based analysis' environment (Guide §2.1, Fig.1): geometric model <-> attributes <-> mesh <-> fields, with attributes organised as 'cases' of 'information nodes' attached to model entities (Beall 1999 thesis; Shephard, IJNME 47:169-190, 2000). Simmetrix commercialises that layer (GeomSim 'geometry-based attribute definition and assignment') and adds 'GeomSim Abstract', which keeps analysis attributes persistent through design changes by mapping them from an abstract component/class model onto the current geometry — a direct commercial precedent for an abstract layer above the B-rep.

Lineage to cite as baseline: Beall & Shephard, 'A general topology-based mesh data structure', IJNME 40(9):1573-1596, 1997 (origin of classification); Garimella, IJNME 55:451-478, 2002 (representation taxonomy); Remacle & Shephard AOMD, IJNME 58:349-374, 2003; Seol FMDB thesis 2005 and Seol & Shephard 2006 (partition model); Celes/Paulino/Espinha, IJNME 64:1529-1556, 2005 (compact adjacency-based structure); Dyedov et al. AHF 2014.

Three different 8-type enums with different orderings coexist (MDS: vertex,edge,tri,quad,wedge,pyramid,tet,hex; apf::Mesh::Type: ...,TET,HEX,PRISM,PYRAMID; PUMI_EntTopology: ...,TET,HEX,PRISM,PYRAMID; SMB file uses yet another order needing smb2mds/mds2smb) — a concrete cost of hard-coded element enums worth avoiding in a versioned IR.

Cross-interface relations available in the open stack: PUMI 'matches' (Copy{peer,entity} pairs in mds_apf.matches, persisted in SMB, adapted by MA adaptMatching/shouldHandleMatching) and Simmetrix 'face matching for periodic and contact boundary conditions'; Simmetrix M_splitMatch split-match copies on an interior model face are what PHASTA uses for 'DG interface' boundaries — the practical precedent for an explicit interface-relation record between duplicated faces.

topic: Non-manifold / cellular topology representations (radial-edge, partial-entity, SGC, Parasolid/OCCT cell complexes, Topologic, Gmsh fragments, Cubit imprint/merge)
summary: Non-manifold boundary-representation (B-rep) research is the lineage that solved "several volumes share one face" in a single model. Weiler's radial-edge structure (1986 RPI thesis, "The Radial Edge Structure", unverified beyond secondary sources) added oriented "use" entities and a radial cycle of face-uses around each edge. It is implemented today as BRL-CAD's NMG library. Lee and Lee's partial-entity structure (SMA 2001; J. Comput. Inf. Sci. Eng. 1:356-365, 2001) claims about half the storage of radial-edge while still deriving full adjacency (abstract only; full text was not accessible). Rossignac and O'Connor's Selective Geometric Complex (SGC, 1989) is the most abstract form. It stores disjoint connected cells, a dimension-independent incidence graph of boundary-of links tagged left/right/both, and an "active" flag per cell, so one cell complex can carry many point-sets. Industrial kernels use the same ideas. Parasolid has bodies, regions, shells, faces, loops, fins, edges and vertices, with general bodies that can be cellular or mixed-dimension. OCCT has TopoDS_CompSolid, with sub-shapes shared by reference. Gmsh uses BooleanFragments to make interfaces conformal, and Cubit uses imprint then merge. For our IR the important lesson is that these structures describe the geometry/partition layers (volumes, faces and the regions between them), not the mesh layer. The cell-complex idea is the right backbone for our geometry and partition layers, and the mesh layer can be a refinement of it.
data_model: RADIAL-EDGE (Weiler). BRL-CAD NMG, verified at https://brlcad.org/docs/api/dd/d4e/topology_8h_source.html (topology.h), is a direct implementation. The hierarchy is model, nmgregion, shell, faceuse, loopuse, edgeuse, vertexuse. Each "use" points to a shared definition: struct face / loop / edge / vertex (vertex has vg_p geometry). Per-use pointers are: faceuse { s_p (owning shell), fumate_p (opposite side), orientation, f_p }; loopuse { up union (fu_p or s_p), lumate_p, orientation, l_p }; edgeuse { up union (lu_p or s_p), eumate_p ("eu on other face or other end of wire"), radial_p ("eu on radially adj. fu, null if wire"), e_p, orientation, vu_p (first vertexuse) }; vertexuse { up union (s_p, lu_p or eu_p), v_p }. All edgeuses around an edge are found by alternating radial_p and eumate_p until the walk returns to the start (source comments and docs). Secondary sources say Weiler stores the radial and loop cycles but not the disk cycle, so some non-manifold vertex configurations need geometric tests to disambiguate (https://ocw.snu.ac.kr/sites/default/files/NOTE/4843.pdf, secondary; unverified against the thesis). PARTIAL-ENTITY (Lee and Lee 2001): region, face, edge, vertex plus partial faces, partial edges and partial vertices (abstract only; claim of about half the radial-edge storage is from the abstract, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1115%2F1.1433486). SGC (Rossignac and O'Connor 1989; Siggraph 96 course notes https://cgvr.cs.uni-bremen.de/teaching/cg_literatur/SIG96sgc.pdf, read directly): a finite set of mutually disjoint connected cells, each an open connected subset of an n-manifold. The incidence graph links each cell to all its bounding and incident cells, with a left/right/both "neighborhood" tag when dimensions differ by one and the lower cell lies in the supporting manifold. Each cell is tagged active or inactive. Optional NAIL tables give the next edge around a vertex in a face, e.NAIL(v,f), and the next face around an edge bounding a 3-cell, f.NAIL(e,r). Boolean-type operations are decomposed into subdivision, selection and simplification. CNRG (Constructive Non-Regularized Geometry) is the construction-tree companion. PARASOLID (secondary sources only, not official Siemens docs): body, region, shell, face, loop, fin, edge, vertex. Edges are classified by fin count (0 wire, 1 laminar, 2 manifold, more than 2 general). A body always has an infinite void region so that regions tile all space. General bodies may mix manifold, non-manifold, cellular and mixed-dimension parts (https://ocw.snu.ac.kr/sites/default/files/NOTE/4844.pdf; https://blogs.sw.siemens.com/plm-components/whats-new-in-parasolid-v-38-0/). OCCT (verified, https://occt3d.com/dev/doc/overview/html/occt_user_guides__modeling_data.html): Vertex, Edge, Wire, Face, Shell, Solid, CompSolid ("set of solids linked through their faces"), Compound. TopoDS_Shape is a by-value handle holding a reference to a shared TopoDS_TShape plus TopLoc_Location plus Orientation (FORWARD, REVERSED, INTERNAL, EXTERNAL). Adjacent solids share the face TShape. Finding the solids that share a face needs TopExp::MapShapesAndAncestors (OCCT forum, via search; unverified). TOPOLOGIC (https://github.com/wassimj/Topologic): Topology (abstract), Vertex, Edge, Wire, Face, Shell, Cell, CellComplex ("a contiguous set of cells joined at shared faces, non-manifold") and Cluster (any collection, nestable). It sits on OpenCASCADE 7.8 (from build instructions) and is AGPL-3.0. GMSH: the model is entities (point, curve, surface, volume) with tags and a boundary list. MSH 4.1 $Entities stores per entity: bounding box, physical tags, and numBounding* tags whose sign encodes orientation (https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html, MSH file format section). A surface is stored once and listed by both neighbouring volumes after fragmenting. CUBIT: geometry-level imprint and merge. Merge is permitted only where the surfaces have matching topology, and imprint creates that match (Cubit docs below).
polyhedra: These structures represent polyhedra natively at the topology level. A Cell, Region or 3-cell is bounded by an arbitrary set of faces, and each face by an arbitrary loop count. The faces can be non-planar and carry holes (loops) in radial-edge, Parasolid and OCCT. Weiler's structure handles faces with holes via multiple loopuses. SGC asks that each cell be connected, which forces separate cells for disconnected components. SGC notes that CW-complex-style restrictions need "bridges" and "cuts" to make faces simply connected, which SGC itself avoids (SGC course notes, section 4). None of them is a mesh format. A polyhedral mesh cell is just a cell whose boundary is a set of polygon faces, so a face-based cell definition is the natural mesh-layer form. Radial-edge per-face-use and per-loop-use records are far heavier than the face-to-cell arrays a mesh needs (storage cost is my inference; not measured).
nonconformal: Kernels in this family treat conformality as a topological identity: two volumes either share the same face (one face entity, two uses, or radially adjacent edgeuses) or they do not. A non-conformal interface is therefore two distinct faces lying geometrically on the same surface, with nothing in the topology linking them. Cubit documents this exactly: merge needs matching surface topology, and imprinting creates it (https://cubit.sandia.gov/files/cubit/15.9/help_manual/WebHelp/geometry/imprint_merge/imprint.htm). The Cubit ITEM tutorial lists failed merges as unmerged overlapping surfaces, floating volumes, and non-manifold curves or vertices (https://cubit.sandia.gov/files/cubit/15.9/help_manual/WebHelp/step_by_step_tutorials/item/step04.htm). Cubit also has mesh-based imprinting (`imprint mesh body 1 2` then `merge`) that finds locations from coincident mesh nodes (https://sandia.gov/files/cubit/15.8/help_manual/WebHelp/geometry/virtual_geometry/partitioned_geometry/mesh_based_imprinting.htm). Gmsh says BooleanFragments "compute all the fragments resulting from the intersection of the entities... making all interfaces conformal", and Coherence under OCC is just a BooleanFragments of all entities with Delete (https://gmsh.info/doc/texinfo/gmsh.html). This confirms the user's terminology. Imprinting is an information-level merge (splitting faces so topology matches), and merging is the topological identification of the two imprinted faces. Detecting a non-conformal contact needs a geometric search (coincident faces in tolerance without shared topology). That is an explicit query over the cell complex, not a stored fact, in all these systems. SGC subdivision is the formal version: subdivide each object's cells at intersections with the other's, then select. A solver that handles non-conformal meshes (mortar, DG, projection) needs the mismatched face pairs. The kernels above only offer "not shared"; any pairing would have to be computed or stored as an explicit relation (my inference). Whether and how solver codes detect this was not covered by my sources.
sets_and_partitions: SGC is the clearest statement of layering. Cells carry an active/inactive flag, and "by choosing which cells of an object are active one can associate various pointsets with a single collection of cells" (SGC notes). Features are "different selections" over one cell set (SGC notes, comparison table). This is a partition layer as a selection over a shared cell complex, matching the user's "material is an abstraction over geometry" idea. CNRG groups cell references into regions (SGC notes). OCCT groups with Compound and CompSolid, and the same TShape can sit in many groupings. Gmsh physical groups are sets of entities with a dimension, tag and optional name, and when any are defined the output mesh contains only elements in at least one physical group unless Mesh.SaveAll is set (gmsh manual, sections 1.1, 1.2.3). Topologic Clusters are nestable arbitrary collections. Parasolid regions are subsets of space that can be solid or void. Cubit uses volumes, blocks, and sidesets/nodesets. Gmsh/OCCT/Parasolid keep geometry, grouping and mesh in separate objects tied by tags (mesh nodes carry entityDim/entityTag blocks in MSH 4.1), so the three user-described layers can coexist. None of the sources defines a general-purpose layer mechanism beyond groups.
strengths: Shared faces between regions are first-class: one face, two incident volumes (OCCT shared TShape; Gmsh boundary lists; SGC incidence graph; radial-edge radial cycle).
Mixed dimensions in one model (wire, sheet, solid), including internal faces for material interfaces and cracks; Parasolid general bodies and Topologic clusters do this.
SGC separates cell decomposition from selection, giving a principled home for the partition (material) layer over one geometric cell complex.
Dimension-independent incidence graph with left/right/both side tags is a minimal, uniform relation set.
Orientation semantics for internal and external boundaries (OCCT INTERNAL/EXTERNAL) are already worked out.
Decades of kernel use; BRL-CAD NMG is open and implements radial-edge fully, so the pointer cycles can be studied.
Gmsh/Cubit workflow evidence: fragment or imprint-and-merge works in production to get conformal multi-material models.
weaknesses: Pointer-heavy structures (use entities and mates) are costly for millions of cells and are not array/columnar; no parallel, partition or I/O story. The size claim for radial-edge is from Lee and Lee's abstract; I did not measure it.
They model geometry and topology, not mesh data: no element types, high-order nodes, fields, or sets of mesh entities.
Weiler's version omits the disk cycle (secondary source), so non-manifold vertex neighbourhoods can need geometry. Partial-entity fixes this at lower cost, but its details were not read.

No standard file format: STEP does not carry OCCT compsolid sharing per a FreeCAD developer on the Gmsh list (https://onelab.info/pipermail/gmsh/2018/012055.html, secondary); OCC users fall back on native BREP.
Conformality is all-or-nothing and depends on tolerance-driven imprint/merge, which fails on misalignment (Cubit ITEM tutorial). Non-conformal contact is not represented as a relation.
Parasolid documentation was not reached (only third-party slides and a Siemens release note), and Weiler's thesis and Lee and Lee's full text were not accessed, so those details are unverified.
Topologic is AGPL-3.0 and tied to OCCT, so it is a design reference rather than a dependency.
lessons_for_us: Adopt the SGC idea as the IR backbone: a single set of disjoint cells per dimension (vertex, edge, face, volume) with a boundary-of incidence graph, plus selections (active flags or named predicates) as the partition layer. Materials, colors and boundary sets then become selections over shared cells, not copies of geometry.

Adopt shared-face semantics from OCCT/Gmsh: a face exists once and is bounded-by listings of two volumes carry orientation or sign. Store the incident-cell pair (and side: left/right/both, as SGC does) on the face, which gives the interface element a solver needs.

Deliberately differ from radial-edge pointer structures: store relations as flat arrays (CSR boundary lists plus signed/oriented references, like Gmsh's signed tags). The edge-to-face radial order is only needed in the geometry layer; compute it on demand, or keep it as an optional index, instead of persisting use-entity objects.

Define imprint and merge as two separate, explicit operations in the IR: imprint is a subdivision at the information level; merge is identifying two faces. Persist a 'coincident-but-not-merged' relation (face pair plus tolerance) instead of leaving it implicit, so a non-conformal-capable solver can read the pairing directly. Confirm in the later non-conformal research topic how solver codes want this.

Keep three tied layers keyed by stable ids: geometry cells (B-rep), partition selections, mesh entities carrying an association back to a geometric cell (as Gmsh MSH4 does with entityDim/entityTag). Make mesh-to-geometry association a first-class relation.
Support mixed dimensions and internal faces from day one (zero-thickness material interfaces, sheets, wire features), with OCCT-style INTERNAL/EXTERNAL orientation semantics.

Treat the Gmsh fragment operation (all-vs-all intersect, Delete operands, result conformal) as the baseline for the geometry-node 'make conformal' step, and Cubit's mesh-based imprint as the baseline for a mesh-layer 'make conformal from mesh' step.
Do not adopt Topologic or OCCT as the IR (licence and kernel coupling). Use them as the baseline for the sentence 'similar to a cell complex, but arrays-first, mesh-aware and layered'.
geometry_association: These systems are the geometry layer. Radial-edge, Parasolid and OCCT vertex/edge/face definitions each point to a supporting geometric entity (vg_p; edge_g_lseg/cnurb; face_g_plane/snurb in NMG; Geom curves and surfaces in OCCT). SGC says each cell lies in a supporting manifold. Mesh association is only partly covered: Gmsh MSH 4.1 groups nodes and elements by (entityDim, entityTag) and can store parametric coordinates of nodes on curves and surfaces (parametric flag, u/v). Cubit and Gmsh keep the B-rep and mesh in memory together. No source gave a formal generic mesh-to-B-rep association schema.
high_order: Not addressed by the topology structures themselves. Geometry carries curved edges and faces (NURBS or analytic), but no per-cell polynomial order or node layout. Gmsh MSH 4.1 can store high-order elements and nodes with parametric coordinates on entities, and has Lagrange basis functions (manual text on iso-parametric Lagrange elements). Details of high-order element types were not part of my sources.
parallel: Not covered by the classical structures; none specifies distribution. The only verified parallel representation here is Gmsh MSH 4.1 $PartitionedEntities: entities get parentDim, parentTag and partition tags, ghost entities are listed with their partition, and Mesh.PartitionCreateGhostCells enables ghost cells. Partitioned entities inherit boundary lists from the parent. This is a useful pattern, with partitions as sub-entities of the geometric cell. Pointer-based structures (NMG, Topologic) are not distributed.
ecosystem: Radial-edge: BRL-CAD NMG library (libnmg, C), used in a CSG/B-rep solid modeler. Partial-entity: academic (Lee and Lee); BRL-CAD notes it as a possible more compact alternative. SGC: IBM Research, said to have influenced CATIA (Rossignac bio, search result), and its successor is Rossignac's Structured Topological Complexes. Parasolid: Siemens kernel inside SolidWorks, Solid Edge and others; SolidWorks exposes a GeneralTopology flag and does not support general bodies. OCCT: open-source kernel used by FreeCAD and Gmsh; the native BREP file keeps compsolid sharing. Topologic: Cardiff and UCL architecture and energy research, with a Python port topologicpy; Rust rewrite 'topologic-fast' appears on PyPI but is unverified. Gmsh: .geo/.msh/Python/C++/C/Julia API, MSH 4.1 format. Cubit: Sandia, with ACIS/OCC-like geometry and imprint/merge commands.
database_like_aspects: This lineage is already database-like. SGC is essentially a cell table per dimension plus an incidence relation table (boundary-of) with an attribute column per link (left/right/both) and a per-cell active flag, so selections are queries (filters over dimension, adjacency, incidence and topological operators, per the SGC notes). NAIL tables are explicit auxiliary indices. OCCT offers query-style helpers such as TopExp::MapShapesAndAncestors (an inverted index built on demand). Gmsh's model API has getEntities, getBoundary, getPhysicalGroupsEntities and getEntitiesInBoundingBox, plus $Entities carrying bounding boxes. Topologic attaches dictionaries and exposes topological queries (unverified detail). None uses an actual schema or query language. The closest transferable point is storing relations as typed tables with on-demand inverse indices and treating partitions or materials as predicates or sets over cell ids.
spec_quality: Mixed. SGC has a formal mathematical definition (cells, boundary, active set, operations) in the Rossignac and O'Connor paper and the Siggraph 96 notes. Radial-edge has a thesis and the BRL-CAD implementation as the practical spec. OCCT's data model is documented in the user guide, but there is no neutral file spec, and STEP loses compsolid sharing per the FreeCAD note. Gmsh MSH 4.1 is a formal, versioned text and binary spec (the only formal file spec in this group). Parasolid has the XT format and docs, but I could not reach primary documentation. Topologic has a conceptual class hierarchy documented in the README but not a file format.
storage: Mostly in-memory object graphs, not a file container. NMG is serialized through BRL-CAD's database (not studied). OCCT uses BREP text/binary files. Gmsh MSH 4.1 is ASCII or binary, organized in entity blocks with size_t tags and a binary-mode endianness marker. Parasolid XT is a proprietary text or binary transmit format (unverified). I found no benchmark numbers on I/O speed or memory for any of these. The only size claim, about half the radial-edge storage for partial-entity, comes from the Lee and Lee abstract (unverified in full).

corrections.claim: Weiler's radial-edge structure (1986 RPI thesis, "The Radial Edge Structure")
corrections.correction: The 1986 RPI PhD thesis is 'Topological Structures for Geometric Modeling'. 'The radial edge structure: A topological representation for non-manifold geometric modelling' is the separate 1988 paper (venue not verified here). The SCOREC PDF link (scorec.rpi.edu/REPORTS/1986-1.pdf) now redirects to the site home page, so the thesis remains unread and the disk-cycle claim stays secondary.

corrections.claim: Radial-edge: 'a radial cycle of face-uses around each edge'; NMG per-use field list; 'edge_g_lseg/cnurb' geometry on edge definitions
corrections.correction: In BRL-CAD NMG the radial cycle is of edgeuses: radial_p = 'eu on radially adj. fu (null if wire)', eumate_p = 'eu on other face or other end of wire'. struct edge holds only eu_p, is_real, index (no geometry pointer); the geometry union g {edge_g_lseg, edge_g_cnurb} and a second list link l2 sit on edgeuse. faceuse also has 'outside'; vertexuse has an attribute union a {vertexuse_a_plane, vertexuse_a_cnurb}. Edge geometry is reached only through a use, not the shared edge definition. (Lee & Lee storage claim is confirmed verbatim by the Crossref abstract: 'reduces the storage size to half that of the radial edge structure'; full title 'Partial Entity Structure: A Compact Boundary Representation for Non-Manifold Geometric Modeling', JCISE 1(4):356-365, 2001.)

corrections.claim: No standard file format: STEP does not carry OCCT compsolid sharing per a FreeCAD developer on the Gmsh list (onelab 2018/012055)
corrections.correction: The cited thread (B. Oswald, J. Theler, J. Sanchez) never mentions STEP or loss of face sharing; it recommends FreeCAD's compsolid mode + .brep export, or Gmsh Coherence, and nobody is identified as a FreeCAD developer. Moreover OCCT's STEP translator has had read.step.nonmanifold / write.step.nonmanifold (default Off, added 2010) which write shared faces once into a STEP non_manifold_surface_shape_representation (NMSSR) and read NMSSR back, so STEP can carry non-manifold shared-face topology as a surface model. Caveats: the OCCT STEP user guide does not document these flags and its write-mapping table has no TopoDS_CompSolid row; default (manifold_solid_brep) export does lose sharing.

corrections.claim: Cubit: 'Sandia, with ACIS/OCC-like geometry'; all Cubit citations are Sandia Cubit 15.8/15.9; 'merge needs matching surface topology'
corrections.correction: Sandia Cubit docs state 'CUBIT usually relies on the ACIS solid modeling kernel' (plus mesh-based geometry), not OCC. The project target is Coreform Cubit; its current help (v2026.8) carries identical imprint, merge and mesh-based-imprint text, so the semantics are current (cite coreform.com/cubit_help/... instead). The merge rule is stricter than stated: entities must correspond geometrically AND topologically, and if both are meshed their meshes must be topologically identical (same counts/connectivity; node positions may differ, lowest-ID entity's positions win). Default merge tolerance 5.0e-4 (lower bound 1e-6); 'Merge ... Force' bypasses the geometric test.

corrections.claim: Lesson: 'Store the incident-cell pair (and side: left/right/both, as SGC does) on the face'
corrections.correction: SGC's neighborhood tag is defined only when dimensions differ by one AND the lower cell lies in the manifold supporting the higher cell (verified). The notes add that when the boundary cell is not in that manifold, e.g. a singular self-intersection edge where four surface branches meet, 'it may not always be possible to define a neighborhood' and suggest 'branch numbers' instead. A 3-valued side tag is therefore insufficient for general non-manifold configurations; the IR needs a fallback (branch index or ordered radial list, i.e. SGC's NAIL tables). The notes also credit Gursoz/Choi/Prinz (NOODLES) with consistent traversal at non-manifold vertices, consistent with the report's secondary disk-cycle claim.

corrections.claim: Topologic: Rust rewrite 'topologic-fast' appears on PyPI but is unverified
corrections.correction: It exists: PyPI 'topologic-fast' v0.2.1, three releases 2026-06-04..2026-06-10, 'ground-up rewrite of Topologic' in Rust (PyO3 bindings, rayon, arena storage, BVH/octree), classifiers AGPLv3+ and 'Development Status :: 4 - Beta'; README's repo link is a placeholder ('github.com/your-repo/topologic-fast'). Treat as an immature, AGPL-licensed curiosity, not a design reference or dependency. (Topologic itself: AGPL-3.0 and OCCT 7.8 confirmed from the GitHub README.)

missing_important: Gmsh BooleanFragments is OCCT's General Fuse algorithm (BOPAlgo_Builder); the Gmsh API doc says 'boolean fragments (general fuse)', and OCCT's spec says the GFA result is a compound whose sub-shapes 'have shared sub-shapes in accordance with interferences between the arguments'. This is the concrete baseline algorithm for the geometry-node 'make conformal' step. (gmsh.info manual API section; dev.opencascade.org specification__boolean_operations.html)

Cubit has explicit geometric queries for non-conformal contact: 'Find Overlap' (surfaces that overlap but are not merged), 'Find Near Coincident Vertex {Vertex|Curve|Surface}' with a tolerance range, Tolerant Imprint driven by merge tolerance, and ITEM 'Detect Potential Problems'. Primary evidence for the report's inference that contact detection is a query, not stored state. (Sandia 15.9 imprint.htm, merge_tolerance.htm, step04.htm)

Cubit does persist intent about unmerged coincidence: per-entity 'Body|Volume|Surface|Curve|Vertex <ids> Merge Off' prevents merging (documented use case: slide surfaces), i.e. a stored 'coincident but deliberately non-conformal' flag, though per entity rather than a face-pair relation. (coreform.com/cubit_help/geometry/imprint_merge/merging.htm)

Cubit's Virtual Geometry (composite/partition) modifies topology 'without affecting the underlying ACIS geometry representation', is fully reversible, and is what mesh-based imprinting creates. It is an existing implementation of the user's partition layer as a separate layer over geometry and belongs in the baseline sentence. (Sandia 15.9 virtual_geometry.htm; mesh_based_imprinting.htm, same text in Coreform v2026.8)

Mesh-layer conformality has a definition in Cubit: merging two meshed entities requires topologically identical meshes (same entity counts and connectivity), not identical node positions. (coreform merging.htm)

OpenFOAM polyMesh is the production array form of the report's recommended face-based polyhedral cell: points, faces (point index lists), owner[face], neighbour[face] (internal faces only), boundary patches as (startFace, nFaces) ranges; each face has exactly one owner and at most one neighbour. (openfoam.com user guide 4.1)

How a CFD code expresses a non-conformal interface: OpenFOAM cyclicAMI stores it in the mesh as a patch pair (patch + neighbourPatch), computes area-intersection weights at run time, and flags mismatch via weight sums != 1 (lowWeightCorrection since 2.3.0; AMIWeights function object). Direct precedent for persisting a face-set pair plus tolerance as the report proposes. (openfoam.org 2.3.0 release notes; doc.openfoam.com AMIWeights)

Gmsh MSH 4.1 already persists an inter-entity relation: the $Periodic block stores entityDim, entityTag -> entityTagMaster, an affine transform and explicit node correspondences; $GhostElements lists elementTag, partitionTag and ghost partition tags; $Parametrizations stores per-curve/surface node parametrizations. These are the closest existing file-format precedents for the report's 'coincident-but-not-merged' face-pair relation. (gmsh.info manual, MSH 4.1 section)

OCCT STEP non-manifold mode (read/write.step.nonmanifold -> non_manifold_surface_shape_representation) means a neutral exchange path for shared-face topology exists, so an IR exporter can target NMSSR for interface-preserving STEP output rather than falling back to native .brep. (OCCT source, see correction)
